3619862853.title: ZombieBuddy
3619862853.description:
A framework that enables advanced Java mods for Project Zomboid.

[b]What it does:[/b]
ZombieBuddy is required by some mods to work. If a mod tells you to install ZombieBuddy, follow the instructions below.

[h1]Installation (One-Time Setup)[/h1]

[b]Step 1:[/b] Subscribe to ZombieBuddy on Steam Workshop

[b]Step 2:[/b] Installation is required ONLY ONCE for ZombieBuddy itself.

[b]🪟 Windows:[/b]

[u]Option A: Automated Installer (Recommended)[/u]
[list]
[*] Download the latest ZombieBuddyInstaller.exe from [url=https://github.com/zed-0xff/ZombieBuddy/releases/tag/windows_installer]GitHub Releases[/url]
[*] Run the installer and choose [b]Install or update ZombieBuddy[/b].
[*] Choose what launch mode to patch:
[list]
[*] [b]Both[/b] (recommended): patches Normal Launch and Alternate Launch.
[*] [b]Normal Launch[/b]: then choose ProjectZomboid64.json, Steam launch options, or both.
[*] [b]Alternate Launch[/b]: patches ProjectZomboid64.bat.
[/list]
[*] The installer shows every system change first and asks for confirmation before applying it.
[*] If Steam launch options need to be changed, the installer will ask you to close Steam at that point.
[*] The same installer can also uninstall ZombieBuddy later: run it again and choose [b]Uninstall ZombieBuddy[/b].
[/list]

[u]Option B: Manual Installation[/u]
[list]
[*] Copy ZombieBuddy.jar and zbNative.dll from:
[code]C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\108600\3619862853\mods\ZombieBuddy\libs\[/code]
to your Project Zomboid folder:
[code]C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\ProjectZomboid\[/code]
[*] Open Project Zomboid's launch options in Steam
[*] Add this launch option: [code]-agentlib:zbNative --[/code]
[*] [b]⚠️ IMPORTANT:[/b] The -- at the end is mandatory - do not omit it!
[*] If you use the game's Alternate Launch option on Windows, set the ProjectZomboid64.bat _JAVA_OPTIONS line to: [code]SET _JAVA_OPTIONS=-agentlib:zbNative[/code]
[/list]

[b]🍎 macOS / 🐧 Linux:[/b]
[list]
[*] Copy ZombieBuddy.jar from the mod's libs/ directory to:
[list]
[*] [b]macOS:[/b] ~/Library/Application Support/Steam/steamapps/common/ProjectZomboid/Project Zomboid.app/Contents/Java/
[*] [b]Linux:[/b] ~/.steam/steam/steamapps/common/ProjectZomboid/projectzomboid/
[/list]
[*] Open Project Zomboid's launch options in Steam
[*] Add this JVM argument: -javaagent:ZombieBuddy.jar --
[*] [b]⚠️ IMPORTANT:[/b] The -- at the end is mandatory - do not omit it!
[/list]

[b]Step 3:[/b] After this setup, all mods that require ZombieBuddy will work automatically!

[h1]Uninstall[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Disable the agent first:[/b] Open Project Zomboid → Properties → clear the Launch Options line
[*] Delete zbNative.dll and ZombieBuddy.jar from your Project Zomboid install directory
[*] Unsubscribe from ZombieBuddy on Steam
[/list]

[h1]⚠️ Security Warning ⚠️[/h1]
Java mods enabled through ZombieBuddy have unrestricted access to your system. Only install mods from sources you trust.

[b]No jar will sneak in.[/b] Whenever a Java mod ships a new or updated JAR, ZombieBuddy shows a native dialog with the mod id, file path, last-modified date, and SHA-256 fingerprint. Nothing is loaded until you click [b]Yes[/b]. You can choose to remember the decision (per-mod, per-hash) or keep it session-only. Persisted allow/deny choices are written to JSON (mod id → { sha256 → true|false }) at:
[list]
[*] [b]Windows:[/b] %USERPROFILE%\.zombie_buddy\mod_approvals.json
[*] [b]macOS / Linux:[/b] ~/.zombie_buddy/mod_approvals.json
[/list]
If a previously-approved JAR changes on disk (hash mismatch), you will be prompted again.
Tip: hold [b]Shift[/b] during game load to force the approval dialog to appear, even for previously approved Java mods.

[h1]Java Mod Policy[/h1]
Controls what happens when an unknown/changed JAR is seen. Pass as a [b]policy=...[/b] argument:
[list]
[*] [b]prompt[/b] (default) - ask me each time via a native dialog.
[*] [b]deny-new[/b] - silently skip any JAR that isn't already approved.
[*] [b]allow-all[/b] - load every JAR without prompting. [b]Not recommended.[/b]
[/list]
Examples (block form, these go into Steam launch options):
[code]
-agentlib:zbNative=policy=deny-new --            (Windows)
-javaagent:ZombieBuddy.jar=policy=deny-new --    (macOS / Linux)
[/code]

[h1]FAQ[/h1]
[list]
    [*][b]Is it a virus?[/b]
    No.

    [*][b]How to start game in debug mode?[/b]
    [code]
    -agentlib:zbNative -- -debug
    OR
    -javaagent:ZombieBuddy.jar -- -debug
    [/code]

    [*][b]Do I need to repeat manual installation after I upgrade/downgrade/validate game?[/b]
    No, if you use the default launcher and have agentlib in Steam launch options.
    Yes, if ZombieBuddy stops loading.

    [*][b]Works on MP?[/b]
    Yes.

    [*][b]Save compatibility?[/b]
    Safe to add or remove on existing saves.

    [*][b]I clicked the wrong button in the approval dialog. How do I reset it?[/b]
    Open mod_approvals.json (path above), under 'mods' find your mod id, then remove or edit the SHA-256 key you want to reset (or change true/false), save, and restart.

    [*][b]Can I see which Java mods were loaded or blocked?[/b]
    Yes - install [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3709229404]Zed's Better ModList[/url] and the status is shown next to each JAR path in the mod list.

    [*][b]Supported game versions?[/b]
    B41, B42.12-B42.17

    [*][b]Can I hide ZB watermark?[/b]
    Yes, in ModOptions. During game boot it is always visible.

    [*][b]WHY ALL LINKS ARE REMOVED FROM THIS PAGE AND COMMENTS DISABLED???!!![/b]
    Steam does that while it checks a newly uploaded mod version for viruses, I suppose. Everything should return to normal in 10..30 minutes, depending on how busy their system is.
[/list]

[h1]Links[/h1]
[url=https://github.com/zed-0xff/ZombieBuddy]GitHub Repository[/url]

[h1]Support the Project[/h1]
If you find ZombieBuddy useful, consider supporting its development:
[url=https://ko-fi.com/zed_0xff][img]https://i.imgur.com/Utx6OIH.png[/img][/url]

3626008449.title: PlumbingFixed [B42.20.2]
3626008449.description:
[h1]PlumbingFixed[/h1]
[b]Improves vanilla plumbing behavior with smarter fluid draw[/b]. Instead of a plumbed sink drawing water from exactly one water barrel until it is depleted, it will draw from all of the barrels. When you are using water from multiple water barrels the tooltips will now report the overall amount in all barrels instead of just in one barrel.

This means you can now [b]perform common actions[/b] without interruption and without having to micromanage your water barrels. Perfect addition for any mid to late-game players who struggle with water management with their water barrels.

[b][u]Works in Singleplayer & Multiplayer[/u] - Safe to enable/disable mid-save.[/b]

[b][u]Works in B42.19/20[/u][/b]

[b][u]THIS MOD HAS NO EFFECT ON UNPLUMBED FIXTURES.[/u][/b]

The mod overrides the following actions
[list]
	[*]Drinking water from a sink
	[*]Filling container from a sink
	[*]Washing yourself/clothes from a sink
	[*]Washing clothes in a washing machine
	[*]Cleaning bandages
[/list]

3627071412.title: Fix NaN Stats [B42.13-B42.20+]
3627071412.description:
[h1]Compatibility: Build 42.13 → 42.20+ (SP/MP)[/h1]
[b]Fix NaN Stats[/b] automatically detects when gameplay values become corrupted as [b]NaN[/b] (Not-a-Number) or [b]Infinity[/b] and safely restores them to valid values — preventing broken moodles/HUD bars, “temperature/wetness = NaN” issues, pain/health glitches, and other weird behavior caused by invalid numbers.
[hr]
[h1]What this mod does[/h1]
Sometimes a value can become [b]NaN[/b] or [b]Infinity[/b] due to a bug, a mod interaction, or an edge case. Once a value is invalid, many systems stop behaving correctly.

This mod is a lightweight safety net:
[list]
[*]Detects invalid numbers ([b]NaN[/b], [b]+Inf[/b], [b]-Inf[/b]) in stats, nutrition, pain/health sources, thermoregulation, and worn clothing.
[*]Repairs only values that are actually invalid (it does [b]not[/b] change normal values).
[*]Runs automatically while you play.
[*]Optional on-screen + log notifications when something is fixed (Mod Options).
[/list]
[hr]
[h1]When should you use it?[/h1]
Use this mod if you notice any of these symptoms:
[list]
[*]A stat/moodle looks “stuck”, behaves strangely, or never updates correctly.
[*]You use status-bar HUD mods (e.g. [i]Simple Status[/i], [i]Modern Status[/i]) and one of the displayed bars shows weird/blank values, freezes, or behaves incorrectly.
[*]The Debug UI shows [b]nan[/b] or an invalid value for a stat, nutrition value, temperature, wetness, pain, or a clothing-related field.
[*]You get the “body temperature = NaN” / “wetness = NaN” type of bug (especially noticeable during winter runs).
[*]You suspect a mod or an edge case caused numeric corruption.
[/list]
You can keep it enabled permanently, or enable it temporarily to repair a save and disable it again afterward.
[hr]
[h1]What it fixes[/h1]
[h2]Character stats[/h2]
The mod checks [b]every[/b] [i]CharacterStat[/i] and repairs any value that becomes invalid.  

Common examples include: Hunger, Thirst, Fatigue, Endurance, Fitness, Drunkenness, Anger, Pain, Panic, Morale, Stress, Boredom, Unhappiness, Sanity, Comfort, Wetness, Temperature, Health, ColdStrength, Sickness, etc.

[h2]Nutrition[/h2]
[list]
[*]Calories
[*]Carbohydrates
[*]Lipids (Fats)
[*]Proteins
[*]Weight (fallback reset if needed)
[/list]
[h2]Pain / health sources (BodyParts / BodyDamage)[/h2]
[list]
[*]Repairs invalid numbers in BodyPart/BodyDamage fields that can cause global [b]Pain[/b] to snap back to invalid values.
[*]Repairs BodyPart [b]wetness[/b] and [b]pain[/b] sources (plus related timers/fields when present).
[*]If a BodyPart’s [b]Health[/b] becomes [b]NaN[/b], it is restored to [b]100[/b] to prevent corruption loops.
[*]Repairs [b]OverallBodyHealth[/b] (General Debuggers → Body) when it becomes invalid.
[/list]
[h2]Thermoregulation (temperature/wetness)[/h2]
[list]
[*]Recovers from “body temperature = [b]NaN[/b]”.
[*]Recovers from “wetness = [b]NaN[/b]” (including per-body-part wetness).
[*]Scans Thermoregulator thermal nodes and performs a safe reset/update when needed.
[*]Includes BodyPart wetness recovery to prevent invalid-number feedback loops.
[/list]
[h2]Worn clothing values (when they become invalid)[/h2]
[list]
[*]Insulation (invalid → restored to a safe/script default)
[*]Wind Resistance (invalid → restored to a safe/script default)
[*]Clothing/item wetness
[*]Blood level
[*]Dirtiness
[/list]
[hr]
[h1]Notifications (optional)[/h1]
If enabled in [b]Mod Options[/b], the mod can display a small message over the character (and also write a log line) when it fixes something.  

This helps you notice when a specific action or mod interaction produced an invalid value.

Example:
[code]Fix NaN: Temp/Wetness | Clothing x4 (Insulation/Wind) | Stats: Thirst | Nutrition: Calories[/code]
[hr]
[h1]Multiplayer notes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Works in [b]Singleplayer[/b] and [b]Multiplayer (hosted/dedicated)[/b].
[*]For MP, the mod should be enabled on the [b]server[/b] so fixes are server-authoritative and clients stay in sync.
[/list]
[hr]
[h1]Performance / resource usage[/h1]
Very low. The mod performs lightweight checks at a fixed interval and only writes values when something is actually invalid. During normal gameplay (with no NaNs/Infs), it effectively does nothing.
[hr]
[h1]Safe to add / safe to remove[/h1]
[list]
[*]Safe to add to an existing save: it only repairs corrupted values.
[*]Safe to remove: it does not add items, recipes, maps, or permanent content.
[*]It simply prevents and repairs invalid-number corruption while enabled.
[/list]
[hr]
[h1]Notes[/h1]
[list]
[*]This mod is a “sanity fixer”: it does not attempt to diagnose the root cause, only to restore valid, playable values.
[*]If you consistently get NaNs/Infs, consider checking mod conflicts and reporting details (build number + mod list + steps to reproduce).
[/list]
[hr]
[h1]Planned improvements[/h1]
Possible future updates may include:
[list]
[*]Configurable check frequency
[*]Custom reset values (per stat)
[/list]
[hr]
[h1]Credits[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Afyrmo[/b] — Original author and main maintainer ([i]Fix NaN Stats[/i])
[*][b]Kaori[/b] — Helpful investigation, reproduction notes, and contributions that improved the 42.15+ fixes (thanks!)
[/list]
[hr]
[h2]More mods & feedback[/h2]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561199133259679/myworkshopfiles/?appid=108600]You can find my other Project Zomboid mods here[/url]
[img]https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/819002974403344349/DD18664314A26EA83C62E9B0127FFCB35092B53A/[/img]
If you find [b]Fix NaN Stats[/b] useful, please consider leaving a [b]thumbs up[/b] and adding it to your [b]favorites[/b] — it helps other players discover it.  

Feedback and suggestions are always welcome.

3627539752.title: TwisTonFire - Map Improvements
3627539752.description:
[img]https://imgur.com/BaUyxax.png[/img]
[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]

[h2]Newest Additions[/h2]
[img]https://imgur.com/97biOAn.png[/img]
[img]https://imgur.com/nQDIhso.png[/img]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/TDg8f8q.gif[/img]

[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]

[h1]TwisTonFire - Map Improvements[/h1]
Make the vanilla World Map cleaner, more flexible, and more comfortable to use.

Resize symbols, scale the complete symbol interface, mix additional colors, draw directly on the map, create dedicated sketch paper, and safely manage your map markings.

The mod uses focused patch-style changes wherever possible instead of replacing complete vanilla files.

[img]https://imgur.com/yDc7Ipa.png[/img]
[img]https://imgur.com/9fsfZyO.png[/img]
[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]

[h1]Features[/h1]
[h2]Improved Map Symbols Interface[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Cleaner Map Symbols layout[/b] with a more organized and responsive interface.

[*][b]Map Symbol Size Slider[/b] for quickly changing the size of placed map symbols.

[*][b]Persistent symbol size[/b]: the mod remembers your last selected size.

[*][b]Custom default size[/b]: save your preferred symbol size and restore it with the Reset button.

[*][b]Complete UI Scale setting[/b]: resize the entire Map Symbols interface from 75% to 140%.

[*][b]Separate UI Scale window[/b] with Save and Reset controls.

[*][b]Custom-font safe layout[/b] that adapts to larger fonts and longer translations.
[/list]

[h2]More Colors and Writing Tools[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Additional mixed colors[/b] for map symbols and map notes:
[list]
[*]Yellow
[*]Purple
[*]Cyan
[*]Orange
[*]Pink
[/list]

[*][b]Consistent color selection[/b] between the Map Symbols menu and the Add/Edit Note window.

[*][b]Vanilla-friendly pen requirements[/b]: regular colors require their matching pen.

[*][b]Mixed colors require both matching pens[/b]. For example, purple requires a red and blue pen.

[*][b]Improved writing-tool support[/b] for compatible modded pens, markers, crayons, and other items using the proper writing tags.
[/list]

[h2]Additional Map Symbols[/h2]
Seven new animal location symbols are included:

[list]
[*]Chicken
[*]Cow
[*]Pig
[*]Rabbit
[*]Sheep
[*]Turkey
[*]Raccoon
[/list]

[h2]Sketch Tools[/h2]
Draw directly on the World Map using a movable Sketch Tools panel.

[list]
[*][b]Freehand Tool[/b] for drawing naturally with your mouse.

[*][b]Straight Line Tool[/b] for creating clean and precise lines.

[*][b]Brush Erase Tool[/b] for removing only the sketch marks touched by the eraser.

[*][b]Adjustable Stroke Size[/b] for thinner or thicker markings.

[*][b]Adjustable Stroke Density[/b] for changing the spacing and smoothness of your strokes.

[*][b]Map color integration[/b]: sketches use the currently selected Map Symbols color.

[*][b]Writing-tool requirements[/b]: drawing requires a pen, pencil, or compatible writing tool.

[*][b]Eraser requirement[/b]: removing sketch marks requires an eraser.

[*][b]Undo and Redo[/b] for up to 20 sketch actions.

[*][b]Accurate cursor preview[/b] that matches the actual size and visibility of the placed sketch marks.

[*][b]Zoom-based sketch visibility[/b]: sketch marks can automatically disappear when the map is zoomed out.

[*][b]Adjustable visibility threshold[/b] through the native Mod Options menu.

[*][b]Performance-aware drawing[/b] that automatically adjusts stroke spacing on maps containing very large numbers of sketch marks.
[/list]

[h2]Persistent and Safe Sketch Tools UI[/h2]
[list]
[*]The Sketch Tools panel remembers its position between game sessions.

[*]The panel automatically adapts to custom fonts and longer translations.

[*]Long button labels are safely shortened instead of breaking the UI.

[*]The panel is clamped to the visible screen and cannot be permanently moved outside the display.
[/list]

[h2]Sketch Paper Map[/h2]
Prepare a dedicated [b]Sketch Paper Map[/b] from a regular Sheet of Paper.

This provides a clean paper surface that can be used for drawings, plans, routes, notes, or anything else you want to sketch without using the main World Map.

[h2]Improved Map Reset Options[/h2]
The vanilla map reset action now opens a safer selection menu.

Choose exactly what should be removed:

[list]
[*][b]Remove Sketch Marks[/b]  
Removes only markings created with the Map Improvements Sketch Tools.

[*][b]Remove Player Symbols[/b]  
Removes player-created map symbols and notes while keeping explored map memory.

[*][b]Full Map Reset[/b]  
Removes player-created symbols and resets the complete explored map memory, matching the original vanilla action.
[/list]

Each destructive action includes a separate confirmation window to prevent accidental map deletion.

[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]

[h1]Translations[/h1]
Translation files are included for 27 languages:

[b]Arabic, Catalan, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Filipino, Finnish, French, German, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Portuguese (Brazil), Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Thai, Turkish, and Ukrainian.[/b]

[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]

[h1]Compatibility[/h1]
This mod is compatible with mods that add additional map symbols.

[b]Do not combine it with another mod that adds its own Map Symbol Size Slider.[/b]

Map Improvements already contains its own localized and persistent Symbol Size Slider and changes the surrounding symbol interface layout.

[h2]Supported Game Modes[/h2]
[quote]

[th]Build 42.20[/th]
[/tr]

[tr]
[td][b]Singleplayer[/b][/td]

[td]✅[/td]
[/tr]

[tr]
[td][b]Multiplayer[/b][/td]
[td]✅[/td]
[td]✅[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]
[/quote]

[b]The current version requires Build 42.19 or newer.[/b]

Your support helps me keep going — thank you very much!

[b]Looking for even more World Map improvements?[/b]

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3571222611][img]https://imgur.com/JBxBPlp.png[/img][/url]

Check out [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3571222611]Darker Map & Satellite View[/url][/b].

3628782804.title: Water Bidon
3628782804.description:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/AGrsCkP.png[/img]

[h1]Water Bidon (40L)[/h1]

[i]A heavy-duty industrial container designed for [b]transporting large amounts of fluids[/b] in survival scenarios.

This bidon is not meant to replace rain collectors, bottles, or small containers — it fills the gap between portable storage and fixed infrastructure. Ideal for hauling resources from rivers, lakes, fuel pumps, or remote locations back to your base.[/i]

[hr]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/10BpRzF.png[/img]
[h2]Key Features[/h2]

[list]
[*] Holds up to 40 liters of fluid
[*] Can be placed on the ground and used without carrying it
[*] Extremely heavy when full — not practical to carry by hand
[*] Compatible with vanilla fluid transfer mechanics
[*] Uses a custom 3D world model with multiple color variants
[*] Designed for logistics and base supply, not direct consumption
[/list]

[hr]

[h2]How to Use[/h2]

[list]
[*] To fill the Water Bidon, you must have a funnel equipped
[*] To empty or transfer the Water Bidon, you must have a rubber hose equipped
[*] The bidon must be completely emptied before changing to a different fluid
[/list]

[hr]

[h2]Intended Use[/h2]

[b]Place the bidon on the ground and transfer fluids using bottles, cooking pots, or other containers. Its large capacity makes it ideal for:[/b]

[list]
[*] Supplying bases without nearby water sources
[*] Transporting fuel, water, or other liquids safely
[*] Stockpiling resources before weather events
[*] Supporting generators and infrastructure systems
[/list]

[hr]

[h2]Balance & Design[/h2]

[list]
[*] Heavier and more efficient than jerrycans
[*] Much smaller than rain collectors or industrial tanks
[*] Encourages planning, transport, and logistics
[*] Fully balanced around weight and capacity
[*] Fluids cannot be mixed — the bidon stores one fluid type at a time
[*] Not intended for direct drinking or consumption
[/list]

[hr]

[h2]Notes[/h2]

[list]
[*] The bidon is designed as a [i]logistical container[/i], not a personal flask.
[*] Works best when placed on the ground.
[*] Vehicle inventories do not support fluid transfer (vanilla limitation).
[/list]

[hr]

[h2]Compatibility[/h2]

[list]
[*] Project Zomboid Build 42
[*] Compatible with vanilla and modded fluid containers
[*] Designed to fit naturally alongside survival, logistics, and infrastructure mods
[/list]

[hr]

[list]
[*] [b]Automatic Update Detection[/b]: Scans your active Workshop mods and alerts you if any have been updated since your last play session.
[*] [b]Copy/Open link[/b]: Allows you to open a workshop link in Steam Overlay,  or copy the link to clipboard.
[*] [b]Changelogs[/b]: Displays a changelog for any mod that includes a ChangeLog.txt in the "common" folder.
[*] [b]In-Game Popup[/b]: See a clear, user-friendly popup listing all mods with available updates, including version and changelog info (if available).

[h2]🔧 Compatibility[/h2]

Workshop Update Checker is not incompatible with ModManager, nor is it flooding steam with excessive requests. The suggested redundancy is personal choice.

3633082678.title: Sentry Turret Upgrade
3633082678.description:
This is an upgrade of the original Sentry Turret mod, updated for Build 42 compatibility.

First, thanks to the original mod author:
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2753312788

English isn't my first language, so please forgive any awkward phrasing.

Goal: This mod isn't about redesigning the gameplay.
The focus is on functionality ,making the turret feel more reliable and easier to read in Build 42.

Fixes & Improvements

✅ Compatibility
Build 42.18 and earlier are no longer supported
Build 42.20+ Single Player / Multiplayer (SP, MP)

-Added PvP, the turret will aim the player who attack the turret owner (alpha test)

-Added compatibility for the Bandit mod. The turret will now aim at hostile NPCs and zombies (Single Player beta)

-Turret ammo compatibility (beta)
Added compatibility with the following mods:

Real Firearms
Guns of Marz
Vanilla Weapons Plus
Hot Brass - Visible Casing Ejection Framework (SP only yet)
AAA_ModernFirearmsSystem

The turret can now recognize ammo from these mods that matches the vanilla turret's calibers. Which calibers aren't supported varies by mod. Only takes effect if the corresponding mod is enabled, and won't affect other players.

-Added an ownership safeguard: when a player places a turret, the nearest player becomes its owner. Only the owner can see the items inside the turret; other players will see an empty inventory. 

New / Improved Features:

7️⃣ Multiplayer support is now available, Beta
-Please expect there may still be bugs
-Minor sync issues or visual glitches may occur

1️⃣ New muzzle flash
-Each shot produces a brief light flash, with brightness varying by turret type
Note: if you can't see the effect, set your Lighting Update Rate to 60

2️⃣ Improved hit feedback
-Added physics-based hit reactions, including knockdown and stagger effects

3️⃣ Bullet tracer / aim indicator
-Displays a brief tracer line showing the direction of fire

[list]
[*] [b]Living Economy & Smart Pricing:[/b] A sophisticated tag-based pricing engine handles inflation and deflation. Item condition, rot, fluids per liter, and randomized durability all directly affect true market value.
[*] [b]Events & Global Heat:[/b] Multi-flash events dynamically change the world. Winter spikes food prices; raids discount weapons.
[*] [b]Realism Update:[/b] Traders sell scavenged goods with randomized durability, not factory-new products. However, producer archetypes (farmers, anglers, etc.) will still sell fresh produce depending on your luck.
[*] [b]Medical Care & Needs:[/b] Hire Doctors, manage the new Infirmary building, and ensure your faction workers are healed and fed through the new tabbed warehouse supply UI. (Requires ZedColonies Addon)

(Requires Objectives Addon)
[/list]

Best for players who want the deep simulated economy and colony management without physical NPCs or the need to travel to traders in person.

3635856965.title: Better Auto Mechanics [B42.20+ MP+SP]
3635856965.description:
[h1]Better Auto Mechanics[/h1]
[b]Train mechanics with a single click. Smarter, more intuitive, and lightweight. In Multiplayer and Singleplayer.[/b]

Rewritten from the ground up, [b]Better Auto Mechanics[/b] is a comprehensive quality-of-life upgrade for the mechanic skill. Inspired by the original mod "[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3387539308]AutoMechanics[/url]", it improves on several key features while still allowing you to train mechanics on vehicles with a single button. And it works in multiplayer!

Compatible with all B42 versions! B41 is not supported, use [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2588598892]this[/url] instead.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]🔧 Key Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Smart XP Tracking:[/b] The mod knows exactly when you can't gain XP from a specific car anymore. It will alert you if a vehicle isn't worth training on, so you never waste time.
[*] [b]Resume Interrupted Training:[/b] If zombies interrupt you (or you cancel an action), you can pick up exactly where you left off. No more starting from scratch and wasting part durability!
[*] [b]Efficiency First:[/b] The mod will never perform an action if it won't yield XP.
[*] [b]Clearer Tooltips:[/b] Know exactly what tools you need and how your skill level, known recipes, and other factors impact the training before you start.
[*] [b]Fast-Forward Supported:[/b] Fully supports speeding up the game in SP, allowing you to breeze through your training sessions. Nearby zombies will still reset the game speed to normal.
[*] [b]Batch Uninstall:[/b] Quickly strip vehicles for spare parts! Use the new context menu to batch-uninstall specific categories like all doors, all tires, or completely strip the entire car bare with a single click.
[*] [b]Translated into:[/b] English, German, Russian, French, simple + trad. Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, and Polish.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]🚗 How to Use[/h2]
[olist]
[*] Open the mechanics window on any vehicle.
[*] Right-click any part.
[*] Select [b]"Train Mechanics"[/b].
[*] Watch the levels go up!
[/olist]
[quote][b]Note:[/b] Pathfinding can sometimes impact the training session. Please ensure your character has some walking space around the car.[/quote]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]💡 Tips[/h2]
[list]
[*] You can only gain XP from a specific vehicle once per day.
[*] Right-click directly on a vehicle in the world to access the "Train Mechanics" button faster.
[*] The "Train Mechanics" button is automatically hidden once you reach Mechanics Level 10.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]⚙️ Mod Settings[/h2]
You can customize the [b]"Minimum Vehicle Part Success Chance"[/b] in the options. This value determines the safety threshold for installing/uninstalling parts; any part with a success chance below this value will be skipped during training.
[list]
[*] [b]0 (Risky):[/b] All parts will be worked on. Be careful—parts [i]will[/i] break or lose condition at lower skill levels.
[*] [b]30 (Default):[/b] A good balance. Parts with a very low success chance are skipped to prevent excessive damage, while still allowing for decent XP gain.
[*] [b]100 (Safe Mode):[/b] Only parts that are guaranteed to succeed will be worked on. This is completely safe at all skill levels, though training may be slower as fewer parts are eligible.
[/list]

[b]Multiplayer / Server Admins:[/b]
Server owners can enforce this setting via Sandbox Options.
[list]
[*] [b]-1 (Default):[/b] The setting is [b]not enforced[/b]. Players are free to use their own local Mod Option setting.
[*] [b]0 to 100:[/b] The setting is [b]enforced server-wide[/b]. Any value greater than -1 will override individual player choices. The value set by the server will be visible in the button tooltip.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]✅ Compatibility & Save Info[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Safe to add and remove mid-save.[/b]
[*] [b]Compatible[/b] with all [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/KI5/myworkshopfiles/?appid=108600]KI5's Vehicles[/url], [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3564950449]Project Summer Car[/url], [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2757712197]Vehicle Repair Overhaul[/url], and most other vehicle mods.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]FEEDBACK & SUPPORT[/h2]
If you find this mod useful:
[list]
[*] ⭐ Rate on Steam Workshop
[*] 💬 Leave comments or [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/discussions/3635856965]Feedback[/url]
[*] 🐛 Post bug reports in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/discussions/3635856965]Discussions[/url] or on [url=https://github.com/Darkblader24/pz-better-auto-mechanics/issues]Github[/url]
[*] 🚀 Contribute to this mod on [url=https://github.com/Darkblader24/pz-better-auto-mechanics]Github[/url]. Translations are very welcome!
[*] ❤️ Buy me a [url=https://ko-fi.com/hotox]Ko-fi[/url]
[/list]

3640105892.title: They Knew [B42] Stable Patch
3640105892.description:
Updates They Knew [B42] for Build 42.20 (tested on 42.20.03) and makes it work on a multiplayer server.

[b]They Knew [B42] is now the ONLY required mod.[/b] The separate 42.13 compatibility patch is no longer needed - unsubscribe from it, or at least remove it from your mod list, before using this version.

[i]Renamed from "They Knew [B42] Patch Patch". The mod ID changed too, so update your server Mods= line to TheyKnewB42Patch.[/i]

[h1]Fixed[/h1]
[list]
[*]Crash to the main menu when killing a hazmat zombie. They Knew still registers its satchel through the Build 41 body-location API, which throws on 42.13+, so the item ends up with a body location the game cannot resolve.
[*]All item scripts converted to the namespaced 42.13+ IDs (base:clothing, base:drainable, base:food, base:container, base:fullsuithead, base:satchel).
[*]The hazmat suit lost its hazmatsuit/SCBA/ignore-zombie-density tags to a duplicated Tags line. Merged back in.
[*]Hazmat zombies dropped no medication at all in singleplayer - the drop code only ran when isServer() was true, which is never the case outside a server.
[*]Loot is now added server-side only, so it no longer duplicates or desyncs in multiplayer.
[*]The hazmat outfit could be registered twice, silently doubling its spawn rate.
[*]Medication effects now run on whichever side owns the player, so the drugs work for every player on a server, not just the host.
[*]Missing sandbox options no longer throw - they fall back to their defaults.
[*]Removed a per-frame infection check that duplicated the once-a-minute one.
[/list]

[h1]Load order[/h1]
TheyKnewB42
TheyKnewB42Patch

[h1]Fixed[/h1]
Please note this does not fix any other source of sickness or infection.  If you have corpse sickness, this does not cure that.  
There is also something called fake infection, which acts like you are infected but are not.   


[h1]Troubleshooting and Errors[/h1]
If you believe you are having a problem you will need to post in the discussions the following information. Failure to post this information will lead to your issue being deprioritized.
[list]
[*]Logs showing the error, if any.
[*]Single player or Multiplayer.
[*]If MP, locally hosted or dedicated server
[*]if MP,mod list and workshop id list from serverconfig.ini file.
[*]description of the problem.
[/list]

Safe to add to an existing save. If you are coming from the old "Patch Patch", swap TheyKnewB42PatchPatch for TheyKnewB42Patch in your mod list - the ID changed with the rename.

Inspired by and using code from pimat.studio
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3626161084

3645687954.title: MoodleFramework Safety Patch

[h1]Moodle Framework – Multiplayer Patch (B42)[/h1]
This mod patches Moodle Framework to properly support multiplayer in Build 42. It fixes instability caused by how the original framework handled moodle data initialization.

[h3]WHAT THIS PATCH DOES[/h3]
[list][*]Removes the global ModData wipe in MF_ISMoodle.lua
[*]Reworks moodle initialization to be per-player and multiplayer-safe
[*]Prevents moodles disappearing or flickering in MP
[*]Fixes client-side nil errors
[*]Improves compatibility with dynamic moodle mods (e.g. NnC Narcotics)
[*]Stabilizes client/server moodle synchronization[/list]

[h3]IMPORTANT NOTE[/h3]
This mod overrides Moodle Framework’s [b]MF_ISMoodle.lua[/b]. If another mod modifies the vanilla [b]ISMoodle.lua[/b], it may cause conflicts. Test those mods before Moodle Framework, otherwise moodle mods should load after this patch.

[h3]MOD LOAD ORDER[/h3]
For best compatibility, use this order:
[list][*]Original Moodle Framework (preferably at the top)
[*]This patch (immediately after Moodle Framework)
[*]Other mods that modify or add moodles[/list] Incorrect load order may cause conflicts.

[h3]SAFETY PATCH FILE[/h3]
This mod still includes [b]MF_SafetyPatch.lua. [/b]
It is now mostly redundant after the [b]MF_ISMoodle.lua[/b] rewrite and remains only as a fallback safety layer for rare edge cases or conflicting moodle mods.

[h3]COMPATIBILITY[/h3]
[list][*]Designed for Build 42[*][b]Tested only on MP 42.13.x[/b][*]Multiplayer-focused fix[/list][h3]No guarantees for:[/h3][list][*]Singleplayer(SP should work without this patch, but patch shouldn't break it)[*]Splitscreen Co-op[*]Earlier builds[*]Future Build 42 updates(B42.14.0+)[*]Build 41(Doesn't work)[/list]

3652008781.title: ExtraBombs 2
3652008781.description:
[h3] Latest Compatible Version: 42.19 (Yes I know the propane tank sizes have changed, I'm working on fixing the models) [/h3]
[h3] 42.18+ multiplayer compatible although as with all MP mods in unstable there can be bugs [/h3]
[h2] Updated & Upgraded sequel to ExtraBombs [/h2]  

With 42.13's changes, a rewrite of the original mod was needed. I took this opportunity to move a few things around & add some new mechanics.

Makes taking the engineer profession worth more than just the free generator knowledge.
[h3]
[list]
	[*] A fourth level of remote trigger for extra long distance 
	[*] New Noise Maker as loud as a house alarm
        [*] 7 New Bombs
	[*] A new Workbench used in the creation of explosives
	[*] Recipe magazine to unlock building the workbench
[/list]
[/h3]

Nothing in this mod is locked or gate kept behind the Engineer profession BUT a lot of the main ingredients in the recipes are items that only the engineer can craft by default.
If you have other mods that get you access to craft or loot the vanilla Bomb items, or you research them or find the schematics then you’ll still be able to use 100% of this mod.

[img]https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/13406627256687939527/25311B3C58D8A6819F880DC55CD77410530348F9/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img]

All the recipes are now located at a Electrical Workbench which can be found in the building menu in a new tab called [b] Extra Bombs [/b]

[img]https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/13708464086908050743/A316F48366F6E71EB833656C10699909BCAB2D32/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img] 

[h2] Extras [/h2]

A 4th tier of remote detonator, lets you activate from a safe distance (has a 55 tile Range) so you won't get caught inside your own explosions

Flux powder, lets you make your own sparklers out of repurposed welding rods

Napalm Mix, Combine polystyrene & some gasoline, now thats some sticky flammable stuff.

Engineers Toolbox, Basic tools & components stuffed into a Toolbox, ready to be used in the building of an Electrical Workbench (The screwdriver & pliers in this recipe WILL be destroyed in the making of the Toolbox)

[img]https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/16108328699599589080/9D4FCF550DA1039B064BFFF46AB10EFA561C1781/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img]

[h2] Big Noise Generator [/h2]

The power of a house alarm in your pocket.
Combine with the long range remote or set it on a timer to precisely gather the whole neighbourhood to one location.
Hmmm.... I wonder if a second long range remote linked to a bomb could be a useful combo.

[img]https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/11160259180071146788/54B53AC0D973F084CE738E153EE5C2C4727D62A4/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img] 

[h2] Lightbulb Bomb [/h2]

A very small explosive (1 tile) perfect for setting traps at choke points like doors or windows.
Due to the small range only the close range motion sensor & a remote trigger can be attached.
Although small, its glass fragments can still one-shot anyone in range & could on rare occasions start a fire.

[img]https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/14422450429289610252/72491685D734146D4239984A5DD4B074FD8FF812/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img] 

[h2] Napalm bomb [/h2]

You are legally required to shout [i]”I cast Fireball”[/i] when using these.
These will cover every tile in range with fire, including buildings, loot containers & you, so you’ve been warned.

[img]https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/10414278679953898533/AEB63F7DD45B9CB70B78529BDF1AC0E92110B423/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img]

[h2] Lunchbox Bomb [/h2]

With Vanilla pipebombs now no longer starting fires, the Lunchbox bombs now is a combination of a pipebomb & a firebomb. Explosive Damage & fire tiles. (any resemblance to bottlecap mines is purely coincidence)
Makes use of either a smoke bomb or an aerosol bomb (good reason to keep hold of that useless insect repellent can) & a choice of shrapnel from nails to lego blocks.

[i] Also available in Pink [/i]

[img]https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/10739472275413346300/0A4EC541A6E207A3C5EEDDA1C55EA5E23B6A0A75/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img]

[h2] Mini Propane Bomb [/h2]

These act like door breaching charges, very small but powerful explosion, causes fire damage to tiles but doesn't start a fire. Great for making an alternative entrance to locked buildings/rooms.
What else were you going to do with those spare propane lantern bottles?

[img]https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/16230586909592546977/1EF48F55C0FB004D907165E29306360958003BC4/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img] 

[h2] Super SmokeBomb [/h2]

A large scale smokebomb, for when you need to loose agro from a large horde or hide during a PVP encounter*. Will cover the area of a propane bomb with smoke.
*Safety not guaranteed, smoke is not bullet proof 

[img]https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/9538054489588961898/DEC3B493907AD89F2A8CFF973226C20EEC50F184/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img] 

[h2] Propane Bomb [/h2]

The pinnacle of pyromancy.
The average survivor couldn't even begin to fathom the engineering genius required to conceive of the mind bending level of intelligence to think up such a weapon of war....... duct tape a Pipe Bomb to the side of a Propane tank.
Because of the range of the explosion you CAN’T throw it far enough to not be in the danger zone, so you have to attach a timer or a motion sensor or a remote trigger for it to work.

[img]https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/16139752933432817927/F3C6584AC317B871119E03F9FE819681C99F3BD5/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img] 

[h2] Oxy-Propane Bomb [/h2]

Whats that? You want the destructive power of the propane bomb but also want to scorch the earth to ash at the same time? Okay I got you.
The same rules apply as the regular Propane Bomb, just make sure you don't care about anything caught in the blast range (or anywhere near by, fire spread is real)

[i] Can be added mid-save, however finding the magazine will require either loot respawn or visiting a new location.[/i]

3653913180.title: Karas Zone Selector API For B42
3653913180.description:
[h1] This is a lightweight API I made for a friend, but feel free to use it too.[/h1]

[h1]What does this mod do?[/h1]
1 The Area Selector is a region selection API built for mod development.
2 It can quickly retrieve all GridSquares within the selected region and return them as a JavaList and a LuaTable.
3 You can choose to use either the JavaList or LuaTable traversal method.
4 This API supports two drawing modes: Unrestricted Region and Restricted Region, and you can manually configure their callback functions.
5 Lets users register a validation function  the API determines the color of the selection box based on the RGBA color values returned by this function.

[h1]How does it work?[/h1]
I’ll post detailed usage examples for this API in the Discussions tab.

[h1]Important Notes[/h1]
Try not to directly copy its code into your mod—instead, use it as a required dependency mod. Unless someone’s holding a gun to your head and forcing you to do otherwise, of course.

3659543622.title: Radio Frequency Manager [B42]
3659543622.description:
Simple re-upload of [url=steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2735294987]Radio Frequency Manager[/url] with small tweaks for B42. All credit to [url=steamcommunity.com/id/kaldoreign]Kaldo[/url] for the original mod.
	[hr]						[/hr]
[h1]Original Description[/h1]
Adds a simple radio frequency library that enables you to easily store known radio channels and then quickly add them to any other device. Now you can easily listen to the same channels in your home, car, your portable radio or any random device in the world without having to manually add the presets every time.

This mod doesn't automatically discover frequencies or change the way stations work in any way, you still have to find them yourself the first time.

[h1]How to use:[/h1]
Open the radio's panel and the Radio Frequency Manager at the same time and use the "Copy from radio" button to save the currently selected channel in the radio's dropdown to the RFM.
If you want to add a custom frequency click the Custom button and type the data in the format 'frequency,station name' (for example: 67.2,My Hidden Channel)

When later you want to add this station to another device, or just quickly tune to it if it already exists, click on the frequency name in RFM while the radio's panel is open. The preset will be created in the radio's preset list if it doesn't exist already and then automatically tuned to.

Click on the colored indicators to the left of a frequency's name in RFM to change colors and easily tell them apart. Press the "X" on the right to delete it from RFM.

[h1]Sandbox options - predefined channels[/h1]
Now you can define specific channels in Sandbox Options and every newly created character will start with them already added to their RFM. These channels must be configured in a very specific way, the text field has a specific format that must be followed:
<frequency>;<channel name>
If you want to add more than one channel, it has to be separated from the previous one with the "|" symbol:
<frequency1>;<channel name1>|<frequency2>;<channel name2>|<frequency3>;<channel name3>
For example:
89.4;Hitz FM|93.2;LBMW - Kentucky Radio
This will result in creation of the Hitz FM on 89.4MHz, and LBMW - Kentucky radio on 93.2MHz.

[h1]Other notes:[/h1]
Holding shift while clicking "Copy from radio" will copy all available presets that haven't already been added to the RFM (Survivor Radio fans will probably find this very useful).

3666180085.title: [B42 SP/MP]Dawn Town
3666180085.description:
Dawn Town was once known as a city that never truly slept. Its narrow streets are suffocated by layers of makeshift buildings, stacked so densely that the sky is barely visible. Endless prayers and constant arguments blend together day and night, like a ritual that never comes to an end. When disaster struck, the already fragile order collapsed almost instantly—gangs, cults, and survivor factions each claiming their own blocks. You won't find a true safe zone in Dawn Town, only corners that haven't been discovered yet.

Map Location:
The map is located to the left of Historic Coalfield, positioned vertically between Echo Creek and Brandenburg.
Cell Position: 10,27

Map Features:
This is a single-cell small city with extremely high building density—movement is heavily restricted, and vehicles can barely enter. Stay alert at all times, as threats may be lurking nearby.
Currently, the map does not include basements or water sources; these will be added in future updates.

Planned Updates:

Improve street layouts and fix unreasonable areas

Add basements

Expand grassy areas across the map — the final plan is for buildings to cover the entire cell

Add a safehouse with convenient access

Enjoy!

Map Folder: DawnTown

[h1]BLACKSTONE – Yellowstone Survival Map[/h1]

[i]A new immersive wilderness map designed for exploration, survival, and multiplayer storytelling.[/i]

[hr]

[h2]OVERVIEW[/h2]

Blackstone is a brand-new custom map built to deliver a balanced and exploration-driven survival experience.

Set in a vast wilderness inspired by Yellowstone (USA), it blends wild nature, populated areas, and hidden locations to create a world that feels alive and rewarding to explore.

From quiet solo journeys to large community servers, the map offers strategic spaces for settlements, faction territories, role-play events, and long-term survival progression.

3671176591.title: dustinguished bolt cutters
3671176591.description:
Simple mod that adds realistic functionality to bolt cutters.

[h3]Also, check out my latest mod [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3755185651]dustinguished cleaning wipes[/url] - clean yourself and items on-the-go, the hemophobes dream![/h3]

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*]Sandbox options for enabling each functionality: cutting locks from garage doors, cutting locks from fence gates, cutting locks from security shutters, and destroying fence sections.

[*]Thematically, the locks are destroyed when cutting them, so no padlock items will drop.  Additionally, the security shutters are "rolled up" after the cutting the lock, destroying them.

[*]How long it takes to perform each action is based on your [b]Strength[/b] level.  The base duration is controlled by a sandbox option, and represents how long it will take a [b]Strength[/b] 0 character to accomplish it.  There is no random chance involved, just time.

[*]Three tiers of [b]Strength[/b] sandbox settings, to reflect how some things may be more difficult to cut that others.  Note: existing saves using previous versions will use the 'minimum strength' setting as the medium difficulty, and then -/+ 2 for easy and hard difficulty.

[*]How much muscle strain is added also accounts for your [b]Strength[/b] level.  The base muscle strain also represents how much will be added for a [b]Strength[/b] 0 character.  (muscle strain values are multiplied by 2.5 on the Indie Stone side of things)

[*]Sandbox option for giving fence sections a chance to drop resources when destroyed.  The resource dropped is based on the type of fence.

[*]Performing an action generates a small amount of [b]Strength XP[/b], and also [b]Maintenance XP[/b] if the bolt cutters get damaged.

[*]Cutting a lock generates a small amount of noise to attract nearby zombies.

[*]Safe to add to, and remove from, existing saves.
[/list]

[h2]Tested Game Versions[/h2]
[list]
[*]42.20 SP/MP
[*]42.19 SP/MP
[*]42.18 SP/MP
[*]42.17 SP/MP
[*]42.16 SP/MP
[*]42.15 SP/MP
[/list]

[h2]Most Recent Changes 21-Aug-26[/h2]
[list]
[*]Hopefully fixed an issue in MP when a nearby player cut a lock, each nearby client would hear the sound as if their character had cut the lock.
[/list]

[h2]Mod Compatibility[/h2]
Shouldn't have any compatibility issues with other mods, it doesn't modify anything from the vanilla game.

[h2]Translations[/h2]
CN and CH provided by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/flameli]Flame[/url]
ES translation provided by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Monsterburn]MoBu[/url]

Google translations for CS, DA, DE, FI, FR, HU, ID, IT, JP, KO, PH, PL, PT, PTBR, RO, RU, TH, and TR.  Hopefully they aren't too terrible, but drop a comment if you can suggest a better translation.

[h2]Known Issues[/h2]

[/list]

3677147974.title: Zed's Universal Mod Unbork
3677147974.description:
[h1]Zed's Universal Mod Unbork[/h1]

Patches renamed or changed game API so [b]old mods keep working on newer game builds[/b]. When the game updates and renames methods (e.g. getDirtyness → getDirtiness) or changes return types (e.g. getTypeString() → getItemType(), getTags() list → set), this mod adds compatibility shims so mods written for older versions still run.

[h1]What it patches[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Clothing[/b] — getDirtiness/getDirtyness and setDirtiness/setDirtyness (whichever spelling the game uses, the other is aliased).
[*][b]Item script (getTypeString)[/b] — ScriptItem no longer has getTypeString() in 42.13+; we restore it by mapping getItemType() back to the old string (e.g. "Drainable", "Literature").
[*][b]Item getTags()[/b] — Old mods expect tags as a list with .get(index); when the game exposes a Set, we add .get() so tag access by index still works.
[*]other stuff
[/list]

Load this mod [b]before[/b] or with mods that target older game versions to reduce breakage after updates. No config required.

[b]Want another mod fixed?[/b] Open [b]one thread per mod[/b] in the Discussion tab (include the mod name and what breaks), so requests can be tracked and prioritized.

[h1]Mod load order[/h1]
[olist]
[*]zdk

[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3718604798]Exhume 41[/url] (optional, if you want to run B41 mods on B42)

3682045254.title: Unified Carry Weight Framework (UCWF)
3682045254.description:
[h1]If you're a user[/h1]
This doesn't do anything on it's own, the modders are supposed to use this to adjust players carry weight without conflicting with each other.

[h1]Mods using this framework[/h1]
And therefore, their weight-related functionalities should not clash.
[list]
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails?id=2914075159]Evolving Traits World (ETW)[/url]
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails?id=1299328280]More Traits[/url]
[/list]
If you have a mod that adjusts carry weight in any way and it conflicts with this framework (it will), just convince them into using the framework, it's the only way to have weight changes from different mods play well with each other. If you know a mod that uses this framework you can mention it so I can add it to the list.

[h1]If you're a modder[/h1]
You are probably aware that majority of mods that modify carry weight conflict with each other and usually it's just "whichever mod applied their override last" sets the weight.

So I made this little thing.

- This allows multiple mods to modify carry weight without overwriting each other changes.
- Supports flat bonuses and multiplications for both base weight (before str applied) and total max weight (after str bonuses are applied)

So something like this is possible and very easy to do now: 

- Mod A has sandbox setting that sets base carry weight to 10 (from 8)
- Mod B has a trait that gives player 0.25 bonus to base carry weight per point of strength
- Mod C has a exoskeleton that when worn increases total carry weight by 50%.

There's a client and a server file with example on how to use the framework, in their respective folders. If you need additional help, ping me in my discord.

[h1]GitHub and Discord[/h1]
If you want to submit translation files, make suggestions or report bugs, the easiest way to do it would be on Discord.

[h1]Credits and Translations[/h1]

3683430283.title: [B42] [SP/MP] No Holes For Ballistic Armor
3683430283.description:
Are you tired of having your fresh ballistic vest ruined by walking through some bushes?  How do you feel about a "bullet-proof" vest being only able to stop one bullet before becoming functionally useless?

If either of these situations grinds your gears, this mod may be for you.

It's a very simple mod that replaces the vanilla bullet-proof armor items (vest, thigh armor, greaves, and vambraces) with nearly identical copies.  These copies are exactly the same in every way except for one property: They can no longer get holes.  This makes them behave much more like steel/scrap armor when it comes to being damaged by zomboids or the environment.

What this mod does is:

-Makes all bullet-proof armor items immune to being damaged by moving through trees/bushes.  They also fully protect any area of your body that they cover from scratches/lacerations from flora.

-Makes all bullet-proof armor items incapable of getting holes.  They take condition damage until they break completely, just like elbow/knee pads and metal armor.

-I fixed a vanilla menu bug that improperly indicated that bullet-proof thigh armor could be worn on the shins.

This mod does NOT make you invincible if you are wearing bullet-proof armor!

These armor pieces only have middling bite and scratch protection and zomboids can still harm you through them.  In my testing, I have discovered that both zomboid attacks and bullets will occasionally damage the condition of the armor piece that they hit.  I have no idea what governs how often that this happens, but if your vest takes enough of a beating (either from bandits or zomboids) it will eventually break and leave you unprotected.  Pay attention to the condition of your gear.

I cannot guarantee that this mod is balanced at all.  It is very simple and just toggles a flag in the item definitions that controls whether or not these armor pieces can receive holes.  I made this because I thought that bullet-proof armor getting ruined by bushes was stupid and unrealistic, and I wanted to share it.

My testing seems to show that this mod is safe to turn on and off without issue on your savegame.  There is no need to start a new game to either install the mod, or to remove it.  However, I do recommend that you keep a backup of your save just in case.

I'm almost positive that this mod is incompatible with any other mod that alters the vanilla bullet-proof armor item definitions.  When in doubt, load this last.

Tested and works in multiplayer.

Let me know in the comments if you run into any issues.

Workshop ID: 3683430283
Mod ID: NoHolesForBallisticArmor

3684025083.title: Jeeve's Patches
3684025083.description:
[h1]Jeeve's Patches[/h1]

Compatibility patches for third-party mods and vanilla PZ bug fixes for Build 42 — crashes, missing translations and engine-level errors, no configuration needed. It targets the modpack the ODYN community server runs; if yours is similar, these may help.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Adding & Removing Mid-Save[/h2]

[b]Add to an existing save:[/b] [b]Safe.[/b] Each patch only acts when the mod it patches is present, and is applied at load time rather than written into your world.

[b]Remove from an existing save:[/b] [b]Safe for the fix and translation patches[/b] — removing one restores the original mod's behaviour, bug included. Two carry a caveat: the [b]Tanker[/b] patch installs a 300L tank as a real vehicle part, so removing it takes that part off the M49A2C and any fuel with it; and the [b]Towing[/b] patch changes how a tow is constrained, so unhitch first. The [b]GGS[/b] and [b]DAMN[/b] patches add recipes whose outputs belong to those mods, so anything already crafted is safe.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]How To Use[/h2]

This Workshop item contains [b]13 mods[/b]: one all-in-one and twelve individual patches. Enable [b]either[/b] the all-in-one [b]or[/b] the individual patches, not both. GGS and ISA are [b]not[/b] in the all-in-one, so enable those alongside it if you need them.

The twelve are [b]Vanilla[/b], [b]Towing[/b], [b]Tanker[/b], [b]GGS[/b], [b]ISA[/b], [b]Moozic[/b], [b]SOTO[/b], [b]Spongie[/b], [b]DAMN[/b], [b]zRe Vaccine[/b], [b]Player Status[/b] and [b]Authentic Z[/b], each listed in your mod list as [i]Jeeve's Patches[/i] plus that name.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Vanilla PZ[/h2]

[list]
[*] [b]Clothing desync[/b] — snapshots what you are wearing and re-equips it when the game strips your outfit mid-action.
[*] [b]Admin Item List Viewer[/b] — the Admin Panel's item list crashed with "toString of non-table: null" on any item using B42.13's newer [code]ItemType[/code] syntax.
[/list]

[h2]BetterTowing — 42.16 Physics[/h2]

Requires [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3633899582]Better Towing & Tow Trucks[/url]. Fixes the 42.16 towing catapult caused by the new angular constraint limits.

[list]
[*] [b]Front hookup ("By Hook")[/b] — rigid tow with lift and mass reduction, bypassing the braking penalty
[*] [b]Rear hookup ("Drag to Reposition")[/b] — rope constraint for repositioning without catapulting
[*] [b]JeevesClaims integration[/b] — tow permission checks on claimed vehicles and land
[/list]

[h2]Tanker Fuel System[/h2]

Adds a 300L TankerTank to the M49A2C, separate from its 90L driving tank. Fill at a powered gas station, then refuel other vehicles from it at base. Other mods' vehicles are untouched.

[h2]GaelGunStore-Firearms[/h2]

Standalone only, rebased against GaelGunStore 1.1 — now a hard requirement, so it will not load without it.

[list]
[*] [b]Gun maintenance kits[/b] — craft the cleaning and disassembly kits the base mod only spawns as loot
[*] [b]900+ name keys[/b] — GGS 1.1's English name files use a key format the game never loads; 801 item and 103 recipe names supplied
[*] [b]Ammo boxes open again[/b] — GGS points its boxes at recipes that don't exist. Restored for every box and carton, .30-30 included
[*] [b]Spanish English text[/b] — hardcoded Spanish in the swap radials and inspect panel replaced
[*] [b]Magazine whitelist[/b] — SVDK, pistol_shotgun and Walther P38 showed no mags in the swap radial
[*] [b]Select-fire reload[/b] — cycling fire mode locked the character model until relog
[*] [b]Ammo carton weights[/b] — all 19 corrected to 90% of the sum of their 12 boxes
[/list]

[h2]Immersive Solar Arrays[/h2]

Standalone only. [b]Do not run alongside Jeeve's Solar Arrays[/b] — that mod replaces the original rather than patching it, and both define a recipe of the same name.

[list]
[*] [b]Powerbank activation[/b] — Turn On / Turn Off did nothing or threw a Lua error in upstream v25.0.1
[*] [b]Generator event errors[/b] — Lua errors spammed clients whenever a generator was plugged in
[*] [b]Ghost powerbank[/b] — the crafting placeholder lingered as a ghost sprite
[*] [b]SolarFailsafe entity[/b] — upstream used an InputFlag B42 lacks, so the recipe vanished
[*] [b]B42.15 translations[/b] — all 8 EN categories, including tooltips upstream lacks
[/list]

[h2]True Moozic[/h2]

[list]
[*] [b]Master volume[/b] — a per-client master volume for the music system, in Options > Mods with optional keybinds. Device volume is shared state, so one player's comfortable level deafens another; now each can turn music down without dropping PZ's master audio and losing footsteps and gunfire
[*] [b]The loot cap actually caps[/b] — "MaxMediaPerContainer = 5" now means five items in the container, not five per media category
[*] [b]Chunk-load exception[/b] — an error thrown once per filled container aborted the cap and spammed the server main loop
[/list]

[h2]Everything Else[/h2]

[list]
[*] [b]SOTO[/b] — the All Thumbs and Disorganized counters were read before SOTO seeded them, throwing errors every tick of an inventory transfer
[*] [b]Spongie's Clothing[/b] — BodyLocationsTweaker rewritten onto public B42 API methods instead of reflection B42.15 restricted to debug mode
[*] [b]that DAMN Library[/b] — vanilla tires lack damnlib's tire tags, so they could not be broken down into the rims and rubber damnCraft consumes. Three recipes close the gap
[*] [b]zRe Vaccine 3.0, Player Status, Authentic Z[/b] — B42.15 JSON translations for every EN category
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

Vanilla clothing fix based on [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3684333893]NakedFix B42 MP[/url] by [b]Zoe[/b]. [b]Build 42[/b], client and server-side. No dependencies on other Jeeves mods.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Part of the Jeeves Ecosystem[/h2]

[list]
[*] [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3660924327]Jeeve's Integration[/url][/b] — Discord relay, player ranks, moodles and server commands
[*] [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3674013419]Jeeve's Claims[/url][/b] — Safehouse, land and vehicle claim protection

[*] [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3687487317]Jeeve's QoL[/url][/b] — Quality-of-life improvements bundle

3684087856.title: Beathoven's Night Vision Framework
3684087856.description:
[h1]Night Vision Framework[/h1]
A framework for adding realistic night vision functionality to Project Zomboid items.
Includes a working example item: [b]Night Vision Goggles[/b] that can be found in military loot.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Known supported Mods[/h2]
[list]
[*] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3470491629]Night Vision Googles[/url]
[*] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3719704041]Ground Panoramic Night Vision Goggles[/url]

[/list]
[hr][/hr]
[h2]How to Use[/h2]
[olist]
[*]Find or spawn the example Night Vision Goggles.
[*][b]Right-click[/b] the goggles in your inventory and select [b]Insert Battery[/b]. This is only available while they are in inventory and not worn.
[*][b]Wear[/b] the goggles.
[*]Press [b]V[/b] to toggle night vision on or off. If your item supports exact [b]_ON / _OFF[/b] or [b]_DOWN / _UP[/b] state tokens, the visor model flips automatically.
[/olist]

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Multiple NV modes[/b] — shipped with Default, Default /w Glare, Single Point Light, Single Point Light /w Glare, White Phosphor, White Phosphor Overlay, White Phosphor Overlay /w Glare, and Zomboid Native modes, with room for add-on modes from other mods. The Debug authoring mode is exposed only in debug-enabled singleplayer.
[*][b]Custom framework overlay[/b] — tint, grain, vignette, flicker, and climate tinting driven by per-mode profiles.
[*][b]Dynamic directional lighting[/b] — raycasted light cone with opening-aware LOS, low-cover exemptions, curtain-aware windows and see-through openings, plus reduced lightpost churn for better performance.
[*][b]Single-point-light modes[/b] — built-in point-light variants can replace the directional cone with one client-local light centered on the player.
[*][b]Debug authoring mode[/b] — built-in live editor with instant preset import for registered non-vanilla modes plus direct directional-light controls, available only in debug-enabled singleplayer.
[*][b]Overlay glare variants[/b] — dedicated glare-enabled built-in modes are available for Default, Single Point Light, and White Phosphor Overlay.
[*][b]Vanilla helper light[/b] — the built-in Zomboid Native mode can still receive a framework indoor helper light in very dark rooms.
[*][b]Singleplayer helper sandbox toggle[/b] — the sandbox can choose whether singleplayer uses the TorchCone-backed directional helper or the lamppost-style fallback helper.
[*][b]Battery system[/b] — install/remove batteries via right-click. Each battery lasts 12 in-game hours. Charge bar visible on the item tooltip and updates live while charge drains. Low battery triggers a flicker warning below 20%.
[*][b]Multiplayer sync[/b] — battery state, live charge-bar updates, battery install/remove actions, and named visor state variants are synchronized through shared/server framework code.
[*][b]Sound support[/b] — on/off clicks plus a subtle ambient hum while NV is active.
[*][b]Fully localized[/b] — 27 language translations included.
[/list]

[h2]Mod Options[/h2]
Open [b]Options → Mod Options → Night Vision Framework[/b] to configure:
[list]
[*][b]Night Vision Mode[/b] — choose between the shipped modes or registered add-on modes. The debug authoring mode only appears in debug-enabled singleplayer.
[*][b]Legacy light cone sampling[/b] — defaults to on for the denser classic cone look; disable it to switch to the lighter sparse sampler on weaker PCs.
[*][b]Toggle key[/b] — rebind the NV toggle key (default: V).
[*][b]Debug Overlay Editor key[/b] — open the live editor while the [b]debug[/b] mode is active (default: N). This row only appears in debug-enabled singleplayer.
[*][b]Enable ambient NV hum[/b] — toggle the looping ambient sound (default: on).
[*][b]Ambient hum volume[/b] — slider 0–100% (default: 30%). Changes apply live.
[/list]

[b]Shipped mode notes:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Default[/b] — classic green phosphor look with the restored wide light cone and no glare.
[*][b]Default /w Glare[/b] — the Default profile with bright-room glare enabled.
[*][b]Single Point Light[/b] — reuses the Default overlay but swaps the cone for one client-local light centered on the player.
[*][b]Single Point Light /w Glare[/b] — the single-point-light variant with glare enabled.
[*]Directional shipped modes default to [b]legacy[/b] cone sampling, but legacy rebuild checks are throttled and players can switch to [b]sparse[/b] sampling at runtime in Mod Options.
[*]Directional LOS now treats fences, counters, and half walls as low cover instead of solid walls, and supported windows or see-through openings follow curtain state.
[*][b]Debug[/b] — live overlay and directional-light authoring mode with instant preset import for registered non-vanilla modes, exposed only in debug-enabled singleplayer.
[*][b]White Phosphor[/b] — cooler grayscale or blue-white profile.
[*][b]White Phosphor Overlay[/b] — white-phosphor overlay paired with the single-point-light path instead of the directional cone.
[*][b]White Phosphor Overlay /w Glare[/b] — the phosphor overlay point-light variant with glare enabled.
[*][b]Zomboid Native[/b] — Zomboid's built-in night vision effect plus a tuned indoor helper light.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]For Modders[/h2]
Add [b]NightVision = true,[/b] to a clothing item script and the framework will handle the rest. [b]Tags = NVITEM,[/b] is still accepted as a legacy fallback. Full documentation lives in [b]README.md[/b].

[b]Features available to modders:[/b]
[list]
[*]Automatic NV detection via the [b]NightVision = true[/b] script key
[*]Battery-aware toggle flow with automatic shutdown on invalid gear or empty battery
[*]Exact state-token swapping for [b]_ON / _OFF[/b] and [b]_DOWN / _UP[/b]
[*]Dynamic directional-light helper, single-point-light helper, or vanilla-style indoor helper reuse
[*]Texture-backed overlay noise via [b]noiseTexturePaths[/b] for filmed or sensor-style modes
[*]Built-in in-game debugger for live overlay and directional-light tuning in debug-enabled singleplayer
[*]External mode registration through [b]NV.RegisterNightVisionMode({ ... })[/b]
[*]Copyable dummy mode example with tuned overlay and light profiles, including comments for the framework light flags and profile variables
[*]Complete example item with models and textures
[/list]

[b]Model swap:[/b] To get the visor-up or visor-down visual, provide two item variants that use exact [b]_ON / _OFF[/b] or [b]_DOWN / _UP[/b] state tokens in the item name. The framework swaps only that exact token, so names like [b]..._UP-HeadStrap[/b] are handled safely.

[hr][/hr]
[b]Multiplayer note:[/b] Battery state, live battery-bar updates, battery install/remove, and named visor state variants use shared or server-authoritative synchronization. The screen effect itself remains local to the wearer, as intended.

3684572876.title: ZBLuaPerfMon
3684572876.description:
[h1]Lua Performance Monitor[/h1]

A Project Zomboid mod that provides a real-time On-Screen Display (OSD) and logging for monitoring Lua function performance.

[b]Features:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Real-time OSD:[/b] View top time-consuming Lua functions directly in-game.
[*] [b]Detailed Logging:[/b] Periodic logging of performance statistics to the console.
[*] [b]Configurable OSD:[/b] Customize the number of functions shown, minimum time threshold, update interval, and visual appearance.
[*] [b]Smart Filtering:[/b] Categorizes functions by source (Mod, Game, or Internal).
[*] [b]Mod Options Integration:[/b] Easily configure all settings through the game's mod options menu.
[*] [b]Toggleable OSD:[/b] Bind a key to quickly show/hide the performance monitor.
[/list]

[b]What it does:[/b]
ZBLuaPerfMon hooks into the game's Lua execution engine to track the execution time of Lua functions. It provides a real-time OSD showing the most time-consuming functions and can log detailed statistics to the console. This is an essential tool for modders to identify and optimize performance bottlenecks in their Lua scripts.

[b]Tested with game versions[/b]
[list]
[*] 42.13
[*] 42.14
[*] 42.15
[/list]

[b]📦 Installation:[/b]
1. [b]Prerequisites:[/b] You must have [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3619862853]ZombieBuddy[/url] installed and configured first.
2. [b]Enable the mod:[/b] Enable ZBLuaPerfMon in the Project Zomboid mod manager.

[b]Links:[/b]
[url=https://github.com/zed-0xff/ZBLuaPerfMon]GitHub Repository[/url]
[url=https://github.com/zed-0xff/ZombieBuddy]ZombieBuddy Framework[/url]

[b]☕ Support the Developer:[/b]
If you find this mod useful, consider supporting the developer with a coffee:
[url=https://ko-fi.com/zed_0xff][img]https://i.imgur.com/Utx6OIH.png[/img][/url]

[b]⚠️ Disclaimer:[/b]
This mod modifies core game Lua execution behavior. While designed for performance monitoring, the overhead of tracking every Lua call may slightly impact game performance when enabled. Use at your own risk.

3685035630.title: Vehicle Safety - Seatbelt, Crash & Ejection
3685035630.description:
[h1]🚗 Vehicle Safety - Seatbelt, Crash & Ejection[/h1]

[i]Every trip can turn into a one-way ride to the morgue. Buckle up.[/i]

[b]⚠️ IMPORTANT:[/b] Set [b]"Player Damage From Crash"[/b] to [b]FALSE[/b] in sandbox options — this mod fully replaces the vanilla crash system.

[hr]

[h2]✨ What's new in v2.2[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Radial menu integration:[/b] Buckle / Unbuckle Seatbelt slice in the vehicle radial menu (V key).
[*] Dynamic label switches between "Buckle Seatbelt" and "Unbuckle Seatbelt" based on current state.
[*] [b]B[/b] keybind still works — both entry points share the same logic.
[/list]

[h2]✨ v2.1[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Phantom crashes from network lag — FIXED.[/b] No more fake injuries for passengers on laggy servers.
[*] Driver-authoritative crash detection with 2-tick confirmation (rejects brief lag spikes).
[*] Server fan-out: every occupant takes proportional crash damage in MP.
[*] Server-side anti-cheat: only the driver can report a crash.
[*] Singleplayer behavior unchanged.
[/list]

[hr]

[h2]Features[/h2]

[h3]🪢 Seatbelt[/h3]
[list]
[*] Toggle on/off with a configurable keybind (default: [b]B[/b]) or via the vehicle radial menu (V key)
[*] [b]70%[/b] crash damage reduction when buckled up
[*] Chest contusion and rib fracture risk on violent crashes
[*] Realistic fumbling delay when exiting the vehicle with the seatbelt on
[*] Moodle status indicator (requires Moodle Framework)
[/list]

[h3]💥 Crash system[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]3 severity levels[/b] — light, medium, violent — based on sudden deceleration
[*] Damage distributed across head, torso and legs
[*] [b]Whiplash[/b]: neck stiffness and pain on medium/violent crashes
[*] Risk of fractures starting from medium impacts (without seatbelt)
[*] Head slams into the windshield during an unbuckled crash
[*] Progressive windshield damage proportional to speed
[/list]

[h3]🪟 Ejection through the windshield[/h3]
[list]
[*] Conditions: no seatbelt + destroyed windshield (0%) + violent crash
[*] [b]Breakthrough ejection[/b]: head punching through a weakened windshield triggers immediate ejection
[*] Staged ejection with knockdown animation
[*] Deep glass cuts from windshield shards
[*] [b]Structure collision[/b]: obstacles in the trajectory stop the ejection with bonus impact damage and arm fractures
[*] Fracture chance proportional to speed
[/list]

[h3]🎯 Passenger damage by seat[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Driver[/b]: 100% damage
[*] [b]Front passenger[/b]: 90% damage (configurable), same windshield effects and ejection
[*] [b]Rear / middle passenger[/b]: 50% damage (configurable), no ejection, no windshield effects
[*] Whiplash reduced by 50% for rear seats
[*] Singleplayer, co-op and multiplayer (server-authoritative damage in MP)
[/list]

[h3]⚙️ Full customization[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]14 sandbox options[/b] to fine-tune every aspect of the mod
[*] Configurable seatbelt keybind
[*] Toggle ejection and windshield damage individually
[/list]

[h2]Compatibility[/h2]
[list]
[*] Build 42.16+
[*] Singleplayer, Co-op, Multiplayer / dedicated server
[*] Compatible with KI5 vehicle packs and any vehicle mod respecting the vanilla API
[/list]

[h2]Optional dependency[/h2]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3396446795]Moodle Framework[/url] — adds a visual seatbelt status indicator. The mod works perfectly without it.

[hr]

[h2]☕ Support the mod[/h2]

If you enjoy this mod and want to support its development, you can buy me a coffee.

[url=https://ko-fi.com/tymox13][b]☕ ko-fi.com/tymox13[/b][/url]

[hr]

[h2]📋 Changelog[/h2]

[h3]v2.2 — Radial Menu[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]NEW:[/b] Buckle / Unbuckle Seatbelt slice in the vehicle radial menu (V key)
[*] [b]NEW:[/b] Dynamic slice label reflects current seatbelt state
[*] [b]KEEP:[/b] Configurable [b]B[/b] keybind still works (shared logic)
[/list]

[h3]v2.1 — Phantom Crash Fix (MP)[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]FIX:[/b] Passengers no longer take phantom crash injuries from network lag spikes — driver-authoritative detection
[*] [b]FIX:[/b] Brief lag spikes no longer mistaken for crashes — 2-tick confirmation with rebound rejection
[*] [b]FIX:[/b] All occupants receive proportional crash damage from server fan-out
[*] [b]NEW:[/b] Server-side anti-cheat — non-driver clients can't report crashes
[*] [b]NEW:[/b] Seatbelt state synced server-side
[*] [b]TARGET:[/b] versionMin bumped to 42.16.0
[/list]

[h3]v2.0 — Multiplayer Fix[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]FIX:[/b] Crash injuries no longer heal instantly in MP — server-authoritative damage
[*] [b]FIX:[/b] All vehicle occupants properly receive crash damage in MP
[*] [b]FIX:[/b] Ejection visible to other players (crash sound broadcast)
[*] [b]NEW:[/b] Server-side damage validation with anti-cheat
[*] [b]NEW:[/b] Windshield condition synced via transmitPartCondition
[*] [b]TECH:[/b] Full client-server architecture
[/list]

[h3]v1.5[/h3]
[list]
[*] Initial release: seatbelt, crash system, ejection, passenger damage, 14 sandbox options
[/list]
