3686455777.title: Crossroads Checkpoint B42
3686455777.description:
*Crossroads Checkpoint*

A fortified military checkpoint and expanded crossroads hub between Muldraugh and West Point.
During the early days of the Knox Event, the military rushed to establish containment lines across Knox Country. One of the largest of these efforts appeared at the highway crossroads between Muldraugh and West Point, where a major road and rail line intersect.
What began as a simple roadblock quickly expanded into a full military screening checkpoint, supported by a National Guard supply yard, rail infrastructure, and a civilian quarantine camp for suspected infected.
This mod transforms the crossroads area into a major point of interest, adding new businesses, infrastructure, and a large military checkpoint that survivors must navigate if traveling between towns.

New Locations
Military Checkpoint
• Highway traffic funnel and vehicle inspection lanes
• Train car barricade blocking the rail crossing
• Guard towers and perimeter fencing
• Military screening area and inspection checkpoint
• Separate quarantine camp for suspected infected
• Holding area where civilians flagged as infected were pulled out of traffic

National Guard Logistics Depot
A military staging area supporting the checkpoint.
Includes:
• National Guard headquarters building
• Vehicle motor pool hangars
• Rail unloading warehouse
• Military storage areas
• helicopter landing pads
• underground bunker access

Civilian Rail Yard
A small industrial rail spur supporting local industry and military logistics.
• warehouse buildings
• rail loading infrastructure
• freight staging areas

Crossroads Businesses
The surrounding crossroads has been expanded with several new and updated locations.
• Refreshed Nolan’s Used Cars dealership
• New car dealership and repair shop
• Truck repair shop
• Beer Barn liquor store
• Farm and hunting supply store
• Welding and metalworking shop
Restaurants & Services

• Updated Spiffo’s with a corrected drive-thru layout
• Roadside café / pancake house
• Grocery store
• Doctor’s office / small clinic
• Video rental store
• Music store

Lodging
• Roadside hotel / motel for travelers passing through the crossroads
Gameplay

The crossroads area now acts as a dangerous choke point between major towns.
Survivors traveling between Muldraugh and West Point will have to pass through the remains of a large military checkpoint and quarantine zone.

Expect:
• dense zombie populations
• military loot opportunities
• abandoned civilian vehicles
• environmental storytelling tied to the Knox containment effort

The surrounding businesses provide additional places to explore and scavenge, turning the crossroads into a small roadside hub that feels like it could have existed in the base game.

Lore Friendly Design
All locations were designed to blend naturally with the vanilla map and fit within the timeline of the Knox Event.
The checkpoint, rail yard, and military staging area tell the story of a containment effort that rapidly escalated as the outbreak spread.

Build Compatibility
Built for Project Zomboid Build 42.
Should work with most map mods unless they modify the crossroads area between Muldraugh and West Point.

*I recommend a ladder climbing mod!*

If you enjoy exploring my maps, you can support future builds here ☕ One cup goes a long way!
https://ko-fi.com/freebird550

Check out my other maps!

Changed loot in a few buildings

3688537535.title: EZRoof [B42.20]
3688537535.description:
Isn't it annoying to build stairs every single time just to put a roof on a rabbit hutch?
At least, it was annoying for me.

EZRoof is a very small quality-of-life mod that lets you place ceilings without building stairs first.

[h2]How to Use:[/h2]
[list]
[*] You have the materials needed to make a floor.
[*] You need a chair or stool. If you don't have these, the "Install Ceiling" option will not appear in the right-click menu.
[*] Be careful not to fall off the scaffolding while installing the ceiling.
[*] No more stairs needed in the rabbit hutch, yay!
[/list]

[h2]Features:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Adds a Place Ceiling option to the right-click menu
[*] Lets you choose between wooden and metal ceilings
[*] [b]Requires a chair or stool as temporary scaffold[/b](This can also be disabled using the sandbox option.)
[*] Works with both carried chairs/stools and nearby placed chairs/stools you can stand on
[*]The goal of this mod is to make roof and ceiling building a little more convenient without heavily breaking vanilla building rules.
[/list]

[h2]Supported version:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Confirmed working on Build 42.20
[*] Multiplayer has not been tested.

[h2]Notes:[/h2]

3694485272.title: Watch Your Step
3694485272.description:
[h1]Watch Your Step[/h1]
[i]Clean up your surroundings bucko![/i]

─────────────────────────────────────────

In vanilla Project Zomboid, a survivor can sprint through a room full of corpses and scattered loot without a second thought. No stumble, no consequence.

[b]Watch Your Step[/b] changes that.

Running or sprinting over loose items and zombie corpses now carries a chance of clipping your foot and going down. A small pile might just knock you off balance. A big one puts you on the floor.

─────────────────────────────────────────

[h2]How It Works[/h2]

[list]
[*] Only triggers while [b]running or sprinting[/b] — walking is always safe
[*] Two outcomes depending on how cluttered the tile is:
[*] [b]Stagger[/b] — you stumble forward but stay upright, no damage
[*] [b]Full fall[/b] — you go to the ground and take vanilla PZ fall damage
[*] A 3-second cooldown prevents repeated triggering in the same area
[/list]

─────────────────────────────────────────

[h2]Trip Chances (defaults)[/h2]

[list]
[*] [b]Loose item[/b] — 2% chance per item on the tile
[*] [b]Zombie corpse[/b] — 10% chance per corpse on the tile
[*] Chances stack — more hazards on a tile means higher risk and a greater chance of a full fall instead of a stagger
[/list]

─────────────────────────────────────────

[h2]Running Skill[/h2]

Your [b]Running[/b] skill reduces trip chance. Higher levels mean fewer stumbles, and at level 10 you are completely immune.

─────────────────────────────────────────

[h2]Sandbox Settings[/h2]

All values are tunable in sandbox options without editing any files:
[list]
[*] Trip chance per loose item
[*] Trip chance per corpse
[*] Fall threshold (how cluttered a tile needs to be to cause a full fall vs stagger)
[*] Trip cooldown in seconds
[/list]

─────────────────────────────────────────

[h2]Multiplayer[/h2]

Works on hosted and dedicated servers. Trip cooldown is tracked server-side.

─────────────────────────────────────────

[b]Mod ID:[/b] WatchYourStep
[b]Build:[/b] 42.x
[b]Version:[/b] 1.0

3694894350.title: Loot Goblin 2000 [B42]
3694894350.description:
[h1]Loot Goblin 2000 for Project Zomboid B42 [SP/MP][/h1]

[quote][i]Your trusty little companion for finding all the good stuff.[/i][/quote]

[h2]Info[/h2]

Ever spent 10 minutes browsing your 50 containers only to realize you have no idea which box that screwdriver ended up in? [b]Loot Goblin 2000[/b] has your back.

[b][url=https://youtu.be/RcfnxfvRspE]watch the intro video that covers the basics[/url][/b]

This mod adds a handy floating panel that lets you search for any item by name (or partial name / item ID) and instantly see which nearby containers hold it. Found what you're looking for? Grab one, grab all, or highlight the item in the container. You can track multiple items at once by stacking search blocks in the panel, so your inner goblin can be greedy about [i]all[/i] the things simultaneously.

[quote]⚠️ [b]Important load order note:[/b] Since [b]Loot Goblin 2000[/b] builds a cache of all available items on startup, it should be placed [b]below any mods that add new items[/b] in your mod load order.[/quote]

The mod requires [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=3508537032]NeatUI Framework[/url] as a dependency.

Supported game versions: 42.14 and up (tested on 42.16).

[h2]Usage[/h2]

Once in-game, press [b];[/b] (semicolon) to toggle the [b]Loot Goblin 2000[/b] panel open/closed. You can rebind this in [b]Options → Mod Options → Loot Goblin 2000[/b] — all options come with tooltips explaining what they do, so go poke around in there.

[b]Quick rundown:[/b]
[list]
[*]Type an item name or ID into the search box — top 5 matches appear instantly
[*]The first result is always a [b]partial match[/b] option (finds anything containing your query)
[*]Select an item and the block switches to [b]finding mode[/b], scanning nearby containers in real time
[*]Use the [b]grab all / grab one / locate[/b] buttons on each found entry
[*]Press [b]'[/b] (apostrophe, also rebindable in mod options) to grab all found items from all containers in your proximity at once
[*]Click the [b]plus button[/b] to add another item to track — stack as many as you like!
[/list]

[b]Templates[/b] let you save and reload your favourite item lists. Hit the template button in the panel header to save your current search setup, load a previously saved one, or clean up old ones you no longer need. The template can also be quickly loaded from the search box by writing its name.

Each search block has an icon button (left of the remove button) that lets you set a [b]specific quantity[/b] that you need. For example, set it to [b]1[/b] for a hammer when preparing for carpentry work (you don't need 10 hammers at once for that, right?) — once your inventory holds at least that many, the block turns [b]blue permanently[/b] and the grab-all hotkey skips it. Click the quantity badge to change or clear the amount. The needed quantity is saved in templates and restored when you reopen the panel.


[h2]Support & Contribution[/h2]

[b][url=https://github.com/deseven/pz-lootgoblin2000]GitHub Repository[/url][/b]

Found a bug? Something not working right? Head over to [b][url=https://github.com/deseven/pz-lootgoblin2000/issues/new]GitHub Issues[/url][/b] — that's the only place where support can be provided, so please don't rely on Steam comments or workshop discussions for help. I might or might not answer there.

Want to make the mod even better? [b]Pull requests are very welcome![/b] Whether it's a bug fix, a new feature, or just tidying something up — contributions are always appreciated.


[h2]Credits[/h2]
[list]
[*]Idea, design, implementation: [url=https://d7.wtf]deseven[/url]
[*]Code: [url=https://claude.ai]Claude[/url]
[*]Icons: [url=https://boxicons.com]Boxicons[/url]
[*]Notification sounds: [url=https://freesound.org]Freesound[/url]
[*]Intro video music: [url=https://www.classicals.de]Gregor Quendel[/url]
[/list]


Workshop ID: 3694894350
Mod ID: LootGoblin2000

3695122429.title: Required Item Navigator [B42.20]
3695122429.description:
Have you ever searched for a recipe, looked at the required items, and then immediately thought, “Okay... but how do I make these materials in the first place?”
At least I do. Constantly.

Required Item Navigator is a very small quality-of-life mod that lets you right-click items shown in the Required Items list to check recipes that produce them, inspect their ingredients, or jump directly to the crafting screen.

[h2]How to use:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Open a recipe in the Crafting or Building window
[*] Right-click an item in the Required Items list that makes you think, “What even is this?”
[*] Choose a recipe from the context menu
[*] Check its tooltip for ingredients and details, or jump directly to the crafting screen
[*] No more mystery ingredient, yay!
[/list]

[h2]Main features:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Lets you look up recipes for items shown in the Required Items list
[*] Works in both the Crafting window and the Building window
[*] If multiple recipes can produce the same item, you can choose from a submenu
[*] Lets you preview recipe details and ingredients in a tooltip before jumping
[/list]

[h2]Supported version:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Confirmed working on Build 42.15
[/list]

[h2]Notes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] For now, some entries such as Unstack may still appear. They are not really "craft this item" recipes in practice, but the game still treats them as recipes, and filtering them out cleanly is more trouble than it is worth.
[*] This mod does not change crafting balance or recipe contents
[*] It is meant as a helper mod to make intermediate items and multi-step crafting chains easier to follow
[*] It will work on MP as well. Probably.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

何かを作ろうとレシピを検索して必要素材を見て、「それで…これらの材料になってるアイテムはどうやって作るんだ…？」となったことはありませんか？少なくとも私はしょっちゅうあります。
Required Item Navigatorは、Required Itemsに表示されている素材を右クリックして、その素材を作れるレシピを確認したり製作画面へ直接飛べるようになるとても小さなQOL MODです

[h2]使い方:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Crafting または Building のレシピを開く
[*] Required Items に並んでいるアイテムから「なんだこれ？」と思った物を右クリックする
[*] 表示されたメニューからレシピを選ぶ
[*] ツールチップで材料等を確認したり、そのまま制作画面へ飛んだりする
[*] 完璧に作り方が分かったぞ！やった！
[/list]

[h2]主な特徴:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Required Itemsがレシピを持つアイテムの場合、逆引きでレシピを確認可能

3696291148.description:
[quote][h1]FIRST IN MOD LOAD ORDER[/h1][/quote]

[quote][h1]Compatibility Notice for Inventory Overhaul Mods[/h1]

Most of Better Pause will work with other mods as long as it is loaded early in your mod load order.

However, complete inventory overhauls can replace vanilla inventory files and may reintroduce pause restrictions inside inventory context menus.

[h2]Clean UI Compatibility[/h2]

Clean UI is supported when the included Better Pause Clean UI compatibility file is loaded after Clean UI.

Recommended load order:

1. TwisTonFire - Better Pause
2. Clean UI
3. Better Pause Clean UI Compatibility File

This allows inventory right-click menus to remain usable while paused.

If another mod completely replaces the inventory system after the compatibility file, it may still reintroduce the vanilla pause restrictions.
[/quote]

[h1]TwisTonFire - Better Pause[/h1]

Better Pause removes the restrictions that Project Zomboid normally applies while [b]Active Pause[/b] is enabled.

In vanilla, many interactions are explicitly blocked while the game is paused. Better Pause removes these restrictions wherever possible, allowing you to inspect menus, prepare actions and queue your next steps while remaining paused.

When you are ready, simply resume the game and the queued actions continue normally.

[h1]Main Features[/h1]

[list]
[*][b]Removes pause restrictions:[/b] Actions and context-menu interactions that are normally blocked during Active Pause can be used while paused.
[*][b]Queue actions while paused:[/b] Plan and prepare actions without having to resume the game first.
[*][b]Automatic pause on world entry:[/b] Optional setting that pauses the game shortly after entering your world.
[*][b]Movable pause message:[/b] The "Game Paused" display can be dragged anywhere on the screen.
[*][b]Persistent pause message position:[/b] Your chosen position is saved and restored between game sessions.
[*][b]Hide pause message:[/b] An optional Mod Option can completely remove the pause message and its background.
[*][b]Localized Mod Options:[/b] The additional Better Pause settings support the available game languages included with the mod.
[/list]

The automatic pause and pause-message options are [b]disabled by default where applicable[/b].

[img]https://imgur.com/a1YFKj0.png[/img]

[h2]Version-Independent Features[/h2]

The additional Better Pause functionality, such as:

[list]
[*]Automatic pause after entering the world
[*]Movable pause message
[*]Saved pause-message position
[*]Option to completely hide the pause message
[/list]

is provided by the mod's common files and is shared across supported game versions.

The actual removal of vanilla pause restrictions is handled separately by [b]version-specific patches[/b], because Project Zomboid's vanilla files can change between updates.

[h2]Important Load Order Information[/h2]

[b]Better Pause must be placed at the very top of your mod load order, before all other mods.[/b]

The reason is simple:

[list]
[*]The pause-restriction patches use [b]full vanilla file overrides[/b].
[*]These files need to load first so other mods can safely apply their changes afterward.
[*]Mods that replace the same vanilla files later in the load order may reintroduce individual pause restrictions.
[/list]

[h2]Why full file overrides are necessary[/h2]

Many of Project Zomboid's pause checks are located high inside large vanilla functions.

Because of this, they often cannot be removed reliably through small Lua hooks or compatibility patches without replacing the affected vanilla file.

Better Pause therefore provides dedicated patches for each supported Project Zomboid version.

[h2]Updates and Game Versions[/h2]

Each Better Pause patch is made specifically for the Project Zomboid version it targets.

When the game updates, the affected vanilla files are regenerated from the new game version and the pause restrictions are removed again.

This keeps the patches closely aligned with the current vanilla files instead of carrying old files forward between game versions.

[h2]Summary[/h2]

[list]
[*]Removes known Active Pause restrictions
[*]Allows actions to be prepared and queued while paused
[*]Optional automatic pause after entering a world
[*]Movable "Game Paused" display
[*]Pause-message position saved between sessions
[*]Optional setting to completely hide the pause display
[*]Localized Mod Options
[*]Version-specific vanilla patches
[*]Common quality-of-life features shared across supported versions
[*]Must be placed [b]first in the mod load order[/b]
[/list]

[h2]Is this mod better than X?[/h2]

I cannot say whether Better Pause is better than another pause mod.

What I can say is that Better Pause is designed around a clear approach:

[list]
[*]It is intended to load before other mods.
[*]Pause-restriction patches are separated by Project Zomboid version.
[*]Old version-specific patches do not overwrite newer game versions.
[*]The common Better Pause features remain available independently of those version-specific patches.
[*]The mod is maintained so new Project Zomboid versions can be supported quickly.
[/list]

The pause restrictions are removed from the affected vanilla files rather than simply being commented out.

3698742271.title: Video Framebuffer
3698742271.description:
The first-ever pixel-level framebuffer for Project Zomboid.

Draw anything -- emulators, video playback, dynamic visualizations, mini-games -- all rendered at GPU speed inside PZ's UI.

PZFB is a library mod that provides a framebuffer API for other mods to use as a dependency.

SETUP (first time, and after every PZFB update):
  1. Subscribe and enable the mod, then start a game.
  2. A red "Setup Required" (or orange "Update Required" after an update) panel appears.
  3. The panel shows where your auto-generated install script is:
     - PZ 42.20 and newer: the script is created inside the mod folder itself (its common subfolder).
       Click "Copy Path" on the panel, then:
         Windows: paste the path into Explorer's address bar and press Enter to run it.
         Linux: open a terminal and run: bash "<paste the path>"
       A fallback copy named pzfb_install.txt is also written to Zomboid/Lua
       (Linux: run it with bash as-is; Windows: rename it to pzfb_install.bat first).
     - Older PZ builds: the script lands in Zomboid/Lua as pzfb_install.bat (Windows,
       double-click it) or pzfb_install.sh (Linux: bash ~/Zomboid/Lua/pzfb_install.sh).
  4. The script auto-detects your PZ install and copies 12 small class files into it.
  5. Restart Project Zomboid. Done.

WHY THE EXTRA STEP: Steam Workshop refuses to distribute .class/.bat/.sh files, and Project Zomboid loads Java classes only from its install directory, so a mod cannot install itself. PZ 42.20 also stopped Lua from writing .bat/.sh files into Zomboid/Lua, which is why the script now lives in the mod folder (PZFB 1.7.2 and older generate no script at all on 42.20 -- update PZFB).

If your antivirus flags the script (it copies files into the Steam install dir), open it in any text editor first to see exactly what it does.

Manual install (if the script cannot find your PZ install): inside the mod folder, rename each file in 42/media/pzfb/Color*.dat to Color*.class and copy them into <YourPZInstall>/zombie/core/. On Windows the install dir is the ProjectZomboid folder itself; on Linux it is the inner ProjectZomboid/projectzomboid folder.

DEMO: Press HOME to open a test framebuffer window, END to close it. These keys are remappable in PZFBTest.lua.

FOR MOD AUTHORS: Add require=PZFB to your mod.info, then use the PZFB Lua API to create and draw framebuffers. API reference: https://github.com/expectbugs/pzfb/blob/main/docs/API_REFERENCE.md

Source: https://github.com/expectbugs/pzfb

3705530591.title: Jeeve's Build
3705530591.description:
[h1]Jeeve's Build[/h1]

[hr][/hr]

Expand your building options by unlocking craft recipes for walls, doorframes, windowframes, fences, stairs, decorative props, floors, garage doors, and light switches — all drawn directly from the tile packs already loaded on your server.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Adding & Removing Mid-Save[/h2]

[b]Add to an existing save:[/b] [b]Safe[/b], provided all five tile packs below are subscribed first — the game refuses to load JeevesBuild without them. Nothing is added to the world or to loot; the new entries simply appear in your build menu.

[b]Remove from an existing save:[/b] [b]Not safe if you have placed any garage doors.[/b] Walls, doorframes, windowframes, fences, stairs, floors and props are made from the tile packs' own sprites, so those survive as long as the packs stay subscribed and you only lose the recipes to build more. Two things do not:

[list]
[*] [b]Garage doors[/b] are the one piece drawn from JeevesBuild's own tiles, and they are the reason this is not a safe removal. The game stores every object you place as a bare tile [i]number[/i], never a name, and that number only means anything while this mod is loaded to own it. Once it is gone the save holds no record of what those objects were, and there is no supported way to undo that. Taking them down first is [b]not[/b] a fix — it has never been shown to work, and the damage happens when the world loads, not when you remove the mod. If you want this mod off a world, start a new one.
[*] [b]Light switches[/b] keep their vanilla sprite but stop working — the wiring is this mod's, the sprite is not.
[/list]

[b]Server admins:[/b] do not delete your save's world dictionary to clear a mod error. Item IDs are re-derived from whatever mods are loaded at that moment, and every stored item is only an ID — containers come back holding different things.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]What It Adds[/h2]

[list]
[*][b]Walls[/b] — craftable wall entities for every supported tile pack
[*][b]Doorframes & Windowframes[/b] — placeable frames that accept vanilla doors and windows
[*][b]Fences[/b] — low fences in every supported material variant
[*][b]Stairs[/b] — multi-segment staircases
[*][b]Decorative misc[/b] — benches, lamps, props, and set dressing
[*][b]Masonry floors[/b] — concrete, pavement, flagstone, cobble, asphalt, stone slab, rubble, rough stone, and road lines
[*][b]Garage doors[/b] — six color/style variants (White Solid, Green Solid, Silver Solid, Grey Solid, Red Windowed, Grey Windowed) in player-selectable widths
[*][b]Light switches[/b] — functional wall-mounted switches with room lighting integration
[/list]

Close to five thousand buildable entries in total, generated straight from the tile packs' own definitions.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Required Tile Packs[/h2]

JeevesBuild is a hard dependency on the following tile packs — [b]all five must be subscribed[/b] for the mod to load:

[list]
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2837923608]Pert's Party Tiles[/url] (bundles Christmas Village content)
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2852704777]Simon MD's Tiles[/url]
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2879745353]Melo's Tiles for Miles[/url]
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3628736763]Community Tile Pack[/url] (Diederik's, Dylan's, Ekron, tkTiles, DTiles, Blackwood — maintained by the Unofficial PZ Mapping Discord)
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3666137359]Rocco's Tiles[/url]
[/list]

These are listed in JeevesBuild's mod.info as [code]require=[/code] — Project Zomboid will refuse to load JeevesBuild if any of them are missing from the mod list. Unsubscribing a tile pack from a world that has JeevesBuild structures in it is a far bigger problem than removing JeevesBuild itself: the sprites those structures are made of go with it.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Design Philosophy[/h2]

[b]Almost zero new assets.[/b] Every buildable entity reuses sprites the tile packs already ship — no competing tilesheets, no duplicate sprites, no texture conflicts. The sole exception is the garage door set, which ships its own small tile pack because no loaded pack provided one.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Compatibility[/h2]

[list]
[*]Build 42 (42.14+)
[*]Multiplayer-safe — server and client content auto-sync on connect
[*]Standalone — no required dependencies on other Jeeves mods
[*]Works with admin build menu / admin cheat mode
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Credits[/h2]

Tile pack authors retain full credit for their original artwork. JeevesBuild is a gameplay-integration layer; none of the sprites are redistributed.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Part of the Jeeves Ecosystem[/h2]

[list]
[*] [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3660924327]Jeeve's Integration[/url][/b] — Discord bridge, ranks and alerts
[*] [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3674013419]Jeeve's Claims[/url][/b] — Safehouse and vehicle claims
[*] [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3672451284]Jeeve's Drops[/url][/b] — Airdrop and supply events
[*] [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3672042113]Jeeve's Hordes[/url][/b] — Horde night events
[*] [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3674452315]Jeeve's Journals[/url][/b] — Skill recovery journals
[*] [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3684025083]Jeeve's Patches[/url][/b] — Third-party mod fixes
[*] [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3687487317]Jeeve's QoL[/url][/b] — Quality-of-life bundle
[*] [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3693550188]Jeeve's Personal Computer[/url][/b] — Computers, games, skill backup
[*] [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3739941052]Jeeve's Zones[/url][/b] — Per-zone map rules
[*] [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3737412008]Jeeve's Solar Arrays[/url][/b] — Off-grid solar power
[/list]

3705580001.title: Car to Car Siphon [42.20]
3705580001.description:
[h1]Car to Car Siphon[/h1]

Transfer fuel directly between two vehicles using nothing but a rubber hose — just like survivors have done.

[h2]How it works — real life[/h2]
In reality, siphoning fuel requires inserting a flexible hose into one vehicle's fuel filler neck, creating a pressure difference (usually by mouth or a hand pump), and letting gravity or suction draw the fuel through the hose into a second container or another tank. It's a slow, manual process that takes several minutes per litre and works best when the donor tank is higher than the receiver.

[h2]How it works in-game[/h2]
[list]
[*] Park two vehicles [b]side by side[/b] so their fuel caps are within ~1 tile of each other.
[*] Have a [b]Rubber Hose[/b] in your inventory.
[*] Stand next to a gas tank, press [b]V[/b] to open the radial menu and select the [b]"Siphon Fuel"[/b] option.
[/list]

[h2]Requirements[/h2]
[list]
[*] Rubber Hose (found in garages, hardware stores, and vehicle trunks)
[/list]

[h2]This is by no means a replacement for Refueling your car the usual ways, its meant to be an emergency solution, its slow, trust me it is ;o . It will scale with your mechanics lvl[/h2]

[i]No electricity, no jerry cans — just a hose and two cars.[/i]

Mod ID: Car2CarSiphon

3707251461.title: Zed's Item Tiers
3707251461.description:
[h1]Zed's Item Tiers[/h1]

Tired of the same loot everywhere and losing the thrill of exploration? [b]Zed's Item Tiers[/b] adds a [b]probability-based rarity system[/b] to Project Zomboid: almost any item can roll as [b]Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, or Legendary[/b] when it enters the world. Higher tiers are genuinely stronger—lighter bags, deadlier weapons, tougher clothes—so scavenging and crafting stay interesting instead of flat. [b]New highlight:[/b] tiered clothing now has active [b]Thermoregulation[/b] behavior, not just static stats.

[h2]How it works[/h2]
[list]
[*]Tiers are assigned when items spawn or appear in containers; [b]Common[/b] items behave like vanilla (no tier bonuses).
[*]Each tier has a [b]default spawn weight[/b] (see Tiers below). You can tune probabilities in the mod’s Lua if you want a stingier or more generous economy.
[*][b]Tooltips[/b] show the item’s tier and the bonuses that apply to that item type, so you can compare loot at a glance.
[/list]

[h2]Tiers (default chances)[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Common[/b] — 80% — White (no bonuses)
[*][b]Uncommon[/b] — 16% — Green
[*][b]Rare[/b] — 3.2% — Blue
[*][b]Epic[/b] — 0.64% — Purple
[*][b]Legendary[/b] — 0.16% — Gold
[/list]

[h2]New: Thermoregulation (clothing)[/h2]
[b]Thermoregulation is now an active mechanic.[/b] On insulated clothing, tier bonuses dynamically adapt insulation while worn:
[list]
[*]All clothing from [b]Rare tier and above[/b] gets Thermoregulation.
[*]If covered body parts run [b]hot[/b], insulation shifts [b]down[/b] (cooling support).
[*]If covered body parts run [b]cold[/b], insulation shifts [b]up[/b] (warming support).
[*]The shift range is tied to the item's [b]Thermoregulation bonus[/b], so higher-tier clothing adapts more.
[*]Thermoregulated clothing also [b]self-dries faster[/b] when wet.
[/list]

[h2]Bonuses by item type[/h2]
Bonuses only apply where the item actually supports the stat. [b]Thermoregulation[/b] is one of the headline systems now. In practice:

[list]
[*][b]Weapons:[/b] damage, crit, handling-style stats where applicable; [b]weapon weight[/b] needs the optional Java path (see ZombieBuddy).
[*][b]Clothing:[/b] bite/scratch (and related) defense, run speed, vision and hearing modifiers where relevant, plus [b]thermoregulation[/b] on insulated gear: while worn, insulation nudges toward what your covered body parts need (hotter → less insulation, colder → more), and tiered clothes with thermoregulation [b]dry faster[/b] when wet.
[*][b]Containers:[/b] capacity, encumbrance reduction, max item size where supported.
[*][b]Drainables:[/b] fluid capacity where the item uses a fluid container.
[*][b]Literature:[/b] mood-related stats and reading speed where the book supports them.
[*][b]Flashlights / battery gear:[/b] lower drain where hooked.
[*][b]Food:[/b] improved hunger reduction on higher tiers where the item is food.
[*][b]Legendary style bonus:[/b] all [b]worn Legendary[/b] items provide a small mood/stress boost, so yes, your cool bellybutton piercing finally has gameplay value.
[/list]

[h2]Crafting[/h2]
Crafted output tier follows your [b]ingredient tiers[/b] in a [b]Factorio-style[/b] way: the result is never worse than the “floor” set by your best ingredient tier, mixed inputs influence the roll, and [b]relevant crafting skill[/b] can slightly improve (or worsen) the outcome. Recycling good components into better gear is part of the loop.

[h2]Optional: ZombieBuddy[/h2]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3619862853][b]ZombieBuddy[/b][/url] enables [b]Java-side[/b] bonuses that pure Lua cannot apply cleanly—most notably [b]weapon weight[/b]. The mod is fully playable without it; you just skip those Java-only perks.

[h2]Compatible mods[/h2]
[list]
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3604080281]Better Clothing Info[/url]
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3437629766]CleanUI[/url]
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3671173479]Glass Cutter[/url]
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3694097672]TooltipLib[/url]
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3659195975]Science, Bitch![/url]
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3555588616]Sewing Workbranch[/url]
[/list]

[h2]FAQ[/h2]
[b]Q: Is it safe to add/remove on existing saves?[/b]
[b]A:[/b] Yes.

[b]Q: What game versions were tested?[/b]
[b]A:[/b] 42.13 - 42.16.

[b]Q: MP support?[/b]
[b]A:[/b] Not tested.

[b]Q: Load order?[/b]
[b]A:[/b] Try to place it last in the list.

[url=https://github.com/zed-0xff/ZItemTiers]GitHub[/url]

3707376688.title: SmartZOptimizer[Legacy]
3707376688.description:
Smart Z Optimizer
Overview
A performance optimization mod for Project Zomboid B42. Reduces processing load during scenes with large numbers of zombies and during bad weather. Requires ZombieBuddy's extension functionality.



Features

Enable Smart Z Optimizer
When a large number of zombies are in the area, this feature reduces system load by skipping the AI processing of inactive zombies (including roaming ones) every few frames—such as those with no target, unalerted, or not attracted by sound.
Once a zombie starts moving or reacts to sound or vision, it automatically returns to normal processing from the very next frame (a delay of up to approximately 100ms may occur before the reaction begins). This has almost no impact on standard zombie behavior.

Weather Particle Render %
Reduces the number of particles rendered during bad weather such as storms, heavy snow, and dense fog, lowering rendering load. 100% disables the effect; 50% halves the particle count. Can be combined with vanilla graphics settings.

Enable OpenCL Weather Acceleration (Experimental)
Offloads part of the weather simulation from CPU to GPU during active weather events, reducing CPU load. Requires an OpenCL-compatible GPU.

Enable Performance Metrics
Outputs optimization status to the console. Use for verification or troubleshooting.

Exclude Corpse Containers
Excludes items inside corpse containers from being scanned for crafting and building recipes.
A restart is required for changes to take effect. You will no longer be able to rip clothing directly from the crafting UI while it is on a corpse; however, moving the items to your inventory or the floor will allow them to be recognized as crafting materials.

Corpse Scan Right-Click Toggle
Key binding to toggle the context menu crafting for items inside corpse containers.
This setting is disabled when "Exclude Corpse Containers" is turned off.



Requirements & Notes

ZombieBuddy is required. Simply subscribing is not enough — please follow the installation instructions on the ZombieBuddy mod page.
OpenCL acceleration is an experimental feature. Testing has only been performed with NVIDIA GPUs and drivers. Compatibility with AMD, Intel, or other GPU vendors is unknown.
Some NVIDIA driver versions may cause issues. A crash was confirmed with driver version 566.36.
If OpenCL is unavailable in your environment, the feature will be automatically disabled.


Workshop ID: 3707376688
Mod ID: SmartZOptimizer

3710116647.title: Better Vanilla Filters and UI
3710116647.description:
[h1]Better Vanilla Filters and UI[/h1]
[i]Build 42 gas mask, respirator, and SCBA/hazmat-friendly filter HUD with smarter mask control, Best Available filter swaps, optional no-mask auto-hide, and RealismV4-friendly QoL.[/i]

[h2]At a Glance[/h2]
[hr][list]
[*]Cleaner [b]Filter UI[/b] for the mask you are actually wearing
[*]Configurable [b]Toggle Mask On/Off[/b] hotkey with smart mask priority
[*]Right-click HUD actions for [b]Wear Filtered Mask[/b], [b]All Mask Actions[/b], and [b]Filter Actions[/b]
[*]Deterministic [b]Best Available[/b] filter attach and replace behavior
[*]Optional no-mask auto-hide plus separate icon and bar scaling
[/list]

[h2]What This Mod Does[/h2]
[hr][list]
[*]Adds a compact on-screen [b]Filter UI[/b] for gas masks and respirators.
[*]Shows the [b]actually equipped mask[/b], not a fake UI-only item.
[*]Displays live remaining filter durability with a large, easy-to-read status bar.
[*]Uses a transparent HUD that can be moved freely and remembers its saved position.
[*]Lets you drag the HUD by left-clicking the mask frame.
[*]Opens custom [b]Mask Actions[/b] and quick-equip options when you right-click the HUD icon.
[*]Shows only real wearable masks in [b]Wear Filtered Mask[/b], not refill filters or carrier items.
[*]Can automatically fade the HUD out when no compatible mask is equipped, if enabled in Mod Options.
[*]Changes bar color as durability drops and gives a strong warning when the filter is critical or missing.
[/list]

[h2]Hotkeys & Shortcuts[/h2]
[hr][list]
[*]Adds a configurable [b]Toggle Mask On/Off[/b] keybind in [b]Mod Options[/b].
[*]If a compatible mask is currently equipped, the hotkey takes that exact mask off.
[*]If no compatible mask is equipped, the hotkey first tries to put the [b]last mask you removed[/b] back on.
[*]If that exact mask is gone, fallback prefers same type, then same family, then full gas masks over lighter respirators, then filtered masks, and only then higher filter percent.
[*]This avoids bad auto-picks where a weaker mask wins just because its filter is slightly fresher.
[*]HUD right-click shortcuts stay available if you prefer explicit manual mask and filter actions.
[/list]

[h2]Gameplay Integration[/h2]
[hr][list]
[*]Reads the real filter state from the equipped item so HUD and tooltip stay aligned.
[*]Includes a [b]sandbox filter durability multiplier[/b] so filters can last longer without changing the HUD's 0-100% scale.
[*]Supports vanilla-style gas masks, respirators, and SCBA/hazmat-style protective gear recognition in the HUD flow, plus compatible modded masks that use the normal filter system.
[*][b]Filter Actions[/b] search your inventory recursively for compatible filters instead of only checking the top level.
[*][b]Best Available[/b] always chooses the non-empty compatible filter with the highest remaining durability.
[*]Replacing a filter puts the old filter back into your inventory instead of deleting it.
[*]Attaching and replacing filters use timed actions instead of instant swaps.
[/list]

[h2]Sandbox & Options[/h2]
[hr][list]
[*][b]Sandbox option:[/b] Filter durability multiplier from [b]x1.0[/b] up to [b]x5.0[/b].
[*][b]Mod options:[/b] separate scale controls for the mask icon and the durability bar.
[*]Compact presets include [b]0.75x[/b] and [b]0.5x[/b], and the durability bar also supports a dedicated [b]3x[/b] option.
[*][b]Mod option:[/b] [b]Enable HUD[/b] to fully turn the HUD on/off per player preference.
[*][b]Mod option:[/b] optional no-mask auto-hide. Off by default.
[*][b]Mod option:[/b] assign your own [b]Toggle Mask On/Off[/b] hotkey.
[*]When no-mask auto-hide is enabled, mouseover or equipping a mask brings the HUD back.
[*]The durability bar always stays normalized to [b]0-100%[/b], even when filters last longer.
[/list]

[h2]Compatibility[/h2]
[hr][list]
[*]Works standalone.
[*]Compatible with [b]Build 42.16.x[/b] and [b]Build 42.17[/b].
[*]Compatible with [b]Gas Mask Attach[/b] for hotbar/attachment-based gas mask carry and quick equip workflows.
[*]Compatible with [b]Necroa Mod[/b] and [b]Necroa Mod | Gamer's Patch[/b] as fallback-compatible filter sources.
[*]Compatible with supported modded gas-mask items such as [b]KATTAJ1 Military Pack[/b], the supported [b][J&G][/b] uniform packs, and current [b]The Ark[/b] reports involving filter swap model refresh.
[*]Does not require [b]Susceptible[/b] to function.
[*]If Susceptible-style HUDs are present, this mod is intended to replace their filter display with its own cleaner panel.
[*]Avoids false HUD triggers from mask carrier pouches and other non-mask container items.
[/list]

3710281407.title: [B42] Peek a View
3710281407.description:
[h1]What it does[/h1]

Your character sees more than your screen shows. PeekAView draws what the game already counts as seen but keeps hidden. No wallhack: line of sight still decides.

[list]
[*][b]Wall cutaway[/b]: walls cut away at greater distance, doorways and corners open up as you approach.
[*][b]Tree fade[/b]: whole trees around your character go see-through, and in your view direction while you aim. On foot and in vehicles. Replaces the vanilla dither circle.
[*][b]Stair view[/b]: the upper floor draws while you climb. Zombies in the room you're climbing into are visible.
[/list]

Every feature has its own toggle under Options → Mods → Peek a View. [b]F8[/b] switches the mod on and off in game (rebindable).

[h1]Requirements[/h1]
[list]
[*]PZ Build 42.20 or later
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3619862853]ZombieBuddy[/url], one-time install for any Java mod
[/list]

On first launch ZombieBuddy asks whether to load PeekAView's JAR, tick Allow.

[h1]Compatibility[/h1]
[list]
[*]Safe to add or remove mid-save, the mod stores nothing in the save.
[*]Runs alongside the Staircast Workshop mod: PeekAView yields its own stair view.
[*]Works with [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3782670683]Wind Sway[/url], my foliage sway mod.
[/list]

[h1]Multiplayer / dedicated servers[/h1]
PeekAView is client-side: the server runs none of its code, each player only sees the effect on their own screen. Two things still have to be in place:

[list]
[*][b]On the server[/b]: both mods go into the server's .ini, so joining clients download and enable them (keep your other entries, separate with semicolons; 3619862853 = ZombieBuddy, 3710281407 = Peek a View):
[code]Mods=ZombieBuddy;PeekAView
WorkshopItems=3619862853;3710281407[/code]
[*][b]On every player's PC[/b]: ZombieBuddy's one-time setup from its Workshop page. The server can't do that part for you.
[/list]

[h1]FAQ[/h1]

[b]What does "Fix B42 Wall-Hiding Bug" do?[/b]
Vanilla B42 can hide upper-floor walls next to player-built structures. The toggle (off by default) stops that. Enable it only if you see the holes: decks attached to vanilla walls render more visibly with it on.

[b]Added it to an existing save and nothing changed?[/b]
Subscribing doesn't switch a mod on in saves that already exist. Load Game → select the save → "Choose Mods..." → tick ZombieBuddy and Peek a View.

[b]Options → Mods → Peek a View says the Java component is not loaded?[/b]
ZombieBuddy isn't installed, or you declined the prompt. To undo a decline, edit [noparse]%USERPROFILE%\.zombie_buddy\mod_approvals.json[/noparse]: in the [noparse]"id": "PeekAView"[/noparse] block flip [noparse]"decision": false[/noparse] to [noparse]true[/noparse], restart PZ.

[h1]Maintenance & Source[/h1]
Last tested against PZ build 42.20.4.
MIT-licensed, fully open source: [url=https://github.com/armakupub/PeekAView]github.com/armakupub/PeekAView[/url]. Forks welcome.

[h1]Attribution[/h1]
Stair view builds on [url=https://github.com/copiumsawsed/pz-Staircast]copiumsawsed/pz-Staircast[/url] (MIT, original Workshop mod) via my read-path fork [url=https://github.com/armakupub/staircast-rp]armakupub/staircast-rp[/url] (MIT).
PeekAView adds: zombies in the room you're climbing into stay visible through the whole climb.

[hr][/hr]

Workshop ID: 3710281407
Mod ID: PeekAView

3710913197.title: Mini Health Plus
3710913197.description:
[h1]Mini Health Plus[/h1]
A modernized and expanded rework of the original [b]Mini Health Panel[/b], designed to give you a clean, compact, and highly customizable overview of your character’s condition without constantly opening the vanilla health panel.

This version is based on [b]Mini Health Panel by Speedy Von Gofast[/b], but has been [b]heavily reworked and extended by TwisTonFire[/b] with many interface, usability, compatibility, and feature improvements.
[h2]What this version adds[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Scalable UI[/b]
[*][b]HD textures[/b]
[*][b]Always-on-top option[/b]
[*][b]Always-visible option[/b]
[*][b]Improved drag and drop behavior[/b]
[*][b]Improved detached settings window[/b]
[*][b]Soft pulse injury animation[/b] instead of the old harsh fast blinking
[*][b]Adjustable animation speed[/b] directly in the built-in settings menu
[*][b]Live preview for animation speed changes[/b] before saving
[*][b]Optional muscle strain indicators[/b]
[*][b]Optional Better Character Info avatar integration[/b]
[*][b]In-game Mod Options[/b] to disable the mod or only show it when treatment is needed
[*][b]Sandbox options[/b] to decide which helper features should be enabled
[*][b]Translations for many languages[/b]
[*][b]Ongoing improvements[/b] with more refinements planned over time
[/list]

[h2]In-game Mod Options[/h2]
Mini Health Plus now includes additional [b]in-game Mod Options[/b] for players and server communities who want more control over when the UI appears.

Current Mod Options include:
[list]
[*][b]Disable Mini Health Plus[/b]  
Completely disables the Mini Health Plus panel if you do not want to use the UI.
[*][b]Only show when treatment is needed[/b]  
Mini Health Plus only appears when there is a wound or condition that truly requires treatment.
[/list]

These options are useful for players who prefer a cleaner screen, or for multiplayer communities where some players may not want the panel visible all the time.
[img]https://imgur.com/gVSPMlP.png[/img]
[h2]Better Character Info integration[/h2]
If [b]Better Character Info[/b] is installed, Mini Health Plus can optionally show the [b]BCI avatar popout[/b] during idle moments.

When enabled:
[list]
[*]The BCI avatar can be shown when Mini Health Plus has nothing important to display.
[*]Mini Health Plus automatically switches back in when a wound, treatment state, stitch check, removable treatment, or relevant muscle strain state needs attention.
[*]The BCI avatar and Mini Health Plus panel are kept separated during normal idle/attention states, so they do not overlap unnecessarily.
[*]A small Mini Health Plus settings gear can appear on the BCI avatar popout while hovering it.
[*]Opening the Character Info screen can still work normally while keeping the Mini Health Plus controlled avatar behavior intact.
[/list]

This integration is optional and only appears when Better Character Info is active.

[h2]Sandbox Options — You decide the rules[/h2]
Mini Health Plus includes [b]sandbox options[/b], allowing world creators and server hosts to decide how much help the UI should provide.

Current sandbox options include:
[list]
[*][b]Enable Replace Bandage[/b]  
Adds the [b]Replace Bandage[/b] context menu entry for dirty bandages.
[*][b]Blue indicator for safe removal[/b]  
Shows when a bandage or splint can likely be removed safely.
[*][b]Purple indicator for stitch check[/b]  
Shows when a stitched wound has likely reached the point where it should be checked.
[/list]

[img]https://imgur.com/KlyPftc.png[/img]

[h2]What it does[/h2]
Mini Health Plus provides a compact and minimalistic overview of your character’s wounds and treatment states.

The silhouette can stay visible at all times, hide itself when there is nothing that needs attention, or only appear when actual treatment is required, depending on your settings.

[list]
[*][b]Pulsing red[/b] means a body part still needs treatment.
[*][b]White[/b] means the wound is currently bandaged or splinted.
[*][b]Sky blue[/b] means a bandaged or splinted body part appears fully healed and the treatment can likely be removed safely.
[*][b]Orange[/b] means the bandage is dirty and should be replaced.
[*][b]Purple[/b] means a stitched wound has likely reached the point where it is worth checking and removing the stitches. In most cases, only a scratch may remain afterward.
[*]If a wound is already bandaged but still pulses, it usually means it is [b]not fully treated yet[/b] — for example: lodged glass, a deep wound, stitches still needed, or another untreated condition.
[/list]

[h2]Muscle Strain[/h2]
Mini Health Plus includes optional support for [b]muscle strain indicators[/b].

The strain display becomes more visible as strain increases and changes color from orange to red depending on severity.

If auto-hide is enabled, the silhouette can briefly reveal itself when a strain threshold is reached. Higher strain levels stay visible longer, and very high strain levels can keep Mini Health Plus visible while attention is still needed.

[h2]Built-in settings[/h2]
Mini Health Plus includes its own detached settings window with options such as:
[list]
[*]Always on top
[*]Always visible
[*]Health bar
[*]Muscle strain display
[*]Window lock
[*]Hover background
[*]Animation speed
[*]Better Character Info avatar on idle, if Better Character Info is installed
[/list]
[img]https://imgur.com/yrkd16r.png[/img]
[quote]BCI is only shown if [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3488600400]Better Character Info[/url] is active.[/quote]
[h2]How to use it[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Left click[/b] opens the vanilla health panel.
[*][b]Right click[/b] opens the Mini Health context menu with available treatment actions and settings.
[*][b]Drag and move[/b] the panel wherever you want on your screen.
[*][b]Gear button[/b] opens the Mini Health Plus settings window.
[/list]

3714025041.title: EBF Chainsaw
3714025041.description:
[h1]EBF Chainsaw[/h1]

[b]Standalone Chainsaw System for Project Zomboid Build 42.20[/b]

This mod adds a standalone and fully functional chainsaw system for Project Zomboid Build 42.20.

The chainsaw can be equipped, started, turned off, refueled, emptied, used as a weapon, and used to cut trees. It has its own fuel system, chain condition system, radial menu support, context menu actions, custom icons, sounds, animations, and multiplayer-focused behavior.

[h2]MAIN FEATURES[/h2]

[list]
[*] Standalone chainsaw item.
[*] Actions to start and turn off the chainsaw.
[*] Fuel system with gasoline capacity.
[*] Add gasoline using a fuel can.
[*] Remove gasoline from the chainsaw.
[*] Chain system with install and remove actions.
[*] Chain wear when cutting trees and attacking zombies.
[*] Broken chains can fall off during use.
[*] The chainsaw can still be started without a chain, but it cannot cut properly or deal full damage.
[*] Custom radial menu using the V key while holding the chainsaw.
[*] Context menu actions with proper icons.
[*] Multiplayer-compatible client-side processing.
[*] Compatible with saves using Authentic Z, while keeping the EBF chainsaw mechanics independent.
[/list]

[h2]CRAFTING[/h2]

The mod includes a manual that teaches the chainsaw recipes:

[list]
[*] Start Chainsaw
[*] Turn Off Chainsaw
[*] Remove Chainsaw Chain
[*] Install Chainsaw Chain
[*] Create Chainsaw Chain
[*] Create Heavy Chain Link
[/list]

You can craft chainsaw chains using metalworking tools and materials.

Chainsaw chain crafting uses welding animations, welding sound, and requires a valid crafting surface.

[h2]GAMEPLAY NOTES[/h2]

[list]
[*] The chainsaw uses gasoline and chain durability separately.
[*] Fuel is consumed during use.
[*] The chain wears down when cutting trees or hitting zombies.
[*] If the chain breaks, it will be automatically removed from the chainsaw.
[*] The chainsaw makes noise while turned on.
[*] The chainsaw becomes even louder when cutting trees.
[/list]

[h2]CHAIN SYSTEM[/h2]

The chainsaw chain is an important part of the system.

[b]Without a chain:[/b]

[list]
[*] The chainsaw can still be started.
[*] It cannot cut trees properly.
[*] It does not deal full damage.
[/list]

3714512452.title: Lifestyle Cleaning Fix - Clean Room Closest Patch
3714512452.description:
[h1]Lifestyle Cleaning Fix - Clean Room Closest Patch[/h1]

This is a tiny [b]Lifestyle Cleaning Fix[/b] compatibility patch for [b]Lifestyle: Hobbies[/b]. It fixes the Clean Room / Do Cleaning tile picker so your character cleans the nearest reachable dirty or bloody tile instead of wandering to whichever reachable tile happened to be scanned last.

[h2]What was wrong?[/h2]

Lifestyle's cleaning helper compares each dirty tile's distance to a variable called [code]lowestdist[/code]. The original logic selected a closer tile, but never updated [code]lowestdist[/code]. That means every reachable candidate kept replacing the previous choice, so the final target was effectively the last reachable dirty tile in the scan order.

[h2]What this patch changes[/h2]

This patch overrides only [code]LSUtil.srqGetClosest[/code] after Lifestyle loads.

[code]
if dist < lowestdist then
    lowestdist = dist
    distchoice = square
end
[/code]

That one missing assignment makes the picker keep the closest reachable square.

[h2]Why use it?[/h2]

[list]
[*] Less weird walking during Clean Room / Do Cleaning.
[*] Cleaning proceeds from nearby messes first.
[*] No balance changes, no item changes, no recipe changes.
[*] Small local Lua override only.
[/list]

[h2]Search terms[/h2]

Also known as a Lifestyle Cleaning Fix, Lifestyle Hobbies cleaning fix, Clean Room fix, Do Cleaning fix, and Project Zomboid B42 cleaning patch.

[h2]Requirements[/h2]

[list]
[*] [b]Lifestyle: Hobbies[/b]
[*] Lifestyle: Hobbies Workshop ID: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3403870858]3403870858[/url]
[*] Project Zomboid Build 42.16+
[/list]

Load this after Lifestyle: Hobbies. The mod declares this dependency automatically.

[h2]Original mod author note[/h2]

This is an unofficial patch for [b]Lifestyle: Hobbies[/b]. Full credit for Lifestyle: Hobbies belongs to its original author, Angry.

This mod does not replace Lifestyle: Hobbies and does not redistribute its assets. It only patches one helper function at runtime.

If the original author wants this patch removed, please contact me and I will take it down. I will also take it down or archive it if the same fix is implemented in the original Lifestyle: Hobbies mod.

[h2]Compatibility[/h2]

Should be compatible with anything that does not also override [code]LSUtil.srqGetClosest[/code] after this mod loads.

[h2]Known Limitations[/h2]

This does not change how Lifestyle detects dirty tiles, consumes cleaning fluid, queues cleaning actions, or handles blocked pathing. It only fixes the nearest-tile selection bug.

3715296334.title: TwisTonFire - Tool Priority
3715296334.description:
[h1]Tool Priority[/h1]
Tool Priority lets you decide which tool should be used first when crafting.
[quote][b]Example:[/b]
Do you really want to use your Multitool for carving your spear or creating planks out of big tree branches?[/quote]
[b]No?[/b]
With this mod you can create your priority list which tool should be used first.

You only need to set up your priorities once. After that, there is no need to open the Tool Priority window again, because your preferences are remembered across sessions.
You only need to open the Tool Priority window again if you want to change the order.
[h2]What this mod does[/h2]
[list]
[*]Adds a [b]Tool Priority[/b] button to the crafting menu.
[*]Shows all reusable tools that can be used for the selected recipe.
[*]Lets you move tools up or down in the list.
[*]Uses the tool at the top of the list first.
[*]Falls back to the next available tool if the preferred one is not available.
[*]Saves your priority order automatically.
[/list]
[h2]Simple example[/h2]
A recipe can use:
[list]
[*]Sharp Stone
[*]Kitchen Knife
[*]Hunting Knife
[*]Multitool
[/list]

If you move [b]Sharp Stone[/b] to the top, the mod will try to use the Sharp Stone first.

If no Sharp Stone is available, it will use the next available tool in your priority list.
[h2]How to use[/h2]
[list]
[*]Open the crafting menu.
[*]Select a recipe.
[*]Click [b]Tool Priority[/b].
[*]Move tools up or down.
[*]Craft as usual.
[/list]
[h2]Notes[/h2]
[list]
[*]This mod only affects reusable crafting tools.
[*]It does not change recipe requirements.
[*]It does not change crafting results.
[*]It does not make unavailable tools usable.
[*]It only changes which valid available tool is preferred first.
[/list]
[h2]Compatibility[/h2]
This mod stays as close to the vanilla crafting system as possible.

[b]Neat Crafting[/b] is supported.

Tool Priority works by changing the preferred tool selection before crafting starts. 
If another mod provides a similar persistent tool priority system, compatibility adjustments may be needed.
[h2]FAQ[/h2]

3717099183.title: Working Knowledge - Lootable Skill Documents
3717099183.description:
That filing cabinet isn't worthless. Somewhere between the expense reports and the insurance forms is a copy of the [i]OSHA 1910 Electrical Safety in the Workplace[/i]. Or an [i]Appalacian Folk Pottery Pamphlet[/i]. Or a [i]Police Academy Handgun Manual[/i].

Working Knowledge adds 372 lootable workplace documents to Project Zomboid — SOPs, reference cards, field guides, training manuals — found in contextually appropriate containers throughout Knox County. Read one, and your character picks up a small amount of practical experience in the relevant skill. Each document can only be read once.

[b]Where to find them:[/b]
Documents turn up rarely in generic filing cabinets and office desks. Dedicated profession containers — police filing cabinets, fire station storage, gun store counters, welding shops, farm tool cabinets, and more — reward targeted searching with higher find rates and more relevant material.

This is the kind of incidental knowledge that was already sitting in these buildings before everything went wrong.

[h2]Configuration[/h2]
Two options are available under [b]Working Knowledge[/b] in the Sandbox settings.

[b]Document Spawn Rate[/b] — Controls how often documents appear in loot containers. Ranges from Very Rare (0.25×) to Abundant (4×); default is Normal. Note that loot is generated when a container is first opened, so changing this setting mid-save only affects areas you haven't visited yet.

[b]XP Grant[/b] — The flat amount of XP awarded when a document is read for the first time. Default is 50. Set to 0 to disable XP entirely while keeping documents as collectibles.

[h2]Languages[/h2]
Localized in English, Simplified Chinese, Russian, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish, and French.

Multiplayer-compatible. Build 42 only.

[url=https://github.com/breweries-wa/pz-working-knowledge]Source on GitHub[/url]

3718906754.title: Sharpenable Glow [B42]
3718906754.description:
[h1]Sharpenable Glow[/h1]
Adds a pulsing golden glow ring around equipped weapons in the left sidebar when they can be sharpened.

No more squinting at item names for "Dull" or "Blunt" — when your blade needs sharpening, you'll see it at a glance.

[hr]
[h2]Notice: All Features Now Also Available in Blade Stat HUD + Gun[/h2]

All three features of this mod (the glow ring on the equipped slots, the yellow dot in the inventory, and the yellow dot on the hotbar) are now also available as options in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3724519253]Blade Stat HUD + Gun[/url] v1.6 by the same author (all default OFF; enable them from the "Sharpenable markers" group in Mod Options).

If you subscribe to both mods, Blade Stat HUD + Gun alone can now give you the same visuals as this mod. Running both together is also safe — no marker is ever drawn twice (this mod's rendering takes priority).

This mod remains fully supported as the lightweight, zero-configuration option: subscribe and it just works.

[hr]
[h2]How It Works[/h2]
[list]
[*] When an equipped weapon's [b]isSharpenable()[/b] condition is true (has sharpness below maximum), a golden glow ring pulses around the weapon slot icon
[*] Works for the primary hand slot
[*] The glow disappears when the weapon is fully sharpened or doesn't have the sharpenable property
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Supported Items[/h2]
All vanilla items with the Sharpness attribute and [b]base:sharpenable[/b] tag — over 70 equippable weapons and tools:
[list]
[*] [b]Knives[/b] — Hunting Knife, Kitchen Knife, Fighting Knife, Fillet Knife, etc.
[*] [b]Axes[/b] — Fire Axe, Hand Axe, Wood Axe
[*] [b]Machetes & Swords[/b] — Machete, Short Sword, Sword
[*] [b]Crafted Weapons[/b] — All spear variants, sawblade bats, scrap weapons
[*] [b]Tools[/b] — Scissors, Scalpel, Straight Razor, Scythe
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Compatibility[/h2]
[list]
[*] Requires: Build 42
[*] Singleplayer and Multiplayer (client-side only)
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Technical Details[/h2]
[list]
[*] Overrides [b]ISEquippedItem.render()[/b] with original function chaining
[*] Uses a pre-generated ring texture tinted gold at runtime
[*] Automatically scales to all sidebar size settings (48–128px)
[*] Minimal performance impact — only checks isSharpenable() per frame
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Update v0.2[/h2]

[h3]Yellow dot in inventory for sharpenable blades[/h3]
[list]
[*] A [b]yellow dot[/b] appears on the bottom-left of sharpenable blade icons in any inventory panel
[*] Drawn over favorite stars and other markers for top priority. When the blade is fully sharpened the dot disappears and the underlying marker is restored
[*] Works in all inventory panels (player, floor, containers, other characters)
[/list]

[h3]Yellow dot on hotbar slots (opt-in)[/h3]
[list]
[*] A yellow dot appears on the top-right of hotbar slots holding a sharpenable blade
[*] Toggled via [b]Options → Mods → Sharpenable Glow[/b] ([b]disabled by default[/b])
[*] Automatically suppressed when [b]Clean HotBar[/b] (Workshop ID:3461263912) is active, since Clean HotBar already renders a sharpness bar
[/list]

[h3]Broken blades are excluded[/h3]
[list]
[*] Vanilla sharpen recipes reject broken items (condition 0) via passesBrokenTest(), so all markers exclude them too
[/list]

[h3]UI coverage extended[/h3]
[list]
[*] The glow ring now also covers the [b]secondary hand slot[/b]
[*] When a stack contains the same item type, only the actually-sharpenable individual rows are marked when expanded
[/list]

[*] [b]Click-to-zoom.[/b] Hover any save thumbnail or Help image and a "+" appears top-right; click the button or the image to open it full-screen, Esc or click outside to close.

[*] [b]Settings screen.[/b] Tabbed panel: thumbnail style (live screenshot or placeholder art), confirm dialogs, Watcher warning toggle, spinner style and size with live preview, HUD position picker (click, drag, 9-point compass, hide), backup directory with reset.

[*] Full keyboard and gamepad navigation. Every screen and dialog works without a mouse. Focus ring, key auto-repeat, right-stick scrolling, gamepad drag for floating panels.

[*] [b]"What's New" popup.[/b] Opens once per release to summarise the changes. It re-enables itself when a new mod version is installed, so future releases always surface their notes even if you previously ticked "Don't show this again".
[/list]

[h1]Recovery and rescue corrupted saves[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Edit Mods.[/b] Checkbox list of every active and installed mod. Pick what stays, what goes, what gets added. Creates a clone with custom mods.txt and a [b]_modded[/b] suffix. Original untouched.

[*] [b]Recovery flags.[/b] One-time fixes applied at the next load: Reset zombies, Reset weather, Reset time of day, Heal player. All stable on B42.

[*] [b]Crash backup.[/b] If the game crashes during a save, the Watcher preserves the partial state in a dedicated [b]_crash_[/b] slot, surfaced on the next main menu.

[*] [b]Save won't load anymore?[/b] Edit Mods handles broken mod dependencies, Recovery Flags handle a broken world state, Crash backup handles unexpected shutdowns. Original save is never overwritten, so you can try combinations safely. Rescues a lot of runs.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/YkYXKtS.png[/img]

[list]
[*] Enable the mod.

[*] Open the folder for your operating system inside the mod ([b]Windows/[/b], [b]Linux/[/b], [b]MacOS/[/b]) and run the launcher inside it: [b]ManualSave_Watcher.cmd[/b] on Windows, [b]ManualSave_Watcher.command[/b] on Linux and macOS. The mod folder lives at Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\108600\3721602150\mods\ManualSaveMod\Windows. A console window stays open in the background, this is required.

[*] In-game: ESC, Save Game, name it, Quick or Full. Or just press shortcuts.
[/list]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/xh1Hu5l.png[/img]

Linux, Steam Deck and macOS are supported in BETA through a new Python launcher and require Python 3 (preinstalled on Ubuntu, SteamOS, Fedora and macOS). 3722760420.description:
Adds Build 42 sandbox settings to make tools last longer. Configure condition wear, drainable tool use, and optional max-condition scaling.

3723127305.title: Nihontō - Authentic Katana Overhaul [B42]
3723127305.description:
[b]2026.08.30 v2.1[/b]
[list]
[*] New sword-care ritual (Te-ire) working on all Nihontō weapons: forage Camellia japonica for its seeds, press them into Chōji oil, then apply the oil with a tissue to a clean, sharpened blade for a temporary, hit-based bonus to condition protection
[*] New "Wipe Blade Clean" action to remove blood before oiling
[*] Custom hand-modeled Camellia japonica plant
[/list]
You can thank (or curse) [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/NoHud]NoHud[/url] for this feature. It was his idea. If you are a Nihontō enthusiast, you might like this feature, otherwise, there is no downside for anyone not wanting to use it.
I did not include the Uchiko ball part, as this would probably be a bit over the top with the realism ... ?

[b]2026.08.18 v2.0[/b]
[list]
[*] Ōdachi and Tantō Saya now spawn in loot (procedural distributions and containers where Katana/Wakizashi Saya already appear)
[*] The Nihontō Tanren-ho and Mall Ninja Monthly now teach the new Ōdachi and Tantō Saya recipes; also cleaned up a stale recipe reference in the Mall Ninja Monthly (the replica scabbard lacquer recipe doesn't actually need to be learned, so this had no gameplay effect)
[/list]

[b]2026.08.18 v1.9[/b]
[list]
[*] Ōdachi now has its own Saya (scabbard) — 15 authentic lacquered variants plus a plain wood/replica version, worn on the back
[*] Tantō now has its own Saya as well — a plain wood/replica version, worn on the hip on the opposite side from the Katana/Wakizashi daishō so it doesn't visually clash
[*] New recipes: craft, lacquer and stain the Ōdachi Saya; craft the Replica Tantō Saya
[*] Translation fixes and additions across all supported languages (CN, DE, ES, JP, PL, PTBR, RU)
[/list]

[b]2026.07.29 v1.7[/b]
[list]
[*] Replica scabbards and Saya can now be carried on the back
[/list]

[h1]The Motivation behind NIHONTŌ[/h1]

I created this mod to address several issues with the vanilla Katana and the Long Blade skill:

[list]
[*] [b]Rarity:[/b] The vanilla Katana is a [i]unicorn[/i] on default settings. It is entirely possible to loot the entire map and never find a single one.
[*] [b]Condition:[/b] Even if you are lucky enough to find one, it has the longevity of a glass ornament. It will break when a zombie looks at it the wrong way.
[*] [b]Repair:[/b] In the vanilla game, you cannot sharpen them.
[*] [b]Crafting:[/b] Vanilla blade crafting feels more like a chore than progression. Welding together scrap swords that break almost instantly or progressing to a master-level blacksmith only to craft slightly better swords didn't feel right.
[*] [b]Lack of Variety:[/b]
[/list]

[h2]Progression & Gameplay[/h2]

What started as a personal fix evolved into a passion project. While the default settings reflect my own preferences, I have added [b]Sandbox Options[/b] to accommodate different playstyles, with more configuration options coming in the future.

In the current version, you can hunt for high-end Katanas for end-game mayhem. However, until you find or forge one, you can hone your skills with [b]lower-tier variants[/b]. These are easier to craft, spawn more frequently in low-tier locations, and bridge the gap in your skill progression.

[h2]Current Weapons & Features[/h2]

[b]A standalone, immersive overhaul for Japanese bladed weapons, specifically designed for Build 42.[/b]

[h3]⚔️ Weapons[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Bokutō[/b] – Hand-carved wooden training sword. Your starting point.
[*] [b]Decorative Katana[/b] – Aluminum wall-hanger. Better than nothing.
[*] [b]Scrap Katana[/b] – Forged from scrap metal. Rough but functional.
[*] [b]Replica Katana & Wakizashi[/b] – Iron blades, Mall Ninja grade. Found in pawn shops and schools.
[*] [b]Nihontō Katana[/b] – Authentic steel. The endgame blade.
[*] [b]Nihontō Wakizashi[/b] – The shorter companion blade.
[*] [b]Tantō[/b] – A compact dagger for close quarters.
[*] [b]Nagamaki[/b] – A long-handled blade/spear hybrid for reach and power.
[*] [b]Ōdachi[/b] – A massive great sword. Slow, devastating.
[/list]

[h3]🗡️ Customization[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Modular Crafting:[/b] Every part – Blade (Tōshin), Guard (Tsuba), Hilt (Tsuka) – is a separate, interchangeable component.
[*] [b]Hilt Colors:[/b] 9 Tsuka color variants for Katana and Wakizashi.
[*] [b]Replica Scabbards:[/b] A single dyeable Saya per weapon – color it any way you like. Every weapon in the mod, including the Tantō, has one.
[*] [b]Authentic Saya:[/b] 15 historically accurate Urushi-lacquered and natural wood Shirasaya variants – now including the Ōdachi.
[*] [b]Custom Assets:[/b] Hand-crafted icons for every component and color variant.
[/list]

[h3]⚙️ Mechanics[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Sharpness System:[/b] Every time the game attempts to decrease a blade's condition, there is a chance to reduce its sharpness instead. A razor-sharp blade protects itself – a dull blade does not. Keep your blade sharp!
[*] [b]Character Feedback:[/b] On-screen warnings when sharpness drops below critical thresholds.
[*] [b]Skill Scaling:[/b] Higher Long Blade and Maintenance skills improve condition protection.
[*] [b]Sandbox Options:[/b] Tune spawn rates, condition values, sharpness mechanics and more. The sharpness mechanic can also be extended to all bladed weapons.
[*] [b]New Literature:[/b] The "Nihontō Tanren-ho" crafting book and the "Mall Ninja Monthly" magazine unlock advanced recipes.
[*] [b]Full Localization:[/b] CN, DE, ES, JP, PL, PTBR and RU.
[/list]

[h2]Cultural Appreciation & Authenticity[/h2]

I have always been deeply inspired by Japanese culture and traditional martial arts. My goal with this mod is to pay tribute to the incredible craftsmanship and heritage of the [b]Nihontō[/b].

I have put a great deal of effort into researching and using [b]authentic historical nomenclature[/b]—from the specific parts of the [i]koshirae[/i] to the distinct eras of swordsmithing—out of deep respect for Japanese traditions. While the "Mall Ninja" items in this mod represent a specific Western pop-culture phenomenon, the Nihontō themselves are intended to be as culturally and historically accurate as possible within the limits of the game.

[h2]Acknowledgments[/h2]

I want to thank [b]Michonne[/b] and [b]Akyohunter[/b] for inspiring me. Before I created this, I used [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2842424482]Michonne's Katana[/url] and [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3668370011]Akyohunter's Legendary Katanas and Wakizashis[/url] extensively. They are great mods, and I highly recommend them if you prefer a simpler way to obtain a Katana or if you aren't interested in my specific sharpness mechanics and obsession with historical accuracy! :D

[i]I hope you enjoy the mod. Please feel free to leave comments regarding bugs or suggestions for improvements.[/i]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Technical Background & Credits[/h2]

Big thanks to Paddlefruit from the official TIS Discord for the awesome Character rig!
When I started this project, I had zero experience with 3D modeling, so this mod is based on a 3D model by [b]mSameja[/b]. Since then, I have learned a lot and reworked almost every aspect of it, but nonetheless, all credit for the original 3D work goes to the artist [b]mSameja[/b].

[*] [b]License:[/b] [url=https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/]CC BY 4.0[/url]
[/list]

[i]Developed by Corvus[/i]

3723654155.title: Come Back Later [B42]
3723654155.description:
[h1]Come Back Later[/h1]

You found a generator you cannot carry.
A crate full of tools you want to loot later.
A car worth coming back for once you have fuel.

Then you leave, survive three more houses, get distracted, and forget exactly where it was.

Or you stop playing for a week, come back to your save, and have no idea which garage had the hammer, which crate had the nails, or where that useful vehicle was parked.

You could mark every hammer, crate, and car manually on the map...
but that gets old fast.

[b]Come Back Later[/b] is a small QoL task list for things you have already found and want to return to later: items, containers, vehicles, and useful world objects like generators, rain collectors, composters, traps, water dispensers, wells, crafting stations, and survival cooking points.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Update - June 2[/h2]
[list]
[*]Added more useful world objects: water dispensers, wells, all rain collectors, composters, crafting stations, and survival cooking points.
[*]World-object entries now show icons in the task list when available.
[*]Picked-up marked items now show an on-character completion message.
[*]Grouped Come Back Later context actions into one submenu for easier muscle memory.
[*]Updated all supported translations.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]What It Does[/h2]
[list]
[*]Mark visible items for later
[*]Mark containers for later, including a snapshot of their contents
[*]Mark vehicles for later
[*]Mark useful world objects for later: generators, rain collectors, composters, traps, water dispensers, wells, crafting stations, and survival cooking points
[*]Review everything in a compact task window
[*]Filter by All / Items / Containers / Vehicles / Objects
[*]Track Todo / Done / Ignored entries
[*]Show how long ago each entry was added, in minutes, hours, or days
[*]Show distance and direction to marked entries, with an option to hide that column
[*]Open the task window from a movable floating interface button
[*]Hide the floating interface button in the mod config
[*]Assign a custom hotkey to open the task window
[*]Show marked things on the world map
[*]Create experimental vanilla map markers only with the separate [b]Mark on map[/b] button
[*]Automatically mark tracked items done when you pick them up into inventory, bags, or hands
[*]Safely persists tasks in player ModData
[*]Includes UI localization for English, French, German, Italian, Spanish, and Russian
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]How To Use[/h2]
[list]
[*]Find an item, container, vehicle, or useful world object you want to return to.
[*]Right-click it, open [b]Come Back Later[/b], and choose:
[list]
[*][b]Mark for later[/b]
[*][b]Mark container for later[/b]
[*][b]Mark vehicle for later[/b]
[*][b]Mark generator / rain collector / composter / trap / water dispenser / well / crafting station / cooking point for later[/b]
[/list]
[*]Open the Come Back Later window from the floating interface button or an assigned keybind.
[*]Use [b]Show on map[/b], [b]Mark on map[/b], [b]Done[/b], [b]Ignore[/b], or [b]Delete[/b] when needed.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Why Use It?[/h2]
Project Zomboid constantly gives you reasons to come back later:

[list]
[*]Too heavy to carry now
[*]Need a car first
[*]Need tools, fuel, bags, or friends
[*]Found a useful container but cannot loot it safely
[*]Spotted a vehicle you want to recover later
[/list]

This mod turns those "I'll remember this" moments into an actual list.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Compatibility[/h2]
This mod is designed to be lightweight and save-friendly.

[list]
[*]No custom items
[*]No custom tiles
[*]No recipes
[*]No vehicles
[*]No custom world objects
[*]No global world data
[*]No required dependencies
[/list]

Tasks are stored only in the player's ModData.

Experimental map markers are ordinary vanilla map symbols created only when you press Mark on map. They may work inconsistently with map/symbol mods. If you remove the mod, those map notes may remain on your map, just like manually placed notes, but they should not break the save.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Singleplayer / Multiplayer[/h2]
Come Back Later is primarily designed for singleplayer.

It can work in multiplayer as a personal reminder list, but it does not reserve loot or protect marked items. Other players can still take, move, destroy, or drive away anything you marked.

In multiplayer, treat it as a private "come back here later" note system, not as a shared claim or ownership system.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Limitations[/h2]
[list]
[*]Does not auto-loot anything
[*]Does not scan hidden containers
[*]Does not reveal unknown loot
[*]Does not reserve or protect marked loot in multiplayer
[*]Not intended as a shared multiplayer team task board in the first release
[/list]

It only remembers things you already found.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Supported Version[/h2]
Project Zomboid Build 42.16-42.99

[hr][/hr]
