3725196303.title: Unwanted Items Collection [B42]
3725196303.description:
[h1]Unwanted Items Collection[/h1]

The [b]Unwanted flag[/b] added in Build 42.12 (right-click an item → More → [i]Mark as Unwanted[/i]) is a useful vanilla feature that grays out marked items in your inventory. On top of that, this mod adds a [b]collection log of items you have picked up, read, or watched[/b]: a new [b]Unwanted tab[/b] in the vanilla [b]Discovered Recipes and Media[/b] window that lists your marked items across four sub-tabs — skill book matrix, magazines, recorded media, and everything else.

[hr]

[h1]Four Sub-Tabs[/h1]

[list]
[*][b]Skill Books[/b] — A matrix of 24 skills × Vol.1–5. Each cell tells you at a glance whether the book is [i]marked[/i], [i]fully read or level-capped[/i], or [i]worth reading right now for an XP boost[/i].
[*][b]Magazines[/b] — Only recipe-teaching magazines ([i]getLearnedRecipes()[/i] non-empty). General magazines and paperbacks fall through to the Other tab.
[*][b]VHS / CD[/b] — Recorded media listed with a category column (VHS / Home VHS / CD).
[*][b]Other[/b] — Everything else: general items (hammers, knives, etc.), procedural literature titles, newspapers, mementos, photographs, and more.
[/list]

[hr]

[h1]Reading the Skill Books Matrix[/h1]

Each cell uses border color and fill to distinguish three states:

[list]
[*][b]White fill + white border[/b] — Marked as Unwanted
[*][b]Green check[/b] — Fully read [i]or[/i] the player's skill already exceeds the book's max trained level (no longer worth reading)
[*][b]Gold 2px border[/b] — [b]Reading this book right now would grant an XP boost[/b] (marked ∧ not fully read ∧ within the useful level range)
[/list]

Rows are grouped per the vanilla skill panel (Survival / Combat / Crafting / etc.); columns are Vol.I–V. The footer shows progress in the form [i]Unwanted: 7 / 120[/i] together with a legend for each symbol.

[hr]

[h1]Skill Progress Mode (Optional)[/h1]

Toggleable via the [b]Show skill progress[/b] checkbox in the bottom-right of the panel (saved per player).

When enabled:
[list]
[*]Skill XP bars are drawn behind the matrix cells (5 columns wide = 10 levels)
[*]Faint blue vertical lines mark each level boundary, making progress easy to read
[*]The column header switches from [i]I II III IV V[/i] (volume) to [i]2 4 6 8 10[/i] (corresponding level)
[*]A label like [i]Lv6 (1234/2400)[/i] appears to the right of each skill name, showing current level and XP progress
[/list]

[hr]

[h1]Other Tab — Vanilla-Style Column Headers[/h1]

[list]
[*][b]Click to toggle sort[/b] — Click again to reverse direction; the current order is shown with ▲ / ▼
[*][b]Drag column header borders to resize columns[/b] — Same behavior as the vanilla [i]ISResizableButton[/i]
[*][b]Long titles are stencil-clipped at the column boundary[/b] — They never spill into the category column (matches vanilla)
[*]Default sort: ascending by category
[/list]

Procedural book titles are shown across three cover variants: [b]Paperback (📘)[/b] / [b]Book (📕)[/b] / [b]both[/b]. A static cover-type map for 1187 titles is extracted from [i]Book.java[/i] and bundled with the mod.

[hr]

[h1]Mark / Unmark from the Panel[/h1]

You can also flip Unwanted flags directly from these panels — no need to go back to your inventory each time:

[list]
[*][b]Right-click a cell in the Skill Books matrix[/b] — Mark or unmark that specific book
[*][b]Right-click an item in Magazines / VHS-CD / Other[/b] — Unmark it (remove from your Unwanted list)
[/list]

This shortcut is opt-in via the [b]Right-click to mark/unmark[/b] checkbox at the bottom of the panel. The setting is shared across all four sub-tabs and saved per player — toggle it on any tab to enable everywhere, toggle off to suppress (useful to avoid accidental clicks).

[hr]

[h1]How to Open[/h1]

[list]
[*]Open the character info window (default key: [b]I[/b]) → [b]Info tab[/b]
[*]Click the [b]Discovered Recipes and Media[/b] button below your avatar
[*]Select the rightmost tab labeled [b]Unwanted[/b] (to the right of Agriculture)
[*]Use the four sub-tabs at the top of the Unwanted panel to switch view
[/list]

No dedicated keybind or standalone window is added. Everything integrates into the existing vanilla UI.

[hr]

[h1]Compatibility[/h1]

[list]
[*][b]Build[/b]: Build 42 (versionMin=42.0.0)
[*][b]Singleplayer[/b]: Tested and confirmed working
[*][b]Multiplayer[/b]: Expected to work as a client-side mod (the Unwanted flag is stored per player in [i]ModData[/i] by vanilla design, so no server-side setup is required)
[*][b]Dependencies[/b]: None — uses vanilla APIs only
[/list]

[hr]

[h1]Limitations[/h1]

[list]
[*][b]Magazines / VHS-CD / Other tabs allow Unmark only[/b] — These tabs list items that are already marked, so right-click can only remove the flag there. To mark a [i]new[/i] item, right-click it in your inventory (More → [i]Mark as Unwanted[/i]) first. The Skill Books matrix is bidirectional because it shows all skill books, marked or not.
[*][b]Titles that exist as both paperback and hardcover[/b] share a single Unwanted flag, since the flag is keyed by [i]literatureTitle[/i] (the title string) in vanilla. Marking one form marks both; the display shows both icons (📘 / 📕).
[*][b]Procedural items in the Other tab[/b] (subjects of photographs, company names on stock certificates, etc.) cannot always be resolved back to a specific source item from their string key alone, so their category may fall back to [i]Memento[/i].
[/list]

3732469752.title: Nimble XP Rebalance
3732469752.description:
[h1]TwisTonFire - Nimble XP Rebalance[/h1]
Usually, I only create quality-of-life mods that do not change core gameplay. 
This is one of the very few balance adjustments I wanted to make, because I believe the vanilla system is simply broken.
[quote]
[h2]What does this mod do?[/h2]
This mod rebalances how Nimble XP is gained.

Instead of relying almost entirely on vanilla's random XP lottery, this mod adds predictable, distance-based Nimble XP while moving in combat stance.

In simple words:
[list]
[*]Move in combat stance.
[*]Actually cover distance.
[*]Gain steady Nimble practice over time.
[*]Nearby zombies increase the XP rate.
[*]Very close zombies give the best XP rate.
[/list]
[/quote]
[quote]
[h2]Why does this mod exist?[/h2]
Vanilla Nimble XP is painfully slow and extremely inconsistent.

In vanilla, Nimble XP is only checked when:
[list]
[*]You are in combat stance / aiming.
[*]You are moving.
[*]You are not in a vehicle.
[/list]
But even if all of that is true, the game does not reward you based on how much you actually moved. It simply rolls the dice.

At normal game speed, the vanilla chance is roughly:
[list]
[*][b]Singleplayer:[/b] 1 chance in 700 per valid movement check.
[*][b]Multiplayer:[/b] 1 chance in 100 per valid movement check.
[/list]
If the roll succeeds, you only get:
[list]
[*][b]+1 base Nimble XP[/b]
[/list]
That +1 base XP is still affected by the usual vanilla learning multipliers from traits, professions, and XP settings.
[quote]Example: 
No multiplier in nimble = [b]0.25 final XP[/b] every 1/700 chance on player movement in aim mode.
[/quote]
The problem is that most valid movement checks still give you nothing. You can move in combat stance for a long time and make no visible progress at all, simply because the hidden XP roll did not succeed.
[/quote]
[quote]
[h2]The problem with vanilla Nimble[/h2]
Nimble is one of the most important long-term combat skills, but without a starting bonus it levels absurdly slowly.

The reason I started looking into this was my own long-term character:
[list]
[*]No Nimble skill bonus.
[*]More than 5 years survived.
[*]Over 1,000,000 zombie kills.
[*]Still only around Nimble level 8.
[/list]
At that point, this no longer felt like difficult progression. It felt like broken progression.

A skill that is used constantly during combat should not feel almost impossible to train naturally.
[/quote]
[quote]
[h2]How this mod changes Nimble XP[/h2]
This mod keeps the idea of Nimble as combat footwork, but makes the progression more logical.

Instead of only asking:
[quote]Did the random XP roll succeed?[/quote]
The mod asks:
[quote]How much did the player actually move in combat stance?[/quote]
XP is based on real movement distance.
[list]
[*]Combat stance movement gives measured Nimble progress.
[*]Zombies nearby increase the XP reward.
[*]Very close zombies count as higher threat and give the best reward.
[*]Teleporting or large position jumps do not grant huge XP.
[*]Singleplayer and Multiplayer are both supported.
[/list]
[/quote]
[quote]
[h2]Sandbox Option[/h2]
This mod intentionally keeps sandbox settings simple.

There is only one admin-facing option:
[list]
[*][b]Require nearby zombie[/b] - If enabled, Nimble XP is only gained while moving in combat stance with a zombie nearby.
[/list]
[/quote]
[quote]
[h2]Multiplayer[/h2]
Multiplayer is supported.

In Multiplayer, the client measures local combat-stance movement, but the server validates the movement before XP is awarded.

This means:
[list]
[*]XP is still handled server-side.
[*]Teleport or lag-spike movement is protected against.
[*]Nearby zombie threat is checked by the server.
[*]The system remains lightweight and performance-friendly.
[/list]
[/quote]
[quote]
[h2]Is this a cheat mod?[/h2]
No.

This mod does not instantly level Nimble.

It does not hand out free XP for standing still.

It simply replaces a frustrating random progression system with a more predictable one based on actual combat-stance movement.

Characters with Nimble-related traits or profession bonuses still benefit from vanilla XP multipliers. Characters without bonuses still learn slower, but they are no longer completely at the mercy of random chance.
[/quote]
[quote]
[h2]Summary[/h2]
[list]
[*]Rebalances Nimble XP gain.
[*]Distance-based combat-stance XP.
[*]Nearby zombie threat bonus.
[*]Works in Singleplayer and Multiplayer.
[*]Server-side XP validation in Multiplayer.
[*]Teleport and large movement jump protection.
[*]Simple sandbox setup.
[*]Designed to make Nimble progression feel fair, not free.
[/list]
[/quote]

[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]
I have been using my mod for quite some time now, and I currently have a long-term character alive with a survival time of 9 months.

My character has a small Nimble bonus from the Gymnast trait, over 150,000 zombie kills, and has reached Nimble level 8.

It feels a hundred times better than the vanilla Nimble roll system. I can honestly recommend this rebalance mod to everyone. It really does feel great.
[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]
[img]https://imgur.com/BaUyxax.png[/img]

3734639991.title: Seed Season Indicator
3734639991.description:
[h1]Seed Season Indicator[/h1]
A mod that overlays markers on seed and seed packet icons in your inventory to indicate the current month's sowing season status. Lets you tell at a glance whether each seed is ready to plant right now.

In vanilla, checking the sowing season requires opening the [b]Info → Discovered Recipes and Media → Agriculture[/b] tab. This mod overlays the indicator directly on seed icons in the inventory, so you can tell whether a seed is plantable right now without opening any other window.

[b]Update (2026-08-31, v1.3.6):[/b] Added an option to show the green star for crops with no Best Month while they are in season (default: OFF).

[hr]
[h2]Marker Types[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Green ★[/b] — Best month ([i]bestMonth[/i]): peak yield period
[*] [b]Green ●[/b] — In season ([i]sowMonth[/i], excluding best/risk): safe to plant
[*] [b]Yellow ●[/b] — Risk month ([i]riskMonth[/i]): plantable, but with a risk of reduced yield
[*] [b]Red ●[/b] — Out of season (outside [i]sowMonth[/i]): cannot plant now
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Display Condition (Vanilla-Compliant)[/h2]
Markers appear only on seeds and seed packets for which you have [b]read the seed packet and learned the corresponding sowing season recipe[/b].

[hr]
[h2]Season Info in the "Category" Column[/h2]
The "Category" column in inventory detail view also shows the season status, and can be sorted by it.
[list]
[*] Display examples: [i]Gardening (Best)[/i] / [i]Gardening (In Season)[/i] / [i]Gardening (Risk)[/i] / [i]Gardening (Out of Season)[/i]
[*] Edible seeds categorized as "Food" — such as "Sunflower Seeds" and "Pumpkin Seeds" — also get the season status, shown as [i]Food (Best)[/i] and so on
[*] Clicking the "Category" column header sorts by [b]Best → In Season → Risk → Out of Season → Unread → Gardening (others)[/b]. Seeds in the "Food" category group together in season order right after the other food items
[*] Useful for bringing "seeds ready to plant right now" to the top of the list
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Season Info in the Tooltip (v1.3)[/h2]
Hovering over a seed or seed packet appends season info to the end of its tooltip.
[list]
[*] [b]This month (July): Out of Season[/b] — the current month's status, color-coded the same as the markers
[*] [b]Planting Season / Best Month / Poor Month[/b] — the list of plantable months, using the same wording as the farming menu
[*] An image of the fully grown crop is shown on the right
[*] Display conditions are the same as the markers (only seeds whose packet you have read; empty seed packets show nothing)
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Options[/h2]
Configure from [b]Options → Mods → Seed Season Indicator[/b].
[list]
[*] [b]Enable Indicator[/b] (default: ON): toggles marker rendering and category column extension
[*] [b]Show season info in tooltip[/b] (default: ON): toggles the tooltip season info
[*] [b]Green star for crops with no Best Month[/b] (default: OFF): crops with no Best Month defined (e.g. Leek, Rosemary) show the green star whenever they are in season, making it obvious at a glance that there is no better month to wait for
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Markers not showing?[/h2]
This mod follows the sandbox setting [i]PlantGrowingSeasons[/i]. If it is disabled, your world has no growing seasons, so [b]all markers are intentionally hidden[/b] (there is no "in/out of season" to show).

[b]In particular, the "Outbreak" difficulty preset[/b] has this [i]PlantGrowingSeasons[/i] setting [b]disabled[/b].

Also note that markers only appear on seeds whose seed packet you have already read (see "Display Condition" above).

[hr]
[h2]Compatibility[/h2]
[list]
[*] Supports: Build 42
[*] Languages: English / Japanese / Russian / French / Korean / Spanish / Brazilian Portuguese (Russian translation provided by HoloBucket, French translation provided by Seijun, Korean translation provided by Hagaren, Spanish translation provided by Salve Sithis, Brazilian Portuguese translation provided by Yhan113)
[*] Standalone — works with vanilla, no additional mods required
[*] When used together with mods that draw "read" markers on seed packets, the markers from both mods may appear side by side on the seed packet icon (no functional impact)
[*] When Show Sowing Season In Seed Tooltip is active, this mod's tooltip section is automatically disabled to avoid duplicate info (markers and the "Category" column keep working)
[*] Not compatible with inventory UI overhaul mods that completely redefine the [i]ISInventoryPane[/i] class (neither marker rendering nor category column extension will function)
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Technical Notes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Wraps [i]ISInventoryPane:renderdetails[/i] to overlay marker textures on seed/seed packet icons via [i]drawTexture[/i]
[*] Wraps [i]ISInventoryPane:refreshContainer[/i] to overwrite the sort key ([i]v.cat[/i]) with custom category keys
[*] Category column display text is replaced via [i]drawText[/i] interception (non-destructive approach, does not call [i]item:setDisplayCategory[/i])
[*] The tooltip section wraps [i]ISToolTipInv:render[/i] and appends rows and the crop image right after the vanilla drawing (temporary [i]DoTooltip[/i] swap, always restored)
[*] Settings are saved via [i]PZAPI.ModOptions[/i] to [i]~/Zomboid/ModOptions.ini[/i]
[/list]

Mod ID: SeedSeasonIndicator

[h1]TwisTonFire - Camping QoL[/h1]

This mod makes setting up and packing away camping gear much easier.

If you have a sleeping bag or tent in your inventory, backpack, or attached to a compatible backpack slot, you can use a simple world context menu option to prepare and place it.

The mod handles the usual steps for you:
detach, move, unpack, and start the vanilla placement cursor.

If no suitable slot is available, the item is placed into your backpack instead.

[h1]What This Mod Simplifies[/h1]

[*]No more manually moving it into your main inventory
[*]No more manually unpacking it before placement

3739595559.title: Water Pipes
3739595559.description:
[h1]🚰 Water Pipes[/h1]

[i]Bring real plumbing to Knox County.[/i]

Project Zomboid lets you hoard water in barrels and pray for rain — but never move it where you need it. [b]Water Pipes[/b] changes that: lay a real pipe network through your base and let water (and other liquids) flow exactly where you want it.

[h2]🔧 What you can do[/h2]
[list]
[*]🧩 [b]Build a pipe network[/b] across floors and walls — pipes snap together into straights, corners, junctions and crossings. [b]Go vertical[/b]: run pipes up walls so rooftop rain collectors feed the kitchen below. Short on metal? A [b]fired clay pipe segment[/b] builds the same pipe — dismantling gives a metal pipe back, but clay is spent for good.
[*]💧 [b]Share your water.[/b] Barrels and rain collectors join the network as one shared supply.
[*]🚰 [b]Plumb your fixtures.[/b] Sinks, showers, toilets and even washing machines pull straight from your network — no more hauling water bottles.
[*]🧱 [b]Hide your plumbing.[/b] Concealed pipes work exactly like normal ones but are invisible once placed. Built with a bucket of cement, revealed any time with [b]Show pipe network[/b].
[*]⛽ [b]Pump any liquid.[/b] Pipe petrol to your generator and keep it topped up automatically; your taps serve whatever the network holds — and with the default Realistic Purification setting, dirty water stays dirty until it passes a purifier.
[*]🔀 [b]Direct the flow[/b] with [b]Fluid Routers[/b] — one-way valves: in through the [b]green band (IN)[/b], out through the [b]red band (OUT)[/b], never back, capped at the pressure ceiling you set. A router [b]empties[/b] the network behind it into the one in front at a rate set by the pressure reaching it, and several fed from one tank take turns. Put a vessel on the router's tile and the two sides exchange only through it — that is how the purifier works. Rotate with [b]R[/b].
[*]🧪 [b]Purify tainted water[/b] with the [b]Electric Water Purifier[/b] — a powered tank that turns dirty water clean as it flows through.
[*]⛏️ [b]Pull water from wherever it is.[/b] An [b]Electric Water Pump[/b] beside a [b]well[/b] or on a [b]river bank[/b] feeds your network non-stop: wells give clean water, rivers give dirty water for the purifier. It sucks from a couple of floors down at most, so place it low, and right-click it to switch it on or off.
[*]🌊 [b]Pressure matters, and it is shared.[/b] Height, distance and pumps decide what reaches each tap, and every consumer is charged for what its neighbours draw — so a long row of sprinklers starves its own far end. Chained pumps add up and a [b]Pressure Gauge[/b] reads any point; the sandbox offers [b]Simple[/b] and [b]Off[/b] modes too.
[*]🌱 [b]Irrigate your crops.[/b] A [b]Drip Emitter[/b] waters its own tile and barely sips; a [b]Sprinkler[/b] blankets its 3x3 but needs pump pressure, pays for all nine tiles whether or not anything grows, and is loud. Both spend water whenever they run — pick your trade. Mind the pressure: too much [b]bursts a drip[/b] (the sprinkler shrugs it off) — cap its line with a router, and patch a burst one with duct tape (right-click → Repair).
[*]🚒 [b]Tap the town water.[/b] Open a [b]fire hydrant[/b] with a wrench for clean, pressurised water until the day the mains is cut — and its gush waters any crops in its own 3x3. Running water, from a hydrant or a sprinkler, soaks whoever stands in it.
[*]⏳ [b]Water goes stale.[/b] Standing water turns contaminated over time and rain spoils uncovered water — keep it moving or purify it. Fully tunable, and optional.
[/list]

[h2]🧰 How to use it[/h2]
[list]
[*]🔧 Grab a [b]Pipe Wrench[/b] and some [b]Pipes[/b]. The [b]Pump[/b] and [b]Purifier[/b] also need welding gear (blowtorch and rods) plus some [b]Electricity[/b] and [b]Metal Welding[/b] skill; the emitters need a little [b]Farming[/b]. Short on pipes? [b]Forge your own[/b] at a forge from iron bar stock, or [b]fire clay pipe segments[/b] in a kiln — cheap and no forge needed, but clay is spent for good and gives nothing back when dismantled.
[*]🏗️ Build menu → [b]Piping[/b] category. Floor pipes route the network; the [b]vertical pipe[/b] climbs between floors.
[*]🪛 With the wrench in hand, [b]plumb[/b] a sink or [b]connect[/b] a generator from its right-click menu.
[*]🔍 [b]Right-click any pipe → Show pipe network[/b] lights it all up: pipes red, sources green, taps and generators blue.
[*]♻️ [b]Dismantle[/b] pipes to recover your materials. The pump and the purifier come apart too, with a blowtorch and a welding mask.
[/list]

[h2]🧪 Electric Water Purifier[/h2]
[list]
[*]⚡ Build the 2x2 tank on a [b]Fluid Router[/b]. While powered it takes tainted water in the router's [b]green[/b] side and sends it out the [b]red[/b] one, clean.
[*]🪣 Runs on a charcoal-and-cloth filter that wears with use: [b]right-click → Repair filter[/b] with charcoal and ripped sheets. Wear is tunable (or off) in sandbox options.
[*]📊 [b]Right-click → Open Purifier[/b] to read it live: levels, power, filtering rate and filter condition.
[/list]

[h2]💡 Tips from the plumber[/h2]
[list]
[*]🏺 [b]Give your water somewhere to live.[/b] Pumps push water IN, but barrels, amphoras and tanks HOLD it. Don't pipe a river pump straight into a sink — put a container or two on the line and let the taps drink from those.
[/list]

[h2]✅ Good to know[/h2]
👥 [b]Multiplayer ready[/b] · 🌍 English, Spanish and Simplified Chinese · 🧱 Designed for [b]Build 42[/b].

[h2]🧩 Tested with other mods[/h2]
🛁 [b]Take A Bath And Shower[/b] — full integration: its bathtubs and showers plumb into the network like any vanilla fixture. Tried another mod alongside? Tell me in the comments and I'll add it here.

[h2]🤝 Collaborations[/h2]
🎨 Tileset and sprite art by [b]aariak_einherjer[/b] — [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/aariak_einherjer/]Steam[/url] · [url=https://www.artstation.com/adrianechanizrol]ArtStation[/url]. 🇨🇳 Simplified Chinese by [b]rakkasumi[/b]. Thank you both! If you draw, translate or have ideas worth trying, get in touch right here — there is still room.

[h2]⚠️ Updating from an earlier version[/h2]
[b]Pressure is now shared along a pipe[/b], so a farm built before v0.9.0 can stop watering: a long row of sprinklers starves its own far end. Nothing is lost or corrupted — the emitters still work, their neighbours are simply out-drawing them.
Fix it by splitting the run into zones with [b]Fluid Routers[/b], which needs no setting changed — or by lowering [b]Shared-pipe demand[/b] in the sandbox, where [b]0[/b] restores the old behaviour exactly. [b]Right-click an emitter that is not watering[/b] and it names the problem and the pressure it lacks.
The mod also tidies an old plumbing record on first load. If a sink, shower or tub acts oddly afterwards, unplumb and plumb it again.

[h2]⚠️ Before you remove the mod[/h2]
Like most Build 42 buildable mods, removing this from an [b]existing save[/b] can trigger a [b]"WorldDictionary"[/b] load error. Fixable — follow [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3187340365]this guide[/url] — and always [b]back up your save[/b] before adding or removing mods.

3739612285.title: Braven's Camouflage Reworked
3739612285.description:
[h1][b]Zombie camouflage[/b][/h1]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2981216690]BitBraven's camouflage mod[/url] always felt like a mechanic that belonged in the vanilla zombie apocalypse experience, and now it returns to Project Zomboid Build 42 in a much more immersive and balanced form.

Grab your frying pan, smash a zombie's skull, and blend into the horde.

[img=https://i.imgur.com/r2rtgOZ.gif][/img]
[quote]
[h2]How does it work?[/h2]

Right-click a zombie corpse and select "Use Camouflage". Your character will gather the zombie's entrails and cover themselves with them to conceal their scent and appearance.

Once applied, the camouflage lasts for a limited time and makes it harder for zombies to identify you. However, the process is exhausting: your character will become slightly fatigued and nauseous—just as anyone would. Needless to say, they'll also be covered in blood and begin to walk like the undead.

[b]But be careful:[/b] if you get too close to them, they'll start to suspect that you're not one of their own. And if you stay there for too long or one of them manages to touch you, they'll quickly realize there's fresh meat hiding beneath those rotten guts!
[/quote]

[quote]
[h2]New Features[/h2]

💠 You now [b]walk like the undead[/b] while camouflaged.
A configurable hotkey can be assigned in the mod options to toggle this animation.

💠 [b]Reworked zombie detection system:[/b]
[list]
[*] Zombies no longer stand around staring blankly at the player.
[*] They now build suspicion over time when you stay too close to them.
[*] Their behavior feels much more natural and immersive, simulating them tracking the player's scent.
[/list]
For players who prefer the original behavior, it can be restored through the Sandbox options.

💠 [b]New sniffing animation:[/b] Zombies will sniff the player when they start becoming suspicious. Walk away when you see it.

💠 [b]Camouflage can deteriorate[/b] if you run or climb wallks within a zombie's line of sight. These actions attract too much attention and reduce the effectiveness of your disguise. Needless to say, zombies don't talk.

💠 You can [b]remove the camouflage[/b] by washing your clothes or yourself.

💠 Now compatible with mods like [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2956146279]Rain Cleans Blood[/url].
[/quote]

[quote]
[h2]F.A.Q.[/h2]

[h3]Does it work in multiplayer?[/h3]
🛑 Use in multiplayer at your own risk. This update is for SP.

[h3]Does it work with existing saves?[/h3]
Absolutely!

[h3]Is the mod compatible with [...]?[/h3]
This mod shouldn't have any incompatibilities with other mods, but if you find one, please let me know.

🔴 If you are using the mod [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3396867685]Starving Zombies[/url] and the zombies feel too aggresive, disable the Sandbox option "Zombies can smell player". 
[/quote]

[h1]So[/h1]
Camouflage remains a useful tool for confusing zombies, but it no longer guarantees complete safety. If you stay too close to them or perform suspicious actions, they'll eventually figure out that you're still alive.

Use it wisely... or end up becoming part of the horde.

[quote]
[h1]Recommended mods[/h1]
If you want blood to fade when it rains, you would use a mod like this one, which will affect your camouflage!

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2956146279][img]https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/16590947677681455242/0492039769B26BAD08ED7B90FFE045EF00DBDF98/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false[/img][/url]
[/quote]

Updated and reworked by 1Vita.

3740052292.title: Companion Dogs [ALPHA]
3740052292.description:
[h1]Companion Dogs [ALPHA][/h1]
Adopt a stray. Feed it, earn its trust, and you end up with a dog that follows you around, warns you about things you cannot see and throws itself at zombies for you. It also has to eat every day, and it can die.

[b]ALPHA[/b], meaning playable and stable but still growing, and new features can bring new bugs. Five breeds in this base mod: [b]Caramelo[/b], [b]German Shepherd[/b], [b]Golden Retriever[/b], [b]Border Collie[/b] and [b]Husky[/b]. They breed and raise puppies too.

[table]
[tr][th]Which version does it run on?[/th][td]Build 42.19 up[/td][/tr]
[tr][th]Can I add it to a save or a server already running?[/th][td]Yes. Dogs spawn in areas you have already explored[/td][/tr]
[tr][th]Does it work on servers?[/th][td]Yes, dedicated and co-op[/td][/tr]
[tr][th]Which languages?[/th][td]Fourteen, listed at the end of this description[/td][/tr]
[tr][th]How many breeds are there?[/th][td]Five in the base mod (listed above), seven in the official collection (linked above), and plenty more made by the community: search the Workshop for [b]CD[/b] or [b]Companion Dogs[/b][/td][/tr]
[tr][th]Can my dog die?[/th][td]Only from hunger. The big vet care update will add death from illness and wounds, and it comes switched off by default in the sandbox[/td][/tr]
[tr][th]Can I have more than one dog following me?[/th][td]Not today. An update to improve this is on the roadmap[/td][/tr]
[tr][th]Will it keep getting updates?[/th][td]Yes. The roadmap is long, and it stays in alpha/beta for a few more months[/td][/tr]
[/table]

[h3]Known issue: dog looks crumpled / has no texture[/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/MDKelzn.png[/img]
[b]Fix:[/b] enable Companion Dogs in the [b]main-menu Mods list[/b], then [b]fully restart the game[/b] before loading your save. Co-op hosts must do the same and restart the server.

[h1]Removing the mod? Read first[/h1]
[b][url=https://companiondogs.pet/docs/en/features.html#23-removing-the-mod-from-a-save-read-this-first]>> Full removal guide <<[/url][/b]

[h1]What your dog does[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Commands[/b] from the radial, the paw menu or right-click, and you can bind hotkeys in Paw menu > Settings
[*][b]Sniff out zombies[/b] in four steps that tell you how close they are, though the loudest alert can pull zombies in
[*][b]Combat[/b] that knocks zombies down, or kills them outright with anything but the small breeds
[*][b]Hunting[/b] that starts at insects and works its way up to deer as the skill grows
[*][b]Saddlebags[/b] for extra cargo
[*][b]Livestock care[/b] that keeps your herd calm while you are away, herds the birds in and shuts the coop at night
[*][b]Needs, loyalty and a companion moodle[/b] per breed
[*][b]Five skills with XP[/b] and inborn trait genes
[*][b]Obedience tricks[/b]: walk to a tile, distract, sniff out an item, fetch it
[*][b]Breeding and puppies[/b]
[*][b]Rides with you[/b] in any vehicle
[*][b]Dogs left at home[/b] wander, nap, sniff and stretch their legs instead of standing frozen
[*][b]A management window[/b] for all of it
[/list]
[b][url=https://companiondogs.pet/docs/en/features.html]>> All the details in the wiki <<[/url][/b]

[h1]Roadmap: coming in Beta[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]More breeds & rarity.[/b] Additional breeds, each with its own traits and skill-XP boosts. Genes scale with rarity: the Caramelo is humble, rarer breeds are born stronger.
[*][b]Vet care.[/b] Wounds, infections, bleeding, and veterinary meds to patch your dog back up.
[*][b]Art & audio polish.[/b] Custom icons, refined skins, new breed models, and better dog sounds.
[/list]

[h1]Credits[/h1]
Animations derived from Quaternius "Ultimate Animated Animals" (CC0). Dog sounds from BigSoundBank / Joseph Sardin (CC0). Custom dog model, skeleton & skinning by the author.

[h1]Translations[/h1]
Fourteen languages so far, English and Portugues (Brasil) by the author and the rest by players who volunteered.
Chinese (简体/繁體中文) by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/duwenju1203/]duwenju1203[/url]. Italian (Italiano) by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/d4rk83]d4rk83[/url]. Japanese (日本語) and Spanish (Español) by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198253359995/]一匹狼[/url]. Thai (ไทย) by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/momineko/]momineko[/url]. Russian (Русский) by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561199176671433/]Jackson WalWhite[/url] and [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561199611785440/]MechJeb2[/url], who also did Ukrainian (Українська). Korean (한국어) by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561199122771464/]Hagaren[/url]. Vietnamese (Tiếng Việt) by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/huuhoa43/]huuhoa43[/url]. German (Deutsch) by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Katinka1988/]Katinka1988[/url]. French (Français) by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/ttmmkk/]lordtmk[/url].

[h1]Asset usage[/h1]
Feel free to build add-ons and new breeds for Companion Dogs, and to use the mod's art in them, just give proper credit :D
For anything outside that, [b]please do not extract, repackage or redistribute the mod's content in unrelated projects without our explicit permission.[/b]

[h1]Support[/h1]
If you enjoy the mod, you can buy me a coffee. Thank you!
[url=https://ko-fi.com/M8F72123UE][img]https://storage.ko-fi.com/cdn/kofi6.png?v=6[/img][/url]

[h2]Question about how a mechanic or a breed works? READ THE WIKI BEFORE ASKING.[/h2]
Every feature, every breed and every sandbox option is documented there, so the answer you are looking for is very likely already written down.
[b][url=https://companiondogs.pet/docs/index.html]>> Companion Dogs Wiki <<[/url][/b]

Come to the Discord to report bugs, suggest breeds, get help or just show off your dog:

3741334453.title: New Hartburg
3741334453.description:
[h1] New Hartburg, KY [/h1]

This mod adds the village of New Hartburg to the standard map.

New Hartburg is located west of Rosewood on the main highway.

If one day you travel west from Rosewood, you will definitely pass by an inconspicuous village called New Hartburg. From the founding of the village until recently, the traditional activity of the settlers was hunting. But after the furniture company "Krypton furniture" built its factory, some of the residents left their job  and retrained as factory workers. Of course, the factory is too large to rely on the strength of local residents, so a workers' village was built south of the plant with similar houses, which were inhabited by people from all over Knox County.

Despite the progress, hunters remained in New Hartburg, devoted to the traditions of their ancestors. Therefore, in the village you can buy yourself a brand new rifle at the local gun store.

New Hartburg - progress and traditions!


This mod is an update to the classic Hartburg map. As time goes on, the vanilla style of settlements in Project Zomboid changes, becoming more detailed, as can be seen in the example of Muldraugh. So I decided to update Hartburg to the new vanilla style, making New Hartburg, unlike its predecessor, not just a settlement made up of previously completed but unused buildings in Pineville and Constown, but a full-fledged village with its own stylistic features and its own logic for the placement of key points of interest.
New buildings have been added, the furniture factory area has been completely updated, the distances between points of interest have been increased, and more farmland has been added, typical of a rural area.

[h2] The village is divided into 4 areas: [/h2]
[list]
    [*]Residential area with gas station, diner, bookstore, post office, laundry and police station.
    [*]Farms.
    [*]Factory "Krypton Furniture".
    [*]A forest area with a shooting range, a lake, and a ranger base.
[/list]

[h2] Village Location: [/h2]

New Hartburg is located west of Rosewood on the main highway.

[h2] Description: [/h2]

All custom tiles are hand-drawn by me, so if anything doesn't work exactly as expected, I apologize. Enjoy the game!

New Hartburg is located between Rosewood and Constown, so it fits perfectly with the second town.

[h2] The map uses cells: [/h2]
(24x42);(25x42);(26x42);(27x42);(28x42);

Whether you're surviving solo or hosting a multiplayer server, these sirens are completely synced and highly customizable.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]A Note From Jim[/h2]
This took a ton of effort and learning. It uses some newer features in the PZ API so if you come across a bug or an error, please report it along with the version of PZ you are running and if it is SP or MP.

Cheers!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Animated 3D Model:[/b] Watch the siren spin as it sounds the alarm!
[*][b]Realistic Audio:[/b] Authentic sound effects featuring a windup, a looping wail and a winddown phase.
[*][b]Automatic Map Placement:[/b] Spawns naturally across the map the moment you load into the world. It uses built-in locations by default, but you can easily drop in your own custom coordinate list!
[*][b]Completely Indestructible:[/b] These can't be dismantled, picked up or smashed with a sledgehammer.
[*][b]Grid & Battery Powered:[/b] You can configure the sirens to only work while the power grid is alive, complete with a customizable battery-backup window for when the power inevitably shuts off.
[*][b]Dynamic Weather Triggers:[/b] Set a custom probability for the sirens to automatically blare when a severe thunderstorm hits.
[*][b]Zombies Love Them:[/b] A running siren will draw the undead from miles away. (The exact radius is totally up to you!)
[*][b]Multiplayer Ready:[/b] Built from the ground up for servers.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]How It Works[/h2]
Just [b]right-click the base of the sirens pole[/b] to pull up the [i]Civil Defense Sirens[/i] menu:
[list]
[*][b]Activate / Stop:[/b] Manually start or silence a specific siren.
[*][b]Activate All / Stop All:[/b] (Admin only) Sound the sirens globally!
[*][b]Add Siren / Remove Siren:[/b] (Admin only) Custom-placed sirens will stick around even after server restarts.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Nerd Stuff[/h2]
[list]
[*]Uses PZ's Global Objects System instead of hand-holding objects through modData. It allows us to place persistent objects outside of loaded chunks.
[*]Uses PZ's "spriteModel" System, the same one that drives animated doors and curtains. 
[/list]

[b]Playing Single-player?[/b] To mess with the sirens, you'll need a specific electrical skill level (default is 6, but you can change this in the sandbox settings). Admin commands like Add/Remove/All are unlocked if you boot up in debug mode.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Multiplayer Permissions[/h2]
Want to control who gets to press the big red button? Access is fully handled through sandbox options and completely supports [b]custom roles[/b] - just type in the role name.

[table]
[tr]
[th]Setting[/th]
[th]What it does[/th]
[/tr]
[tr]
[td]Who can control sirens[/td]
[td]Choose between specific Listed Roles, Everyone, or Players with a high enough electrical skill.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
[td]Control roles[/td]
[td]Which roles are allowed to start or stop a local siren (Default: admin).[/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
[td]Admin roles[/td]
[td]Which roles can add/remove sirens and trigger the global start/stop commands (Default: admin).[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]
[hr][/hr]

[h2]Sandbox Options[/h2]
Tailor the mod exactly to your server's needs:
[list]
[*][b]Placement:[/b] Toggle auto-placement of the built-in sirens, and add any coordinates of your own. The two stack: with auto-placement on, your extra locations are placed alongside the built-in list; turn it off to place only your own.
[*][b]Permissions:[/b] Set who can control sirens, define control/admin roles, and tweak the required Electrical skill level.
[*][b]Power Settings:[/b] Toggle power requirements and adjust the battery backup lifespan (in months).
[*][b]Events:[/b] Adjust the severe weather trigger chance (%).
[*][b]Zombie Attraction:[/b] Tweak the zombie attraction radius and how long the siren runs (in real seconds).
[*][b]Siren Run Time:[/b] How long the siren runs in real seconds.
[*][b]Wake sleeping players[/b]: a siren sounding within earshot can jolt sleepers awake, within a radius you choose. The [b]Deaf[/b] never hear it, the [b]Hard of Hearing[/b] only at half range, and the more exhausted a sleeper is, the closer the siren has to be.
[*][b]Scheduled siren tests[/b]: sound every siren on a routine: daily, weekly (on Wednesday), twice monthly (1st & 15th), or monthly (on the first Wednesday), at an hour you set. Optionally run the test [i]without[/i] drawing zombies.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[i]All sandbox-configurable and off by default, so existing saves and servers are untouched until you opt in.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]For Server Owners & Modders[/h2]
Want to trigger sirens using your own custom server events? Just drop a Lua script into your [i]media/lua/server/[/i] folder. Here's a quick example of making them go off every day at 6:00 AM:

[code]
if isClient() then return end

require "CivilDefenseSiren/SSirenSystem"

local function onEveryHours()
    local sirens = SSirenSystem.instance
    if not sirens then return end
    
    -- Triggers the alarm at 6 AM
    if getGameTime():getHour() == 6 then
        sirens:startAll()   -- You can also use: startAll(runSeconds, radius, volume)
    end
end

Events.EveryHours.Add(onEveryHours)
[/code]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Add-On Mods[/h2]
Basic code to create an addon mod that places sirens at x,y coords.
[list]
[*]Replace the coordinates with your own { x, y } coords
[*]suppressDefaults = true hides the base mod built-in sirens so ONLY the
ones specified are placed! 
[*]Remove that option or set it false to add yours TO the built-in list instead
[code]
require "CivilDefenseSiren/jb_SirenConfig"

CivilDefenseSiren.registerSirens({
    { 6543, 5210 },
    { 6710, 5388 },
    { 6822, 5104 },
}, { suppressDefaults = true }) -- or false to keep default sirens
[/code]

[b]Other handy functions include:[/b] [b]startAt(x, y, 0)[/b], [b]stopAll()[/b], and [b]stopAt(x, y, 0)[/b].
[i]Note: Scripted triggers respect your sandbox power settings and will only affect sirens that are already placed in the world.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Safe to add mid-save![/h2]
Yes, it is completely safe to add this to an existing, running server. All siren states are managed by the server and pushed to clients. This means whether someone logs in late or the server reboots, the alarms will stay perfectly in sync.

[hr][/hr]
[b]Reworked texture and model by Some_stranger. [/b]

[hr][/hr]

3761077099.description:
[h1][B42] Vanilla Firearms Expansion [CLASSIC][/h1][b]A Build 42 port of the classic Vanilla Firearms Expansion.[/b] This is not a new mod. It is a Build 42 fork of the original [i]Vanilla Firearms Expansion[/i] by Vilespring, Stendo_Clip and Spuchel - all models, textures, icons, sounds and design are their work. The original is a Build 41 mod and work on it is ongoing; this fork just brings it to Build 42. One of the original authors, Stendo_Clip, has passed away. This fork keeps the mod running.

[h1]What you get[/h1][list][*]Around 40 firearms in vanilla's art style - pistols, revolvers, SMGs, rifles, shotguns and machine guns, with their own models, textures, icons, sounds and animations.[*]Attachments that fit the weapon they belong on: optics, bipods, slings, recoil pads, choke tubes, ammo straps and coupled magazines.[*]Additional calibres alongside vanilla's, with magazines, boxes and cartons for each.[*]Folding stocks, bayonets, weapon lights and alternate weapon models.[*]Craftable ammunition packing, integrated with vanilla's own recipes rather than sitting beside them.[/list]

[h1]Loot[/h1]Firearms are placed by rarity tier rather than scattered evenly. Common weapons turn up in houses, cars and pawn shops; rare ones concentrate in police and military locations. Container density is tuned per location type, so a gun store feels like a gun store and a bedroom drawer does not.

Sandbox options control the overall rate and each location group separately. Vanilla firearms can optionally be pulled from VFE's loot tables if you want the mod's weapons to carry the game.

[h1]Admin configuration[/h1]An in-game panel for per-weapon and per-class tuning: damage, fire rate, jamming, reload speed, range, loot density and rounds per ammo box. Changes apply live and sync to connected clients. Loot changes take effect on the next server restart.

[h1]Multiplayer[/h1]Built and tested on a dedicated PvP server. Server-authoritative where it matters.

[h1]CD: Rottweiler[/h1]
[b]Rottweilers for Companion Dogs[/b] - the first optional breed add-on for [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3740052292]Companion Dogs[/url].
Built for [b]Build 42 (42.19+)[/b]. Works in [b]singleplayer, co-op AND dedicated servers[/b], and is [b]safe to add to existing saves[/b].

[b]REQUIRES the base mod [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3740052292]Companion Dogs[/url] (0.6.3 or newer).[/b] Subscribe to it as well, enable both mods in the main-menu Mods list, and fully restart the game (this loads the dog model correctly - same as the base mod).

[h1]The dog[/h1]
A [b]combat-category dog[/b]. The Rottweiler is a powerful guard dog bred for protection work: broad-chested, black-and-tan, and utterly fearless. As a companion it is a true warrior on par with the German Shepherd - same lethality, same fast Combat learning - but with its own look, its own temper, and its own way of making you stronger.

[h1]Benefits[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Full combat breed[/b] - learns Combat twice as fast, hits hard at high skill, knocks zombies down, and keeps fighting where most breeds panic.
[*][b]Front Line moodle[/b] - unique to the Rottweiler. Its icon shows whenever a fed, loyal Rottweiler is at your side. While that dog is actually [b]engaged in combat[/b] near you, every [b]melee[/b] swing you make [b]refunds about 35% of the endurance it cost[/b] - fighting shoulder to shoulder keeps your wind. Melee only (no benefit from firearms), and it needs a cared-for dog: a starving or disloyal Rottweiler gives nothing.
[*][b]Industrial guard dog[/b] - stray Rottweilers guard warehouses, factories, storage yards and junkyards, with a rare chance in residential homes. Roughly a [b]10% chance per industrial building[/b] and about [b]a quarter of the stray rate in homes[/b] (both scale with the sandbox Animal/Dog spawn multiplier). Tame one the usual way: feed it until it trusts you.
[*][b]Everything from the base mod[/b] - Follow/Stay/Guard, sentinel alerts, hunting, saddlebags, needs & loyalty, skills & genetics, and breeding (cross-breed litters with the other breeds included).
[/list]

[h3]Warning - removing the add-on[/h3]
Do NOT remove this add-on from a save that has living Rottweilers: the game engine discards animals of unknown types. Your other dogs and the base mod are unaffected.

3763470184.title: Propane Exchange Cabinets
3763470184.description:
Adds branded propane tank exchange cabinets (Fossoil, DirectFlame, Zippee's) that spawn at gas stations and Zippee's convenience stores.  Stable42.20 confirmed working.

Each cabinet is a lootable container stocked with 0-6 propane tanks, weighted toward either near-full or near-empty (never a middle fill level) - similar to gas-grill tank odds, but fuller.

Sandbox options let you tune spawn chance, max tanks per cabinet, and fill-level weighting & if you want only weathered cabinets or a mixture of old and new (default behavior) to spawn.

Can be added mid-save - spawn adjusted, will check all areas when entered (even previously visited) to determine if cabinet spawn check is run - (note: for busy multi-player servers this may appear to not be working in heavy traveled areas because the scripts only run when a  chunk cycles out and back).

[H3]Warning about Removal[/h3]
Once any propane cabinets have been added to the world (this is the same for any mod that adds custom placed objects) you can't remove the mod without first removing all the placed instances of the object. Otherwise you will get errors.  I have added some scripts to help automate some of this process, please see the Discussion topic regarding mod removal instructions.  Multi-player removal is especially dangerous.

Updated Feature List:
Propane cabinets can now be picked up and rotated in all directions. I also moved the default container size to be 100 from 50, seemed appropriate given it takes up the same vertical space as two stacked crates.
The cabinet's model now reflects what's actually inside it - stocked cabinets show tanks on the shelves, empty ones show bare shelves, and it updates live as you loot (whether you click it, right-click it, or just walk past with your inventory open). Also gave it its own icon and "Propane Cabinet" tooltip in the inventory panel instead of the generic "Crate" one.
Adds several new rural locations as possible spawn points (Echo Creek garden center).
Build 42 Only: Adds craftable unbranded model to game, requires recipe from new Special edition welding magazine - currently a 25% drop chance per propane cabinet, once per save. The drop percentage and whether more than 1 magazine can drop per save is configurable in sandbox options.
Build 41 : Version is now live and tested. The Propane cabinet spawns work, however the craft option has been removed for build 41 (larger changes would have been required).

Multi-player:  42 Multi-Player should now be working.  41 Multi-Player "may" be working, but I haven't had the time to test, if someone else does, let me know. Thanks!

3767639280.title: [B42.20] Item Arrange
3767639280.description:
[h1]Item Arrange[/h1]
[b]V2.9. Build 42.20. Single player and Multi Player[/b]

[table]
[tr]
[td]
[h1]
[list]
[*]Works in SP & MP
[*] Hold shift key while dragging items from your inventory to a neighboring ground tile to have them arranged.
[*] items will be arranged on the floor as well as on surfaces of the furniture.
[*] Not every item and every furniture works yet
[/list][/h1]
[/td]

[h2]What does this mod do?[/h2]
This mod changes how items are placed when dropped on the ground, tables, shelves, countertops, and other surfaces. Instead of being scattered randomly, items are arranged in an orderly and visually pleasing way.

The result is a cleaner-looking world that's both more practical and more immersive.

[h2]Why is this interesting?[/h2]
[list]
[*]More practical – No more messy piles. Items are easier to find and organize.
[*]Better looking – Project Zomboid's 3D item models look great, and displaying them neatly opens up many new decoration possibilities.
[*]More realistic – The number of items that can be placed on a surface is no longer limited by the container's weight capacity, but by the actual space the items occupy.
[/list]
[h2]How to use the mod
HOLD SHIFT KEY WHEN DROPPING ITEMS
[/h2]
Items are arranged automatically when you drop them from your inventory.

Simply drag the items holding shift keY onto the desired surface before releasing it. You can place items on the ground beneath your character or on any adjacent surface, such as tables, shelves, and countertops. [b]Just drag them to the ground of the current tile or adjacent tile. [/b]

[h2]Donations / Payments / Gifts[/h2]
[url=/ko-fi.com/M4M7SGR4P][img]https://storage.ko-fi.com/cdn/brandasset/kofi_bg_tag_dark.png[/img][/url]

[h2]Limitations[/h2]
[list]
[*]Not every item can be arranged. Currently, only items with simple, regular shapes (such as boxes or cylinders) are supported.
[*]Not every surface is supported yet. Each surface must be configured manually, which is a time-consuming process. Support for additional furniture and objects will be added over time.
[/list]

[h2]Contact and Support[/h2]

Steam lacks any reasonable moderation tools and is thus allowing bad language, hate, harassment, spam and threats. As a result the comment section had to be disabled. The the preferred method of communication is now Discord.

3771638611.title: Fancy Handwork B42.20
3771638611.description:
A suite of animations that make your character feel more alive.

Your character reaches out to what it interacts with - doors, light switches,
stoves, curtains, vehicle doors - instead of triggering them from a distance.
Items are posed properly in each hand, including a weapon in the off hand.

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*]Hand animations for doors, curtains, garage doors, appliances and vehicles
[*]Reaches behind without turning around when the object is at your back
[*]Crouches to lift a closed garage door, reaches up to pull an open one down
[*]Off-hand item poses - carry a knife or a torch and still look right
[*]Reaches for belt and holster slots with the hand on that side
[*]Hold the Modifier key with a hotbar key to equip into the off hand
[*]Cooking and vehicle repair animations
[/list]

[h2]Requirements[/h2]
None. Build 42 loads this mod's animations on its own.

[b]B42 AnimSet Fix is no longer required and is no longer a dependency.[/b]
It never did anything on Build 42 - the functions it tried to call do not
exist in the game any more - so it has been dropped entirely.

[h2]"B42AnimSetsFix is missing" when loading an old save[/h2]
This is not coming from this mod. Every save records the mods that were
active when it was created, in [i]Zomboid\Saves\<mode>\<save>\mods.txt[/i].
If your save was made while AnimSet Fix was installed, that file still lists
it, and the game warns you when it is gone.

One way to fix it:
[list]
[*]Open that mods.txt in a text editor and delete the AnimSet Fix line
[/list]

[h2]Multiplayer[/h2]
People needs to test it. The vehicle entry, clothing reported on earlier versions are fixed.

[h2]Known limitation[/h2]
An item in the off hand shifts during a handgun's recoil. This is vanilla
behaviour - it happens without this mod too, with a handgun and a flashlight.

Build 42 update by klitoris mahpus

3772052709.title: Spawn Selector [B42 Stable]
3772052709.description:
[h1]Spawn Selector[/h1]
Spawn Selector replaces fixed spawn lists with a full world map.

Choose Spawn Selector from the starting-location screen, create your character as normal, then select your exact starting position before entering the world.

[url=https://discord.gg/MqKMUuNyfH] [img]https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white[/img][/url]

[img]https://i.postimg.cc/yN6FG04T/3581012563-preview-download-ezgif-com-resize.gif[/img]

[h2]How It Works[/h2]
[list]
[*]Select Spawn Selector from the vanilla starting-location menu.
[*]Complete sandbox settings, occupation, traits, and character creation normally.
[*]Use the full world map to choose a starting position.
[*]Click Spawn Here to move the character to the selected location.
[/list]

The map cannot be closed until a location has been selected.

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*]Choose any mapped location instead of selecting from a predefined list.
[*]Supports solo and multiplayer.
[*]Automatically displays compatible enabled map mods.
[*]Supports panning and zooming across the complete available world map.
[*]Switch between the standard map and Build 42's detailed terrain view.
[*]Switch between floors to select if you are spawning on the ground floor (default) or upper floors/lower basements.
[*]Displays town names while zoomed out to make navigating the world map easier.
[*]Includes toggleable, colour-coded points of interest for identifying building types while zoomed in. Server owners can disable this feature through the sandbox settings.
[*]Optionally gives players the matching key for the building they choose to spawn in. This is enabled by default and can be disabled through the sandbox settings.
[*]Includes localisation for every language natively supported by Project Zomboid.
[*]Optional Random Spawn challenge mode with hidden destination coordinates.
[*]Places Spawn Selector at the top of the starting-location list.
[*]Prevents the selector from reopening after a character has completed selection.
[*][b]Death Zone Protection[/b] - optionally blocks a player from spawning back near where their previous character died, for a configurable radius and real-world duration.
[*][b]Building Type Blocking[/b]: nine sandbox toggles (Weapons & Military, Medical, Law Enforcement, Retail & Shops, Food & Drink, Industrial, Residential & Lodging, Civic & Public, Recreation) let admins stop players from manually, randomly, or random-building spawning inside specific categories of building, e.g. gun stores or police stations.
[/list]
[h2]Spawn Safety[/h2]
The character is temporarily placed at an isolated staging location while the selection screen is open.

After selecting a destination, the mod provides a short arrival period while the surrounding area finishes loading. Nearby zombies and zombies inside the destination room are cleared during this period. If the selected position is indoors, the mod also attempts to switch on the room lights.

This prevents characters from being attacked before the player has control.
[h2]Map Mod Compatibility[/h2]
Spawn Selector reads the map directories included in the current world. Compatible map mods with standard Project Zomboid world-map data should appear automatically.

For multiplayer, map mods must be installed and configured on the server. A map installed only on the client may appear differently or may not exist in the server world.

Map mods without world-map drawing data may exist in-game but appear blank in the selector.

[h2]Multiplayer Installation[/h2]
Install the mod on the server and all connecting clients.

[code]
WorkshopItems=3772052709
Mods=SpawnSelector
[/code]

Restart the server after changing the mod list.

[h2]Requirements[/h2]
[list]
[*]Project Zomboid Build 42
[*]No additional framework or dependency
[/list]

3775026731.title: Wounds Overhaul [B42]
3775026731.description:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/FEdNglN.jpeg[/img]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Overview[/h2]
Vanilla medicine is a bite, a clock and a pill. This mod gives you a body you have to read, hands that can do a bad job, and blood that runs out - and can be put back.

Everything below can be done wrong. That is the point.

[h1]======================================================[/h1]
[h2]Examination[/h2]
The Health tab shows a silhouette coloured by how bad, not by what. To learn what, you look: left-click a limb and the character actually examines it. Right-click to treat what you found.
[list]
[*]Takes 3 to 12 seconds depending on First Aid
[*]A bandage hides the wound - you see the dressing and whether it hurts
[*]Higher skill: numbers on bars, the sepsis meter, the stage of a Knox infection
[/list]

[h1]======================================================[/h1]
[h2]Sepsis[/h2]
A dirty wound festers; a festering wound reaches the blood. About twelve hours in you feel run down - that is your only cheap warning. Then fever, then you can barely stand, then around day three you die.
[list]
[*]Antibiotics are a course: one pill holds 16 hours, three in a row to finish, a gap rolls it back
[*]Cleaning and dressing slow the infection - a surgeon's hands far more than a novice's
[*]A sterilized bandage does the antiseptic's work while it stays on
[/list]

[h1]======================================================[/h1]
[h2]Stitching[/h2]
Stitches are placed by hand: press on one mark, drag the needle across, release on the other. An untrained hand shakes, stress and exhaustion shake any hand, a surgical needle forgives and a bone one does not. A bad seam tears open when you run or fight. Below First Aid 2 the aim marks are not drawn - you sew along the edge by eye - and the needle hurts even on a perfect pass.

Lacerations can be closed too: trim the ragged edges with a scalpel first (First Aid 2).

[h1]======================================================[/h1]
[h2]Blood[/h2]
Heavy blood loss keeps you weak and cold for days after the cut is dressed - unless you put it back. All of this is a sandbox option, off by default.
[list]
[*]Draw from your own arm into a blood bag and transfuse it into yourself or a patient; bags are single-use
[*]Your own blood is always safe; a stranger's depends on blood group
[*]Everyone has a group on real population odds and nobody knows theirs until a typing kit says so - an untrained eye misreads it, crossmatching never does
[*]A wrong transfusion means hours of fever, the volume lost and kidneys paying later
[*]Keeps 8 hours warm, 35 days in a powered fridge; a cooler slows the clock, a freezer ruins it
[*]Carries what the donor carried - Knox included
[/list]

[h1]======================================================[/h1]
[h2]Also[/h2]
[list]
[*]Open fractures worsen every hour unsplinted and feed the infection
[*]Overdoses wear the liver and kidneys; the next one lands on the last
[*]The blood option puts its supplies in hospital loot: labelled blood bags, transfusion set, typing kit. Off, the mod is pure Lua and leaves nothing in a save
[/list]

[h1]======================================================[/h1]
[h2]Sandbox[/h2]
Every illness switches off on its own. Speeds, the examination requirement, blood storage time, examining while walking, bandages hiding wounds, pixel art mode, medical item frequency - all on the mod's page.

[h1]======================================================[/h1]
[h2]Compatibility[/h2]
Singleplayer and multiplayer. Works with Antibodies, Hex's Bruise System and The Only Cure. Not with other health or blood overhauls.

[h1]======================================================[/h1]
[h2]About[/h2]
The Lua is written with an AI assistant. Design, balance and testing are mine. No generated art: limb sprites are built in Figma, wounds, stitches and icons are vector.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]0.4.8[/h2]
[list]
[*]MP: a bandage that played its animation and did nothing - and a friend's bandage you could not remove - is fixed at the root: the stuck "being treated by X" flag is now cleared on the server at the moment vanilla decides, not only when somebody examines the limb
[*]MP: trimming a laceration that silently did nothing now says why in the server log
[*]A bandage over stitches no longer makes the stitched wound vanish: the engine drops the stitched flag under a dressing, the mod now puts it back
[*]A seam tears only while there is still a wound under it - it reads the closure's own clock, so no more bleeding on healed flesh and no more closures that could never tear
[*]Removing stitches no longer sews them back a few seconds later, and an examined wound no longer drops to "unexamined" just because it started bleeding again
[*]Stitching without training is harder and hurts: below First Aid 2 the aim marks are not drawn - you sew along the edge by eye; a needle through skin costs pain even on a perfect pass, less the better you are
[*]Pixel art mode (sandbox, off by default): every drawing in the mod - limbs, wounds, needles, skulls - through a pixel grid
[*]Blood bags, transfusion and typing kits spawn about half again as often, and a sandbox slider now scales that rate (0 removes them from loot)
[*]Servers must update and restart
[/list]




[hr][/hr]

Spanish added - thanks Lancer. Polish added - thanks AdamowY.

If the mod is worth a coffee to you:
[url=https://ko-fi.com/iitori][img]https://i.imgur.com/kA4WJlV.png[/img][/url]
[hr][/hr]
Websites and design are my day job - have a look:
[url=https://mibrain.site/][img]https://i.imgur.com/yHIOf0R.png[/img][/url]

-6 points

-8 points

*+1 Strength

*Reading skill books also provides flat XP.

-22 points

+2 points

+6 points

3778165486.title: [B42.20] Console Fixes
3778165486.description:
[h1][B42.20] Console Fixes[/h1]
[b]Mod ID:[/b] Build42ConsoleFixes
[b]Workshop ID:[/b] 3778165486
[b]Current version:[/b] 1.0.3
[b]Supported builds:[/b] 42.20.x

A focused ZombieBuddy repair package for noisy or broken diagnostic paths in Project Zomboid Build 42.20. It keeps real content errors visible while preventing known false-positive and headless-server-only error families.
[h2]Included fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Optional animation folders:[/b] missing mod [i]AnimSets[/i] or [i]actiongroups[/i] directories no longer produce hundreds of [i]AdvancedAnimator[/i] stack traces.
[*][b]Checksum null paths:[/b] checksum enumeration safely skips only entries for which Vanilla supplies no usable absolute path. Normal checksum enforcement remains active.
[*][b]Local-coop startup:[/b] the normal Steam-launched client passes ZombieBuddy into its spawned Coop Server JVM, while server-managed translation mods no longer move themselves and their dependencies ahead of the server-provided order.
[*][b]Headless model checks:[/b] Dedicated Servers no longer run client-only model and mesh validation that cannot render anything there.
[*][b]Headless XUI warnings:[/b] Dedicated Servers suppress only the known [i]Could not find icon:[/i] warning family.
[/list]
[h2]What this mod deliberately does not do[/h2]
It does not add missing assets, repair broken vehicle or map content, disable Lua checksums, hide client render diagnostics, or suppress unrelated warnings and exceptions. Existing or unreadable media paths retain their Vanilla diagnostics.
[h2]Requirements and installation[/h2]
[list]
[*]Project Zomboid Build 42.20.x
[*]ZombieBuddy 2.3.2 or newer (Workshop ID [i]3619862853[/i])
[*]Enable [i]ZombieBuddy[/i] before [i]Build42ConsoleFixes[/i] on the Dedicated Server and connecting clients, then fully restart both.

3779164273.title: Improvised Silencers - Build 42.20 Compatibility
3779164273.description:
[h1]Improvised Silencers – Build 42 Update & Expansion[/h1]

This is an unofficial Build 42 update and expanded version of Maxwell218’s excellent [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2799742455]Improvised Silencers[/url].

The original mod has not been updated since 2024. Since I am a huge fan of the mod and wanted to continue using it in Build 42, I initially ported it to the current version of Project Zomboid. Since then, its systems have been extensively reworked and expanded with improved weapon compatibility, attachment handling and new suppressor sounds.

[b]All credit and major props go to Maxwell218, the creator of the original mod.[/b] This version would not exist without their original work.

[h2]Features[/h2]

[list]
[*]Five different craftable suppressors
[*]Professional suppressor
[*]Metal pipe suppressor
[*]Hand torch suppressor
[*]Water bottle suppressor
[*]Potato suppressor: a deliberately weak one-shot gag attachment made from a potato
[*]Different noise-reduction and weapon-range trade-offs
[*]11 new suppressed weapon sounds: 4 for pistols, 4 for rifles, 2 for shotguns and a dedicated potato shot
[*]Professional suppressors can also be found as loot
[*]Compatible with the new vanilla Build 42 firearms
[*]Automatic Guns of Marz compatibility
[*]Automatic Vanilla Firearms Expansion Classic compatibility
[*]Optional Extended Realism Mode with configurable suppression, suppressor durability and caliber-based wear
[*]English, German, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Ukrainian, Turkish, Spanish and Simplified Chinese translations included
[/list]

[h2]Build 42 Changes[/h2]

[list]
[*]Recipes migrated to the new Build 42 craftRecipe system
[*]Weapon-part and attachment definitions updated
[*]Suppressor statistics and weapon handling rewritten for Build 42
[*]Suppressed-shot sounds expanded with weapon-family and suppressor-specific variants
[*]Loot distributions updated
[*]Translation files migrated to the Build 42 format
[*]Support added for the new vanilla Build 42 weapons
[*]Optional sandbox-based suppressor durability and caliber-dependent wear added
[*]One-shot potato suppressor added with its own sound and visual model
[/list]

[h2]Extended Realism Mode[/h2]

[list]
[*]Optional sandbox mode, disabled by default to preserve the standard mod balance
[*]Configurable noise-reduction values for all four standard suppressors
[*]Optional suppressor durability with condition shown in weapon tooltips and the inventory
[*]Optional caliber-based wear: small calibers consume less durability, while rifle and shotgun ammunition consume more
[*]Multiplayer compatible; the server sandbox settings control the behavior
[/list]

[h2]Compatibility[/h2]

[list]
[*]Requires Project Zomboid Build 42.20 or newer
[*]Designed to remain compatible with existing saves
[*]A screwdriver is required to attach or remove the four standard suppressors; the potato suppressor can be fitted by hand
[*]Do not enable this port together with the original Workshop version
[*]Guns of Marz and Vanilla Firearms Expansion are optional and can be used together
[/list]

Always back up important saves before adding or updating mods.

[h2]Guns of Marz Support[/h2]

[list]
[*]Automatic compatibility with supported [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3722134990]Guns of Marz[/url] firearms
[*]All five suppressors can be attached directly to supported Guns of Marz rifles and handguns
[*]Professional and metal pipe suppressors are supported on Guns of Marz shotguns
[*]Guns of Marz muzzle adapters are not required
[*]Guns of Marz remains optional and is not required to use this mod
[/list]

[h2]Vanilla Firearms Expansion Support[/h2]

3779327129.title: CD: Labrador
3779327129.description:
[h1]CD: Labrador[/h1]
[b]Labrador Retrievers for Companion Dogs[/b] - an optional breed add-on for [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3740052292]Companion Dogs[/url].
Built for [b]Build 42 (42.19+)[/b]. Works in [b]singleplayer, co-op AND dedicated servers[/b], and is [b]safe to add to existing saves[/b].

[b]REQUIRES the base mod [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3740052292]Companion Dogs[/url] (0.6.6 or newer).[/b] Subscribe to it as well, enable both mods in the main-menu Mods list, and fully restart the game (this loads the dog model correctly - same as the base mod).

[h1]The dog[/h1]
The [b]hunting dog[/b]. Where the Rottweiler is a wall and the Doberman is a blade, the Labrador is a pair of hands. It is the only dog that reliably brings things back to you, and on purpose the worst fighter available.

[h1]Benefits[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Trains Hunting twice as fast[/b] - it shares that with the Golden Retriever, but the two split the job: the Golden [i]finds[/i] the game, the Labrador [i]brings it back[/i]. Obedience comes close behind, so it still climbs the trick tree (go to a spot, distract zombies, sniff out an item, fetch it while you sleep) ahead of most breeds, and its nose is above average too.
[*][b]Soft Mouth moodle[/b] - unique to the Labrador. Other breeds only start carrying their kills home at a high Hunting skill; a Labrador does it [b]from the very first rabbit it can catch[/b], and it will not give up on the way back the way other dogs do. It also turns up carrying [b]something else it found[/b] more often than not. A starving or disloyal dog gives nothing.
[*][b]You learn from the work[/b] - while a fed, loyal Labrador is at your side you gain [b]Butchering and Short Blade XP faster[/b]. It hands you the carcass, you take it apart, and you get better at both ends of that job.
[*][b]Not a fighter, and that is the point[/b] - the Labrador has the weakest bite in the family, cannot knock a zombie down, and a fight rattles it badly. Pair it with a guard breed, or keep it for the work it is actually good at.
[*][b]Common in homes, and out in the woods[/b] - the Labrador was the most popular dog in America, so it is the easiest breed add-on to find: roughly [b]half the base stray chance per house[/b], on top of the usual strays. Wild ones also turn up around [b]hunting cabins, campsites, boathouses and ranger stations[/b] (both scale with the sandbox Animal/Dog spawn multiplier). Tame one the usual way: feed it until it trusts you.
[*][b]Everything from the base mod[/b] - Follow/Stay/Guard, sentinel alerts, hunting, saddlebags, needs & loyalty, skills & genetics, and breeding (cross-breed litters with the other breeds included).
[/list]

[h3]Warning - removing the add-on[/h3]
Do NOT remove this add-on from a save that has living Labradors: the game engine discards animals of unknown types. Your other dogs and the base mod are unaffected.

[h1]Part of the Companion Dogs family[/h1]
This is an optional add-on. The tameable dogs, follow/guard, needs, skills and breeding all live in the base mod - get it here:
[b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3740052292]>> Companion Dogs (base mod) <<[/url][/b]
More breed add-ons are on the way, each one a separate optional download.

3780639614.title: [B42.20+ MP] - Push Vehicle
3780639614.description:
[h1]Push Vehicle[/h1]

Ever had a vehicle blocking the road with no way to move it by hand?

Push Vehicle lets you physically push stationary vehicles forward or backward, or turn them from the sides, using your character's Strength. Server admins can configure stamina cost, push cooldown and the maximum pushable vehicle weight.

[h2]How to Use[/h2]

[b]Keyboard & Mouse[/b]

[list]
[*]Stand at the front/rear to move it straight, or near the front/rear section of either side to turn it
[*]Make sure you are close enough for the green interaction square to appear
[*]Right-click the vehicle and select [b]Push Vehicle[/b], or use the configurable [b]Push Vehicle[/b] hotkey
[*]The hotkey can be assigned under [b]Options → Key Bindings[/b]
[/list]

[b]Controller[/b]

[list]
[*]Stand at the front/rear to move it straight, or near the front/rear section of either side to turn it
[*]Press [b]D-pad Up[/b] to open the vehicle radial menu
[*]Select [b]Push Vehicle[/b]
[/list]

Front and rear pushes move the vehicle straight. Push near the front or rear section of either side to gradually turn the vehicle.

[h2]Features[/h2]

[list]
[*]Push vehicles forward or backward from the front or rear
[*]Turn vehicles by pushing near the front or rear section of either side
[*]Server admins can disable side pushing in Sandbox settings
[*]Configurable Push Vehicle keyboard hotkey
[*]Uses the vanilla shove animation
[*]Push strength scales with your Strength level
[*]Heavier vehicles are harder to move
[*]Pushing consumes stamina, with a configurable cost multiplier
[*]Configurable delay between pushes
[*]Optional maximum pushable vehicle weight
[*]Works with trailers
[*]Full controller support
[*]Multiplayer compatible and tested
[*]Vehicle movement is synchronized between players
[/list]

[h2]Strength Scaling[/h2]

Your Strength level directly affects how much force you can apply when pushing a vehicle.

[list]
[*]Strength 0: ~60% push power
[*]Strength 5: ~130% push power
[*]Strength 10: ~200% push power
[/list]

Vehicle weight is also taken into account, so a lightweight car is much easier to move than a heavy van or truck.

[h2]Balanced & Vanilla-Friendly[/h2]

Push Vehicle is designed to feel like a natural part of Project Zomboid rather than a cheat.

Stronger characters can move vehicles more effectively, while heavy vehicles still require significantly more effort. Pushing also consumes stamina.

The mod only affects stationary vehicles and does not replace normal vehicle physics or collision behavior.

[h2]Sandbox Settings[/h2]

[list]
[*][b]Allow Side Pushing[/b] — enabled by default
[*][b]Stamina Cost Multiplier[/b] — default 1.0x
[*][b]Push Cooldown[/b] — default 1.0 second
[*][b]Maximum Pushable Weight[/b] — default 0 (no limit)
[/list]

These settings are enforced by the server in multiplayer and are also respected in singleplayer.

[h2]Controller Support[/h2]

[b]Full controller support.[/b]

Controller players can access Push Vehicle directly from the standard vehicle radial menu by pressing D-pad Up while standing in a valid front, rear or side-turn position.

Controller support works in both singleplayer and multiplayer.

[h2]Multiplayer[/h2]

[b]Fully multiplayer compatible and tested.[/b]

Players can take turns pushing the same vehicle, and vehicle movement is synchronized between connected players.

Keyboard, mouse and controller players can all use the mod together.
Server admins can configure side pushing, stamina cost, push cooldown and maximum vehicle weight via [b]Sandbox Settings → Push Vehicle[/b].

[h2]Build Compatibility[/h2]

Made for Project Zomboid Build 42.
