3007922923.title: Proper Vehicle Injuries for MP [B41 & B42]
3007922923.description:
Check out my other mod, [b][u][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2998737588&tscn=1689876920]ComfySleeping[/url][/u][/b]!


[b][u]Artwork Credit[/u][/b]
Credits to Errorthy for drawing the thumbnail!


[h1][u]Purpose[/u][/h1]
The name says it all!

Proper Vehicle Injuries was built to make injuries from car crashes to be more consistent and configurable. Players are now able to configure a large array of options, and can even be hurt by crashing into dense groups of zombie hordes!


[h1][u]Features[/u][/h1]
[list]
[*][b][u][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3055029361]Working Seatbelt[/url][/u][/b] support: PVI is compatible with Working Seatbelt, reducing injuries if seatbelts are buckled, airbags are installed, and potentially ejecting the player out of the vehicle!

[*][b][u][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3048123717]Real Knockouts[/url][/u][/b] support: Car crashes can now knock the player out. Knockout chance is configurable per severity level and overrides Real Knockouts chance for car crashes only.

[*][b][u]Helmets protect your head[/u][/b]: Does what it says on the tin! Helmets offer head protection with the highest protection helmets being full-face helmets (like motorcycle helmets), and half-face helmets (riding helmets) give a lower injury reduction.

[*][b][u]Multiplayer Support:[/u][/b] Now you can share your collision related injuries with others!

[*][b][u]Varying Severity Levels:[/u][/b] Different speeds can cause different injuries, with different times needed to heal. The faster you go, the worse it'll be!

[*][b][u]Zombie Hordes:[/u][/b] Trying to make a quick get away, and slam into a horde? Congratulations, because it's not just other vehicles and buildings that you can collide with!

[*][b][u]Full Limb Fractures:[/u][/b] Makes that broken arm just that much worse, by breaking the rest of it!

[*][b][u]Fatal Crashes:[/u][/b] Going full speed and not paying attention? Hitting a pole or other objects from full speed can very well now spell the end of your character!

[*][b][u]Customizability:[/u][/b] Not a fan of how often certain injuries happen? Nearly all of the variables for this mod are available in the sandbox options!
[/list]


[h1][u]Planned Features[/u][/h1]
[list]
[*] Minimum injuries - Currently the injury count is entirely random aside from the general body damage the player receives (this is what lowers your healthbar on collision).
[/list]

If you have any other ideas that you think would be in line with the mod, feel free to add them to the "Ideas & Suggestions" discussion. However, please note that this is a passion project of mine, so suggestions may or may not be implemented!


[h1][u]SANDBOX OPTIONS[/u][/h1]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/discussion/3007922923/3807281445009927262/]Click here to see the sandbox options and their description/examples![/url]

If the above link isn't working, keep scrolling and look for the pinned "Sandbox Options" discussion board.


[h1][u]FAQ (READ BEFORE COMMENTING)[/u][/h1]
[list]
[*][b][u]Is PVI compatible with B42.20+?[/u][/b]
[/list]
It should, yes! PVI works with the latest version of B41 and B42.

[list]
[*][b][u]Does the load order matter when using PVI, Working Seatbelts, and Real Knockouts?[/u][/b] 
[/list]
No. According to my personal save and user reports, the load order of the three mods does not appear to matter.

[list]
[*][b][u]Does this mod have any incompatibilities?[/u][/b] 
[/list]
It shouldn't, however extremely touchy vehicles may trigger false positives and result in 'whiplash' injuries. However, this shouldn't be an issue for 99% of vehicles.

[list]
[*][b][u]Does this mod work in SP/Coop/Dedicated MP?[/u][/b] 
[/list]
Yes, it works in all 3!*

* Injuries are no longer authorized by the client,  so PVI will need to have injury code moved to the server side. If you notice injuries from crashes disappearing immediately after crashing, this is why.

[list]
[*][b][u]Is this safe to add to a current save?[/u][/b] 
[/list]
Yes!

[list]
[*][b][u]I'm adding this to an existing SP save, how do I change the sandbox options mid save?[/u][/b] 
[/list]
Use a mod such as [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2894296454&searchtext=change+sandbox+options]Change Sandbox Options[/url] to modify them.

[h1][u]KNOWN ISSUES[/u][/h1]
[list]
[*] Possible compatibility issue with hotwire nerf mod, may cause immediate stop of hotwired vehicle, causing false positives for collisions.
[*] Injury authority moved from client to server. This means that the server must deal and handle injuries, injuries dealt by the client (as PVI currently does) causes them to briefly appear then disappear when the server sends over what it believes is the player's current injuries, effectively making PVI's crash injuries disappear.
[/list]


[h1]Translations[/h1]
PVI has translations for the following languages:
[list]
[*]English - Translated by Fluffy89
[*]Brazilian Portuguese - Translated by Sknurt
[*] Simplified Chinese - Translated by Phoenix
[/list]

Thanks to all who have provided or helped translate the mod into various languages! If there are any translation or spelling issues in any of the available translations, or you would like to translate the mod, please let me know!

[url=http://theindiestone.com/forums/index.php/topic/2530-mod-permissions/?p=36478][img]https://i.postimg.cc/P5RLhyGd/MODS-03.png[/img][/url]

Feel free to include the mod in modpacks/workshop collections here on Steam. You are however NOT AUTHORISED to do any of the following:
[list]

[*] Modify Comfy Sleeping's code (you may create patches, but they must require Comfy Sleeping).
[*] Share, upload, or scrape my code for use in training LLM's, or to be part of their dataset.

3444499190.title: Farming Expansion B42
3444499190.description:
[h2]Updated for b42.20 not tested in mp[/h2]

[b][h2][url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cXxhD_WJPA0]Review of the mod[/url][/h2][/b]

The mod adds the ability to grow fruits (apples and grapes at the moment, more in future).
These plants survive the winter and do not progress in the winter, and continue their life cycle in the spring.
Trees and grape vines do not rot after they have reached the final stage of growth.
After harvesting, they return to the stage at which the bush/tree grew and the fruits grow again.
Seeds can be found in the same place as vanilla seeds. They can also be crafted.
If you can't craft seeds from rotten apples/grapes try press craft button and speed up time

Can be installed into an existing save. All you need to do is find seeds in unexplored territory or find apples/grapes (fresh or rotten) and make seeds from them.

The mod also adds the ability to create vinegar and salt:
1. In order to produce vinegar, you will need a Hand Press from pottering and a fermentation barrel added by the mod. Squeeze the juice from the apples and make vinegar from it.
2. To create salt, you can search for rock salt by Foraging in the same places where you find rocks, clay, limestone (you can find it from level 2 Foraging) Then you just need to grind it with mortar and pestle.

UPD 16.03
Added the ability to create wine and added yeast to the vinegar craft. Also added the ability to create seeds from rotten fruits.

UPD 17.03
Added a fermentation pot which helps in creating beer and sugar. Now you can create beer from wheat, cider from apples, sugar from sugar beets, yeast from beer. The pot itself can either be found in kitchens in unexplored territory or created yourself in the metalworking tab

UPD 30.03
MAJOR UPDATE. The method of creating items has been completely reworked. Now everything that requires maturation must stand in a barrel for several days until it is fully ready. Including vinegar and yeast in a jar for several days.

-All items now have hints on what to do with them next.
-Added the ability to create whiskey.
-Russian and Ukrainian localization added.
-Added a fermentation barrel and a wooden barrel for storing drinks (A wooden barrel has a specific sound when pouring from it).
-The ability to build a fermentation barrel has been removed as it no longer has crafting options.
-Added moonshine still.
-All crafts are now located in the Farming Expansion tab.
-Reduced salt spawn and reworked item consumption in crafting after the release of 42.6.
-Cherry added.
-Added the ability to create juice in 5 and 10 liters at once.

In future:
-Adding crafts to various alcoholic drinks.
-Adding more fruit trees.
-Also suggest your ideas in the comments.

v1.3 fix 2
-The seed crafting recipe has been adjusted to reflect the latest updates. It now uses only 1 fruit, even if it's rotten.
-The juice recipe has been fixed. It now uses whole fruits instead of hunger units.
-The beer brewing recipe has been fixed so that it no longer destroys an extra keg.
-Fixed the sugar base recipe to use whole vegetables instead of hunger units.

Suggestions for balancing things are also welcome.

If backpacks can have bedrolls and tents attached underneath, shouldn't weapons be able to hang there too?

BagBottomWeaponAttach is a very small quality-of-life mod that lets bag bottom attachment slots hold large back-slot weapons, similar to the normal back slot.

[*] Use BedrollBottom, BedrollBottomBig, or BedrollBottomALICE depending on the backpack shape or size
[*] Example: to add vanilla Schoolbag support, use addAttachmentsProvidedPatch("VANILLA_SCHOOLBAG", "Base.Bag_Schoolbag", "BedrollBottom")

[hr][/hr]

This is a library mod that simplifies the process of adding features to weapon mods. By itself, this mod does not change the game.

[h3]For End Users[/h3]
Subscribe to this mod only if another mod lists it as a required dependency.

[h3]For Modders[/h3]
What sets this framework apart is its focus on making weapons modular platforms for ammo, magazines, and attachments instead of forcing each weapon to use rigid, exact parts and ammunition types.

[b]Current Systems[/b]
[list]
[*] Ammunition system for weapons and magazines that can use more than one ammo type, with optional stat changes per load.
[*] Animation system for weapon cycling, racking, and extra ammo-count visuals.
[*] Bayonet system for both attachable bayonets and built-in bayonets.
[*] Custom stats attachment system so installed parts can modify weapon stats while attached.
[*] Dynamic attachments system for parts that swap between two states, such as folded and deployed variants.
[*] Folding bipod system with optional stat and visual changes between folded and deployed states.
[*] Folding stock system with optional stat and visual changes between folded and deployed states.
[*] Magazine system for assigning multiple compatible magazines or speed-loaders to the same weapon family.
[*] Prevent removal system for permanent or non-removable weapon parts.
[*] Railing system for defining which accessories a rail accepts, plus weapon-specific exclusions.
[*] Rate of fire system for custom RPM, burst settings, and optional spread tuning.
[*] Stats factory helpers for setting, scaling, and adjusting weapon stats across the framework.
[*] Underbarrel system for grenade launchers, shotguns, and other alternate weapon modes.
[*] Universal attachment system for generic kits that install different real parts depending on the weapon.
[*] Upgrade exclusives system for blocking incompatible upgrades from being installed together.
[*] Explosives system for throwable explosives and explosive ammo with custom arcs and detonation behavior.
[*] Distribution functions for adding, removing, and tuning weapons, parts, and ammo in loot tables.
[/list]

[b]Coming Soon[/b]
[list]
[*] Custom animations with visible magazines during the animation process
[*] Hip firing, dual wielding, and firing while running
[*] Further improvements to the explosives system
[/list]

To add these systems to your mod, read the API docs included in the mod files for setup details and examples.

3779343349.title: Custom Light Switch [42.20.4]
3779343349.description:
[h1]Custom Light Switch[/h1]

[i]Read the guide, grab a screwdriver, wire up any room you build yourself.[/i]
[i]No more pitch-black player-built rooms because "there's no switch here".[/i]

[h2]What it does[/h2]

In vanilla, wall light switches only exist in buildings the game generates — build your own walls and you're stuck in the dark. This mod adds a fully functional wall light switch you can build (and dismantle) yourself, in any room, with the game's real lightbulb and power system underneath.

[h2]Features[/h2]

[list]
[*] [b]Build in all 4 directions[/b], always placed flush against the wall
[*] [b]Actually lights a room you built yourself[/b]: in the base game, only rooms that already existed on the map from the start can ever light up, never ones you build yourself. This mod creates the lighting itself the moment you place a switch, with a generator running
[*] [b]Multiple switches, one room[/b]: if a room has more than one switch, they stay in sync — flipping one turns the room's light on or off for all of them
[*] [b]Universal dismantle[/b]: works on any wall switch, even ones already in the generated world (not lamps, fixtures, or streetlights — only real switches)
[*] [b]Random salvage[/b] on dismantle (25% chance per material) to stop infinite farming
[*] [b]Screwdriver wear[/b]: chance to lose 1 condition per build or dismantle, same system as any tool in the game (hammer, axe...) — regular, old, or improvised all work, but the improvised one wears down faster
[*] [b]Electrical XP[/b]: +5 on build, +2 on dismantle
[*] [b]Recipe tied to a findable item[/b]: the magazine spawns in electronics store and bookstore loot, or learned automatically at Electrical level 3
[*] [b]100% compatible with the native electrical system[/b]: lightbulb, generator power cuts, everything behaves like a vanilla switch
[/list]

[h2]How to use[/h2]

[olist]
[*] Find "The Great Mystery of the Light Switch" magazine (electronics stores, bookstores) and read it (requires Electrical level 1) — or just reach Electrical level 3, the recipe unlocks on its own, no magazine needed
[*] Carry a screwdriver (regular, old, or improvised), 1x Electronics Scrap, 1x Electric Wire, 2x Screws
[*] Right-click an interior wall → [b]Build a Light Switch[/b]
[*] Add a generator nearby, same as any switch in the game — your room actually lights up, even a brand new one
[*] Right-click any switch → [b]Dismantle Light Switch[/b] to take it back down (recipe known + screwdriver required)
[/olist]

[h2]Compatibility[/h2]

[list]
[*] Project Zomboid Build [b]42.20+[/b] (Stable)
[*] Solo: Yes (tested)
[*] Multiplayer: Yes, tested and confirmed working on a live dedicated server (build, dismantle, lighting, recipe learning)
[*] Other mods adding walls/rooms: Yes (generic wall detection via tile properties)
[/list]

[h2]Languages[/h2]

English, French, Russian (translation by AVA)

[hr][/hr]

[h1]Version française[/h1]

[i]Lis le guide, prends un tournevis, câble n'importe quelle pièce que tu construis toi-même.[/i]
[i]Fini les pièces plongées dans le noir faute d'interrupteur.[/i]

En vanilla, les interrupteurs muraux n'existent que dans les bâtiments générés par le jeu — si tu construis tes propres murs, impossible d'en avoir un. Ce mod ajoute un interrupteur mural constructible (et démontable) toi-même, dans n'importe quelle pièce, branché sur le vrai système d'ampoule et de courant du jeu.

[h2]Fonctionnalités[/h2]

[list]
[*] [b]Pose dans les 4 directions[/b], toujours collée au mur
[*] [b]Éclaire vraiment ta pièce construite toi-même[/b] : dans le jeu de base, seules les pièces déjà présentes sur la carte au départ peuvent s'allumer, jamais celles que tu construis toi-même. Ce mod crée l'éclairage lui-même dès que tu poses un interrupteur, avec un générateur en marche
[*] [b]Plusieurs interrupteurs, une pièce[/b] : si une pièce a plusieurs interrupteurs, ils restent synchronisés entre eux, actionner l'un allume ou éteint la pièce pour tous
[*] [b]Démontage universel[/b] : marche sur n'importe quel interrupteur mural, même ceux déjà présents dans le monde généré (pas les lampes, luminaires ou lampadaires, seulement les vrais interrupteurs)
[*] [b]Récupération aléatoire[/b] au démontage (25% de chance par matériau) pour éviter le farm infini
[*] [b]Usure du tournevis[/b] : chance de perdre 1 de condition à chaque construction ou démontage, même système que n'importe quel outil du jeu (marteau, hache...) — classique, vieux ou improvisé tous acceptés, mais l'improvisé s'use plus vite
[*] [b]XP Électricité[/b] : +5 à la construction, +2 au démontage
[*] [b]Recette liée à un objet trouvable[/b] : le magazine apparaît dans le loot des magasins d'électronique et des librairies, ou apprise automatiquement au niveau Électricité 3
[*] [b]Compatible à 100% avec le système électrique natif[/b] : ampoule, coupure de courant par générateur, tout fonctionne comme un interrupteur vanilla
[/list]

[h2]Comment l'utiliser[/h2]

[olist]
[*] Trouve le magazine "Le grand Mystère de l'interrupteur" (magasins d'électronique, librairies) et lis-le (Électricité niveau 1 requis) — ou atteins simplement le niveau Électricité 3, la recette se débloque toute seule, sans magazine
[*] Prends un tournevis (classique, vieux ou improvisé), 1x Pièce électronique, 1x Fil électrique, 2x Vis
[*] Clic droit sur un mur intérieur → [b]Construire un interrupteur[/b]
[*] Ajoute un générateur à proximité, comme pour n'importe quel interrupteur du jeu — ta pièce s'allume vraiment, même toute neuve
[*] Clic droit sur n'importe quel interrupteur → [b]Démonter Interrupteur[/b] pour le retirer (recette connue + tournevis requis)
[/olist]

[h2]Compatibilité[/h2]

[list]
[*] Project Zomboid Build [b]42.20+[/b] (Stable)
[*] Solo : Oui (testé)
[*] Multijoueur : Oui, testé et confirmé fonctionnel sur un vrai serveur dédié (construction, démontage, éclairage, apprentissage de la recette)
[*] Mods ajoutant des murs/pièces : Oui (détection de mur générique via propriétés de tuile)
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

Found a bug? Have a suggestion? Drop a comment below — I read everything.

Created by [b]Ghoosty[/b].

2142622992.title: Repair Any Clothes
2142622992.description:
Makes you able to repair any clothes you want, such as vests, bulletproof vests, jumpsuits, etc.

Working for B42!

[h1] Are you generous and thankful for the mod? [/h1]
[url=https://www.rspca.org.uk/getinvolved/donate/online] Please consider to donate to animals in need! [/url]

[i] In 4 years and over 1.3 million concurrent subscribers, I have only earned 5 euros in that entire time from mods.
It was a very rewarding 5 euros, I mean who the hell ever gets paid for their hobby?
But that's exactly what it is, a hobby, and I would honestly feel better in my heart knowing that an animal gets to live a happy life instead of me having some pocket change for a coffee because of a zombie game, and my wife being a seamstress. [/i]

[i] 
Thank you CarlosRojasCu for updating the mod when I was busy
Thank you everyone for almost half a decade of positive comments, happy moments and for being grateful.
You all helped me stay focused and inspired to challenge myself and be a better person.[/i]




Have you ever found a snazzy Jumpsuit, only to be forced to throw it out, because of ugly holes?
And what of the lovely Santa Suits, for when you wanted to bring Christmas Joy to the Undead of Kentucky, only to have them crying like Snoopy from "The Peanuts" because all the Santa Suits were ruined.

Have you ever wanted to express your inner fursona in an apocalypse, but alas, you had to make due with your human skin, because all Spiffo suits were fit for peasants?
What about all the poor gopniks and lovely slavs who need to show off their perfect Adidas suit only to have some filthy rotter chomp in their lovely shell suit jacket or pants?
And of course, your ultra cool survivors with mood swings had no way to express their darkness, and how unique they were without their fingerless gloves.

What about your trusty boots or fancy leather shoes? Got a hole in them, and for some reason you can't slap some duct tape on it?
That's also taken care of now, as you too can sit down, and master the art of becoming a cobbler, also known as a shoemaker!
Fix those pesky holes with the corresponding material, and you can walk over all the puddles Kentucky has to offer, water or brains from the zombies you've stomped!

Search no longer weary traveler, because gone are the days of throwing out clothes you, for some reason, couldn't fix!
WASTE NOT WANT NOT with this mod, as it allows you to fix all clothing, so whether you're a hobo, furry, teenage flick vampire, military man with enough equipment to break your back, YOU TOO, can look your very best in the Apocalypse!

This mod puts all the clothes you couldn't fix before, and makes them fixable.
No limitations, no telling you "You can't fix broken shoes".
Just this one mod that does everything, and it's completely vanilla friendly.




[h1] FAQ [/h1]
Q: Does this work with my version, multiplayer, singleplayer?
A: It works with Build 42 both multi and single.

Q: How do I fix my clothes completely without having patches on them?
A: Level your tailoring to at least 8!

Q: I can't repair something
A: Make sure you have needle, thread and ripped sheets, denim or leather strips.

Q: I still can't repair it!
A: Then another mod is breaking it for you. Enable only this mod to see if it works, then start enabling the other mods you use to find the broken mod.


Q: Am I allowed to repack your mod, alter it in any way and upload it to the workshop?
A: Only if you put it under a different name, artwork, and if you're running a server and need to alter it, privatize it.


In your server settings turn off AntiCheatProtectionType21.
Use link below if you're still having issues.
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3417055526] If you're having trouble joining or starting your server that was running the old version, a B41 version can be found here, from before the mod was improved.[/url]

[*]Mod works perfectly in both multiplayer and singleplayer modes, making it a must-have mod for all gamers who love literature.

Overall, the this is a fantastic mod that makes it much easier for you to keep track of all the literature items you come across in your gameplay. With its many great features and configurable settings, this mod is perfect for all literature enthusiasts out there!

3755731521.title: [42.20] Lethal Stealth Fix - LTSSync nil guards
3755731521.description:
[h1][42.20] Lethal Stealth Fix - LTSSync nil guards[/h1]

Fixes the crash [b]"Expected a table"[/b] at [b]LTSSync.lua:66[/b] ([b]LTSSyncProneStatesFromServer[/b]) and prevents the same class of error in sibling network handlers when a server/client command delivers an empty/nil payload.

[h2]What does it do?[/h2]
In Build 42, [b]RET_LTS.LTSSyncProneStatesFromServer(args)[/b] calls [b]pairs(args)[/b] without checking [b]args[/b], so an empty payload from the server throws "Expected a table" and breaks the prone-state sync.
This fix monkey-patches the global [b]RET_LTS[/b] network handlers to bail out early when [b]args[/b] is not a table, and also hardens the sibling handlers [b]LTSSyncProneStatesFromClient[/b], [b]LTSSyncSpeedFromClient/FromServer[/b], [b]OnSneakActionEvent[/b] and [b]CrawlUnderVehicleClientAction[/b].

[h2]Requirements[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Lethal Stealth[/b] (Mod ID [b]RET_LethalStealth[/b]) - must be active
[/list]

[h2]Compatibility[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Build 42.20[/b]
[*] Load this mod [b]after[/b] Lethal Stealth in your mod list
[/list]

[i]If the original author fixes their mod, use theirs instead.[/i]

3757137484.title: [B42] Echoes of Knox - Dynamic Story Events
3757137484.description:
[h1]Echoes of Knox [B42][/h1]
[h3]Radio Distress Calls. Handwritten Clues. Stories You Follow.[/h3]
[h3]Dynamic Story Teller / Diegetic Quest System[/h3]
[h3]Version 1.0.1[/h3]

[b]Tune your radio to 101.9 MHz. Echoes adds this channel to your radio presets. Write down what you hear. Follow the lead.[/b]

Echoes of Knox fills Knox County with the traces of people who were here before the outbreak took them. Radio distress calls, handwritten notes, hidden stashes, barricaded rooms, blood trails, and bodies with one last message in their pocket.

You are not following quest markers. You are following breadcrumbs left by the dead.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]How It Works[/h2]

[list]
[*] [b]Hear a signal.[/b] Radio distress calls broadcast on 101.9 MHz. Select Echoes Emergency Traffic in your radio's Channel presets, tune in, turn up the volume, and listen. The signal fades. It repeats a few times. Then it is gone.
[*] [b]Write it down.[/b] Grab a pen or pencil and any writable surface :  paper, notebook, journal, index card. Jot the clue before you forget it.
[*] [b]Find a clue.[/b] Notes found in the world, including notes carried by some zombies, can point you toward a scene too.
[*] [b]Follow the lead.[/b] A radio message or written clue points you toward a place. A clinic. A checkpoint. A rooftop hideout. A family home. Go there.
[*] [b]Discover what happened.[/b] Find the scene. A locked room. A hidden stash. A failed shelter. A body. A warning scrawled on a scrap of paper. Sometimes supplies. Sometimes only the aftermath.
[/list]

No quest log. No map markers. No NPCs telling you where to go. Just you, a radio, a pen, and the world.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]What You Will Find[/h2]

Every signal leads to a procedural scene assembled from modular story pieces. What you find depends on the story, the location, the timing, and a little luck.

[list]
[*] [b]Notes and journals[/b] :  last words, warnings, supply lists, evacuation plans, and clues to scenes elsewhere
[*] [b]Hidden stashes[/b] :  supplies someone cached before they ran out of time
[*] [b]Barricaded rooms[/b] :  someone tried to hold out here
[*] [b]Bodies and blood trails[/b] :  the aftermath did not go well
[*] [b]Abandoned vehicles[/b] :  crashed, stripped, or left behind
[*] [b]Corpse clues[/b] :  some zombies still carry notes. Check their pockets.
[/list]

Stories appear around clinics, schools, churches, restaurants, roadsides, checkpoints, family homes, prepper caches, barricaded buildings, and rooftop hideouts. Some clues branch into follow-up scenes at another location, and some are written for a specific person or group.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Sandbox Settings[/h2]

You control the pace. Sandbox options let you tune:

[list]
[*] How often radio signals appear
[*] How often killed zombies carry clue notes
[/list]

Discovered events persist in your save. Leads do not vanish when you log off.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Compatibility[/h2]

[list]
[*] Built for Project Zomboid Build 42.20 stable
[*] Standalone :  no other mods required
[*] Single player (multiplayer world edits are not supported yet)
[*] [b]Requires a new save.[/b] Not compatible with existing worlds.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Release Notes[/h2]

[h3]v1.0.1[/h3]

[list]
[*] Improved radio tuning, nearby radio selection, and fixed not being able to tune to station.
[*] Prevented duplicate radio signal delivery and kept unfinished scene signals available for replay
[*] Hardened note, corpse, stash, and aftermath placement for more reliable scene generation
[/list]

[h3]v1.0.0[/h3]

[list]
[*] Expanded procedural story library with new food, prepper, barricaded, rooftop, and checkpoint scenarios
[*] Cross-category follow-up leads that carry stories into new locations
[*] More specific POI matching for story premises, including civic subtypes
[*] Context-aware target clues and richer multi-stage scene variation
[*] Radio signal clues with manual jotting
[*] Corpse note clues
[*] Placed notes, stashes, corpses, zombies, barricades, blood, vehicles, and aftermath scenes
[*] Persistent world events
[*] Sandbox options for signal pacing and corpse clue chance
[/list]

More stories, note variants, stash types, scene details, and follow-up chains are planned.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Credits & Support[/h2]

Favorites, ratings, bug reports, and content feedback help the mod grow.

[url=https://ko-fi.com/xela146][img]https://i.imgur.com/YdRA7LZl.jpg[/img][/url]

[hr][/hr]

3788758917.title: Foode's GOM + Lethal Stealth Compatibility Patch
3788758917.description:
[h1]FOODE'S GOM + LETHAL STEALTH COMPATIBILITY PATCH[/h1]

[h2]Stay Low. Keep Firing.[/h2]

A lightweight compatibility patch for [b]Guns of Marz[/b] and [b]Lethal Stealth[/b].

[b]Built for Build 42 • Multiplayer Tested[/b]


[h1]OVERVIEW[/h1]

Love the weapon variety of [b]Guns of Marz[/b] and the expanded movement offered by [b]Lethal Stealth[/b]?

So do I.

Unfortunately, combining the two could cause GOM firearms — especially automatic weapons — to behave incorrectly while using Lethal Stealth's crouch and prone stances.

[b]This patch fixes that interaction.[/b]

GOM weapons can now be used while crouched or prone without the firing bounce that previously disrupted movement and combat.

The goal is simple:

[b]Make the two mods work together without changing what makes either of them great.[/b]


[h1]WHAT THIS PATCH FIXES[/h1]

[list]
[*] Fixes firing bounce while crouched
[*] Fixes firing bounce while prone
[*] Supports automatic fire while using Lethal Stealth stances
[*] Supports semi-auto and burst-fire behavior
[*] Preserves Guns of Marz weapon behavior
[*] Preserves Lethal Stealth crouch and prone functionality
[/list]


[h1]MULTIPLAYER[/h1]

[b]Multiplayer tested.[/b]

This patch has been tested with multiple players using Guns of Marz weapons while:

[list]
[*] Crouching
[*] Going prone
[*] Aiming and firing
[*] Using semi-auto, burst and full-auto fire
[*] Reloading magazines
[*] Switching fire modes
[*] Changing stances during combat
[/list]

Extended testing with automatic weapons showed [b]no firing bounce and no errors[/b] during our testing.


[h1]REQUIREMENTS[/h1]

This is a compatibility patch and does [b]not[/b] replace either original mod.

You will need:

[list]
[*] Guns of Marz
[*] Lethal Stealth
[/list]

[b]Both mods should be installed and enabled before this patch.[/b]


[h1]LOAD ORDER[/h1]

Recommended order:

Guns of Marz

Lethal Stealth

[b]Foode's GOM + Lethal Stealth Compatibility Patch[/b]

The compatibility patch should load [b]after both mods[/b] so its changes are applied last.


[h1]DESIGN PHILOSOPHY[/h1]

[h2]NO MORE FIRING BOUNCE. STEALTHY. SMOOTH. DEADLY.[/h2]

This isn't intended to rebalance Guns of Marz or redesign Lethal Stealth.

It exists specifically to resolve the conflict between them.

[b]GOM stays GOM.[/b]

[b]Lethal Stealth stays Lethal Stealth.[/b]

This patch simply lets them play nicely together.


[h1]CREDITS[/h1]

[b]Guns of Marz[/b] and all of its original assets and systems belong to its respective creator(s).

[b]Lethal Stealth[/b] and all of its original assets and systems belong to its respective creator(s).

This Workshop item does not redistribute either original mod and is intended only as an independent compatibility patch.

Thanks to the original mod authors for their work.


[h1]FOODE'S WASTELAND[/h1]

Originally developed and tested as part of the mod setup used for [b]Foode's Wasteland[/b].

The compatibility patch itself is not server-specific and can be used anywhere the supported mods are installed.

[b]Built for Build 42.
Multiplayer Tested.
Stay Low. Keep Firing.[/b]

3789895769.title: Guns of Marz - Durability Patch
3789895769.description:
[h1]Guns of Marz - Durability Patch[/h1]
[i]A lightweight and configurable balance patch for Guns of Marz.[/i]

[h2]What is this mod for?[/h2]
Guns of Marz includes a large and detailed firearm collection, but some servers may prefer weapons that last longer or hit harder. This external patch lets server owners adjust those values without replacing or editing any original Guns of Marz file.

It is designed for Build 42 multiplayer and dedicated servers, with conservative defaults that preserve the behavior of the previously published version.

[h2]Default balance[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Maximum condition x2[/b] - enabled by default, with a minimum ConditionMax of 20.
[*][b]Wear resistance x3[/b] - enabled by default by tripling ConditionLowerChanceOneIn.
[*][b]Firearm damage x2[/b] - available as an option, disabled by default.
[/list]

Updating from v1.0.2 without changing the Sandbox settings keeps the same durability and wear behavior. Damage remains unchanged.

[h2]Sandbox settings[/h2]
Each feature can be controlled independently under [b]Guns of Marz - Durability Patch[/b]:
[list]
[*][b]Double maximum condition[/b]
[*][b]Triple weapon wear resistance[/b]
[*][b]Double firearm damage[/b]
[*][b]Detailed debug logging[/b]
[/list]

A full server restart is required after changing these settings. The patch deliberately avoids fake hot reloads, permanent scans and per-frame processing.

[h2]How it works[/h2]
[list]
[*]Only weapon definitions whose full type begins with [b]MarzGuns.[/b] are eligible.
[*]Magazines, ammunition, attachments, vanilla weapons and firearms from other mods are not modified.
[*]Original GoM values are captured before applying the selected settings, preventing x2 from becoming x4 or x8 after repeated starts.
[*]Optional damage modifies only [b]MinDamage[/b] and [b]MaxDamage[/b]. Projectile count is never changed, including on shotguns.
[*]SWMG attachment and ammunition modifiers continue to apply normally.
[/list]

[h2]Existing saves and weapons[/h2]
The mod can be added to an existing world. New weapons immediately use the configured values.

Already-correct weapons are left untouched. If a loaded or equipped GoM firearm still carries a different ConditionMax, it is synchronized through SWMG while preserving its current condition percentage. No global map scan or permanent inventory scan is used.

[h2]Performance and multiplayer[/h2]
[list]
[*]One small pass over item scripts during startup.
[*]No OnTick loop.
[*]No recurring inventory or world scan.
[*]No additional network spam.
[*]Shared Sandbox settings for consistent server and client values.
[/list]

[h2]Requirements and load order[/h2]
[list]
[*]SWMG / Gunworks framework
[*]Guns of Marz
[*]This patch loaded after both dependencies
[/list]

[h2]Important[/h2]
This Workshop item contains no Guns of Marz models, textures, sounds or scripts. It does not replace original GoM files and only adjusts exposed weapon statistics at runtime.

[hr][/hr]
[h1]Résumé français[/h1]
Ce patch externe permet de régler la durabilité et les dégâts des armes Guns of Marz sans modifier le mod original.

[list]
[*][b]Condition maximale x2[/b] - activée par défaut, minimum 20.
[*][b]Résistance à l'usure x3[/b] - activée par défaut.
[*][b]Dégâts des armes à feu x2[/b] - option disponible, désactivée par défaut.
[*]Réglages indépendants dans les options Sandbox.
[*]Aucun cumul des multiplicateurs après plusieurs redémarrages.
[*]Aucun scan permanent et aucune boucle OnTick.
[*]Les armes vanilla et celles des autres mods ne sont pas modifiées.
[/list]

Après une modification des options Sandbox, un redémarrage complet du serveur est nécessaire. Une mise à jour depuis la v1.0.2 avec les réglages par défaut conserve exactement le comportement précédent.

3543612325.title: Restore Engine Quality [B42]
3543612325.description:
Restore your vehicle's engine quality with a Wrench, Spare Engine Parts, and Mechanical skill 4+

Unlike vanilla engine [i]condition[/i] (which affects durability), engine [i]quality[/i] determines starting reliability, fuel efficiency, and cold weather performance. This mod lets you restore quality from any percentage up to 100%.

[h2]Why Use This Mod?[/h2]
[list]
[*]Have you ever found a great military vehicle, but its engine quality is completely ruined?
[*]Have you already repaired and fully upgraded a car for long trips, but starting the engine still requires minutes of attempts?
[*]Then this mod is for you - restore the engine to its day-one state, just like it was set from the factory.
[/list]

[h2]Key Features[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Engine Quality Restoration[/b]: Improve quality from any percentage up to 100%
[*][b]Skill-Based Mechanics[/b]: Higher Mechanics skill = better quality increases per iteration (just like vanilla [url=https://pzwiki.net/wiki/Engine#Repairing]engine repairing[/url] works)
[*][b]Configurable Resource Cost[/b]: Adjust engine parts consumption multiplier in Menu -> Options -> Mods -> Restore Engine Quality (1-5 per restoration, default: 2)
[/list]

[h2]How to Use[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Requirements:[/b] Wrench (or Ratchet Wrench), Spare Engine Parts, appropriate Mechanics skill level (4+)
[*][b]Access:[/b] Right-click vehicle Engine → Restore Engine Quality [i](the same context menu where "Repair Engine" located)[/i]
[*][b]Process:[/b] Each restoration consumes engine parts and improves quality based on your skill
[/list]

[h2]Resource Cost[/h2]
By default, requires 2x more Spare Engine Parts than regular engine repair (making it more challenging but not grindy). You can adjust this multiplier in mod options from 1x (same as repair) to 5x (very expensive).

[h2]Engine Quality Effects[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Starting Reliability[/b]: Lower quality = higher chance to fail starting
[*][b]Fuel Efficiency[/b]: Lower quality = up to 50% more fuel consumption
[*][b]Cold Weather Starting[/b]: Quality ≤65% struggles in cold weather
[*][b]Engine Power[/b]: Higher quality = more horsepower (affects reverse speed)
[/list]

[h2]Requirements[/h2]
[list]
[*][url=https://pzwiki.net/wiki/Wrench]Wrench[/url] (or any WRENCH-tagged tool, e.g. Ratchet Wrench)
[*][url=https://pzwiki.net/wiki/Spare_Engine_Parts]Spare Engine Parts[/url]
[*]Minimal [url=https://pzwiki.net/wiki/Mechanics]Mechanics[/url] level 4/5/6 for standard/heavy-duty/sports vehicles respectively.
[/list]

The percentage each (2) engine parts restore depends on your mechanics skill and car type (modded vehicles can use their own required mechanics level).

For example, at level 10 mechanics, 50 spare engine parts will restore a standard car's engine quality from 0% to 100%.

Based on your Mechanics level, each 2 Spare Engine Parts will restore 1-5% Engine Quality.

[code]1 + (<Mechanics Level> - <Required Level>) / 2[/code]

[table]
[tr][td][b]Mechanics Level[/b][/td][td][b]Standard Cars[/b][/td][td][b]Heavy-Duty Cars[/b][/td][td][b]Sports Cars[/b][/td][/tr]
[tr][td]4[/td][td]1%[/td][td]n/a[/td][td]n/a[/td][/tr]
[tr][td]5[/td][td]1%[/td][td]1%[/td][td]n/a[/td][/tr]
[tr][td]6[/td][td]2%[/td][td]1%[/td][td]1%[/td][/tr]
[tr][td]7[/td][td]2%[/td][td]2%[/td][td]1%[/td][/tr]
[tr][td]8[/td][td]3%[/td][td]2%[/td][td]2%[/td][/tr]
[tr][td]9[/td][td]3%[/td][td]3%[/td][td]2%[/td][/tr]
[tr][td]10[/td][td]4%[/td][td]3%[/td][td]3%[/td][/tr]
[/table]

[h2]Motivation[/h2]
Inspired by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2577243435]Easy Engine Rebuild[/url] (B41 only), but fully developed from scratch as a new mod with a focus on a lore-friendly way to restore the engine.

Unlike Easy Engine Rebuild, this mod gives you the ability to restore the engine iteratively, similar to how vanilla engine repair works.

[h2]Compatibility[/h2]
[list]
[*]Supported builds: 42.17+ (tested on b42.20.4 SP & MP)
[*]Safe to add/remove mid-game
[*]Works with all vanilla vehicles
[*]Works with [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2757712197]Vehicle Repair Overhaul[/url], [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3387539308]AutoMechanics[/url] and other popular mechanics mods
[*]Works with [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=3414495781]KI5[/url], Autotsar vehicles, and should work with most other vehicle mods as well  
(please let me know in the comments if you find any unsupported modded vehicle)
[/list]

[h2]Feedback[/h2]
Found a bug or have suggestions? Leave a comment! I'd love to hear your thoughts and improve the mod further.

3583147716.description:
[img]https://imgur.com/BaUyxax.png[/img]
[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]
[img]https://imgur.com/RMruQmJ.png[/img]
[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]

[h1]Singleplayer + Multiplayer[/h1]

[b]Orderly Chaos now supports both Singleplayer and Multiplayer.[/b]

[quote]
[b]Important:[/b] I do [b]not recommend adding this mod to existing worlds / existing servers[/b].

For the best and safest experience, use it on a [b]fresh world[/b] or a [b]fresh server[/b].
Because this mod changes how loose floor items are handled, old saves may already contain legacy floor clutter states that were never created with Orderly Chaos in mind.
[/quote]

[b]TL;DR[/b]
[list]
[*] Dramatically reduces stutter when many items lie on the ground.
[*] Auto-converts loose floor loot into a single [i]Clutter Pile[/i] container once the threshold is reached.
[*] [b]Placed items are excluded[/b] (your decorations/base layout stay exactly as you arranged them).
[*] Empty piles remove themselves automatically.
[*] Includes a [b]Singleplayer version[/b] and a [b]Multiplayer version[/b].
[/list]

[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]

[h2]What it does[/h2]
When too many loose items sit on one tile, the game repeatedly evaluates interactions, rendering and floor-object handling for every single object.

Orderly Chaos replaces that costly situation with one tidy container: the [i]Clutter Pile[/i].

You still loot normally, but the engine only has to deal with one container instead of dozens of separate world items.

[b]Result:[/b]
[list]
[*] smoother approach to loot-heavy tiles
[*] fewer hitches around messy areas
[*] cleaner visuals
[*] less floor clutter chaos
[/list]

[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]
[img]https://imgur.com/RRwg92x.png[/img]
[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]

[h1]Included Versions[/h1]

[b]1) Singleplayer[/b]
[list]
[*] Mod ID: [b]twistorderlychaos[/b]
[*] Uses [b]Mod Options[/b]
[*] Settings can be changed live in-game
[/list]

[b]2) Multiplayer[/b]
[list]
[*] Mod ID: [b]twistorderlychaosmp[/b]
[*] Uses [b]Sandbox Settings[/b]
[*] Server-friendly setup so all players use the same rules
[/list]

[quote]
Use the Singleplayer version for solo play, or the Multiplayer version for hosted / dedicated multiplayer.
[/quote]

[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]

[h1]Settings[/h1]

[b]Nearby Pile Behavior[/b]
You can decide how new floor drops behave when a pile is already nearby:
[list]
[*] [i]Absorb into a nearby pile[/i]
[*] [i]Create a new pile instead[/i]
[/list]

[b]Pile Creation Threshold[/b]
Set the amount of loose floor items needed before a pile is created.

Default: [b]12[/b]

[quote]
[b]Note:[/b] If you are standing directly on a pile, drops are always absorbed into that pile.
[/quote]

[b]Singleplayer:[/b] configured through [b]Mod Options[/b]  
[b]Multiplayer:[/b] configured through [b]Sandbox Settings[/b]

[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]

[h2]Compatibility / Usage Notes[/h2]

[b]Recommended usage:[/b]
[list]
[*] Start a [b]new save[/b] or [b]new server[/b]
[*] Use the correct version for your mode
[*] Keep existing decorative placed items untouched thanks to exclusions
[/list]

[b]Not recommended:[/b]
[list]
[*] Adding the mod to long-running existing worlds
[/list]

[img]https://imgur.com/RQYClYI.png[/img]

[h2]FAQ[/h2]

[b]Does this delete my stuff?[/b]
No. Items are moved into a container you can open and loot like any other.

[b]Will it move my decorations?[/b]
No. Anything placed with the game’s [i]Place[/i] tool is excluded.

[b]Does it work in Multiplayer now?[/b]
Yes. Use the [b]Multiplayer version[/b] of the mod.

[b]Can I add it to an existing world?[/b]
You [b]can[/b], but it is [b]not recommended[/b]. A fresh world/server is strongly preferred.

[b]How do I configure it?[/b]
Singleplayer uses [b]Mod Options[/b]. Multiplayer uses [b]Sandbox Settings[/b].

3745718141.title: US Military Grenades [B42]
3745718141.description:
[h1]US Military Grenades [B42][/h1]

[b]Update 2.22[/b]
---
Fixed a bug where GrenadeBallistics.lua and MineExplosionFX.lua could fail to load their required files, which could break explosion/flare effects and mine detonation FX.
Added Korean, Turkish, and Ukrainian translations, and completed missing translation strings (mainly around the debug-spawn key) for all previously-supported languages.
---

[b]Update 2.1 - Craftable Grenades + Grenade Bouncing[/b]
---
You can now craft your own grenades from scratch! Forge a grenade shell, build the fuze assembly, weld yourself a striker lever, then assemble everything together with gunpowder into a working Mk2, M26 or M67 grenade.
Producing a grenade is not a trivial task, so the recipes require very high skills to produce and are additionally locked behind a new manual: "TM 9-1300-214: Military Explosives" - look for it where you would expect to find such a thing and maybe as contraband somewhere?

If you're playing with the "Delayed Fuse" sandbox option enabled: grenades that don't detonate on impact can now bounce once or twice before coming to rest and arming for real. The bounce depends on the actual calculated throw energy. Heavier throws bounce further, heavier grenades bounce less, and it roughly follows the direction you threw it in - with a little natural randomness so it doesn't look robotic.

Also lowered the minimum for the "Loot Multiplier" sandbox option from 0.1 to 0.01, for anyone who wants grenades to be even rarer than before.

Also fixed a crash that could happen when an explosion needed to shatter several nearby windows at once, and a visual bug where a bounced grenade would snap to the center of its tile instead of staying exactly where it landed.
---

[b]Update 2.0 - This was a big one and a LOT of work, but I think you will like it.[/b]
---
On squares that are visible to the player but invisible to the character the aim marker turns red. I don't hard-block the throw, you can still throw at a red marker if you really want to. Just know you're throwing blind at that point: you don't actually have eyes on what's there, so the grenade might not land where you expect - and if you're standing close to whatever's blocking your view, that could get dangerous real fast.

Added a sandbox option to disable instant-exploding grenades. You can decide if you want instant explosions or more realistic behaviour. Set the "Delayed Fuse" option to true, and decide how long the grenade sits armed after landing before it explodes.
Threw the grenade against a wall by accident? ... You now have some time to escape your doom :D
If a delayed-fuse grenade gets stuck against a wall above ground level, it now falls down to the real floor below.

Completely reworked how the game figures out where you're actually aiming. Changed fence/obstacle recognition from a blacklist to a sprite based getLastPicked. What this means: prior to today's change, the mod checked passability using a square collision check, then checked the tile, and if it was a fence, let the grenade pass if it had enough ballistic height. This turned out to be very unreliable - there are often small objects near fences, and other things I can't fully explain, that incorrectly triggered "obstacle" detection.

I've gone further and thrown that whole approach out. Targeting now uses the exact same depth-correct picking the game itself uses to highlight objects under your cursor. On top of that, the precise height on whatever you're aiming at is now taken into account too - aim partway up a wall and the grenade actually targets that exact spot.

With targeting this precise I added window demolishon - a grenade punches straight through glass without losing momentum, but shatters it on the way through.
Explosions now also shatter nearby windows in a radius around the blast (plus the floor above and below) - on buildings and on vehicles alike.

Also reworked throwing down from height - the drop trajectory now properly accounts for the extra range the fall itself gives you, so tossing a grenade off a rooftop actually reaches further than a flat throw would.

This is a much safer approach to a problem the game engine gives me no clean way to solve 100% - and at least now you can safely throw grenades over fences and even low buildings, and through windows!
The system is not perfect by any means. I am trying to calculate a 3D trajectory using 2D blocking sprites. This is a faulty system by default. Throwing straight up onto a higher floor especially can still land a bit off. But I will try to improve it as I go along.

And here I need your help!!!
Please test the grenades! Throw them into walls, buildings, doors, windows, up onto roofs, anything you like. If you think something should have stopped the grenade and it didn't (or the other way around), report it to me with as much detail as possible - a description of the obstacle and its location, if you can.
With your help, I'll keep tightening the ballistics and make them as realistic as possible.

I realize that in their current state (not craftable), grenades are a rare and valuable commodity. To help with testing, I've added a debug-spawn key that doesn't require switching to full debug mode: hold Shift + Numpad "+" (rebindable in Mod Options) to spawn a single flashbang directly into your inventory, whenever you want to do some trajectory testing.

3755993986.title: Gas Pump Indicator
3755993986.description:
[h1]Gas Pump Indicator[/h1]
A mod that colors the LED slit on gas pumps — the small lit indicator above each nozzle — to show fuel and power state at a glance.

In vanilla, the only way to check a pump's state is to right-click it (or read the small "OUT OF GAS" sign that appears next to some pumps at random). This mod paints the LED slit that already exists on every pump sprite, so the state is legible at a glance from anywhere on screen.

[b]Update (2026-08-07, v1.6):[/b] The remaining fuel readout has moved from Mod Options to the sandbox settings, so it can be managed server-side in multiplayer. If you had it enabled in v1.5, it will be off again by default. On a new world you can turn it on in the sandbox settings at world creation. On an existing world, add [b]-debug[/b] to the game's launch options, turn it on in the debug menu's sandbox options, then reload the world.

[hr]
[h2]LED States[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Green LED[/b] — Power on, fuel remaining
[*] [b]Red LED[/b] — Power on, tank empty
[*] [b]No LED[/b] — No power (grid or generator offline). In multiplayer there is one more case where the LED stays off; see the Multiplayer section.
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Glow at Night (new in v1.2)[/h2]
At night the LED glows in its green/red color, so the state stays readable in the dark. By day it keeps blending with the ambient light as before.

Vanilla 42.20 also added a lit-pump effect, but it only lights up at night while the power grid is still on, and only in white. This mod's LED also works on generator power, and at night it glows green/red in place of vanilla's white light.

[hr]
[h2]Remaining Fuel Readout[/h2]
Turn on "Show remaining fuel in the right-click menu" in the sandbox settings and the pump's right-click menu shows how much fuel is left. Off by default.

Sandbox settings are fixed once a world is created, so changing this on an existing world needs the [b]-debug[/b] launch option and a reload of the world.

A pump with no power shows no readout, since its fuel amount has not been determined yet.

[hr]
[h2]Vanilla-Authentic Visuals[/h2]
The LED slit shape (the small parallelogram slit above the nozzle) is taken directly from the original pump sprite, so the recolored LED lines up pixel-for-pixel with the vanilla art. A luminance blend fades the edges into the surrounding pump body, avoiding the "flat colored sticker" look.

Left and right nozzles on the same pump tile pair are evaluated independently. Both 2x and 1x sprite resolutions are supported.

[hr]
[h2]Supported Pump Sprites[/h2]
All 8 vanilla gas pump sprites are covered:
[list]
[*] Fossoil pumps (East/South facing × left/right tile)
[*] Gas2Go pumps (East/South facing × left/right tile)
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Compatibility[/h2]
[list]
[*] Supports: Build 42
[*] Works in singleplayer and multiplayer
[*] Standalone — works with vanilla, no additional mods required
[*] Safe to add to or remove from existing saves (no world state is modified)
[*] No script or recipe additions — rendering and UI only
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Multiplayer[/h2]
Tested on a Build 42 co-op host.
[list]
[*] The LED is rendered locally on each player's screen. The mod never modifies or transmits world state — no fuel rolls, no signs, no network packets.
[*] Like any mod, it must be added to the server's mod list to be active in multiplayer.
[*] MP-only detail: a powered pump can show no LED if the game has not yet determined its fuel amount (typically a pump running on a player-placed generator that nobody has used). This is intentional — on a client the mod only reads what the server has already determined. Use the pump once, or leave and revisit the area — either action triggers the server to determine the fuel amount, and the LED lights up from then on.
[/list]

[hr]
[h2]Notes[/h2]
After activating a generator that powers a pump, the LED may take a few seconds to appear. The mod itself polls frequently, but this delay comes from the vanilla grid-power propagation and is not something the mod can shorten.

[hr]
[h2]Technical Notes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Uses [i]IsoObject.setOverlaySprite(name, false)[/i] — the generic overlay slot rendered unconditionally by the engine, called in its non-transmitting form so the overlay stays client-side (multiplayer-safe)
[*] Pump discovery is coordinate-based (not IsoObject-reference-based), so chunk unload/reload cannot desync the overlay from the pump
[*] Combines [i]LoadGridsquare[/i] event registration with a 5-second box-scan safety net around the player, so no pump is missed even if the event fires before the mod is attached
[*] State re-evaluated at ~5 Hz per tracked pump; cost is negligible even in dense scenes
[*] Handles map spots where several pump objects overlap on one square, each with its own fuel reserve (these exist in the vanilla map, e.g. around Louisville)
[*] The night glow is a fullbright overlay sprite carrying the unlit flag; vanilla 42.20's white lit patch is disabled at the source by stripping the HasLightOnSprite property from the pump sprites (v1.4), with the old slot-plugging kept as a fallback
[/list]

3759277273.title: Survivor Quirks
3759277273.description:
[h1]Survivor Quirks[/h1]
Adds 37 new character traits (24 positive, 13 negative) to spice up character creation. Every trait blocks its logical opposite, so you can't pick both sides of the same coin. Built with multiplayer in mind from the start.

[h2]Positive Traits (24)[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Second Wind:[/b] Once per day, recovers a burst of endurance when completely exhausted.
[*] [b]Battle Trance:[/b] Killing a zombie up close steadies the nerves and restores endurance for a short while.
[*] [b]Sixth Sense:[/b] Feels a sudden chill when a zombie closes in from behind.
[*] [b]Night Stalker:[/b] Learns sneaking and light footwork faster while sneaking at night.
[*] [b]Rain Dancer:[/b] Never catches a cold from the rain and enjoys being out in it.
[*] [b]Grave Calm:[/b] Feels at ease around the dead. Less stress and sadness near corpses.
[*] [b]Contortionist:[/b] Slips through broken windows without getting cut.
[*] [b]Improviser:[/b] Keeps battered weapons barely working. They never break completely.
[*] [b]Die Hard:[/b] Bleeds half as long and shrugs off pain quickly.
[*] [b]Lone Wolf:[/b] Feels calmer and happier when nobody else is around.
[*] [b]Team Spirit:[/b] Feels better around other survivors and stays in shape with company.
[*] [b]Motivator:[/b] Lifts the mood of survivors nearby.
[*] [b]Field Medic:[/b] Tending other survivors' wounds relieves stress and teaches first aid faster.
[*] [b]Early Bird:[/b] Tires more slowly during the morning hours.
[*] [b]Nocturnal:[/b] Tires more slowly late at night.
[*] [b]Pack Mule:[/b] Can carry 20% more weight.
[*] [b]Caffeine Fiend:[/b] Coffee and tea work twice as well.
[*] [b]Keen Nose:[/b] Smells rotten food in the inventory before tasting it.
[*] [b]Slow Heart:[/b] Panic fades away noticeably faster.
[*] [b]Magpie:[/b] Sometimes spots small trinkets others would overlook when searching containers.
[*] [b]Cold Comfort:[/b] Standing close to another survivor in the cold shares warmth and eases the chill for both.
[*] [b]Sturdy Stitch:[/b] Stitched wounds leave noticeably less lasting pain than usual.
[*] [b]Herdsman:[/b] Animals kept and cared for breed more reliably under your watch.
[*] [b]Whistle While You Work:[/b] Sometimes whistles during repetitive work, lifting the mood but drawing attention.
[/list]

[h2]Negative Traits (13)[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Short Winded:[/b] Loses endurance faster during exertion.
[*] [b]Snorer:[/b] Snores loudly while sleeping. The dead may hear it.
[*] [b]Afraid of the Dark:[/b] Grows panicked in darkness without a light source.
[*] [b]Weather Sensitive:[/b] Rain brings gloom and headaches, storms even more so.
[*] [b]Squeamish:[/b] Feels sick around corpses.
[*] [b]Bleeder:[/b] Wounds bleed considerably longer.
[*] [b]Motion Sickness:[/b] Gets queasy as a passenger or at high speed.
[*] [b]Paranoid:[/b] Sometimes panics for no reason at all.
[*] [b]Sweet Tooth:[/b] Grows unhappy after a day without something sweet.
[*] [b]Bad Back:[/b] Can carry 15% less weight.
[*] [b]Weak Knees:[/b] Sometimes trips for no reason while sprinting, a brief loss of speed.
[*] [b]Jumpy Trigger:[/b] Aiming a firearm and getting startled can trigger an accidental shot.
[*] [b]Slow Sort:[/b] Moving items between containers takes noticeably longer than usual.
[/list]

[h2]Server Settings[/h2]
Every trait can be individually enabled or disabled, and its point cost can be adjusted, through the Sandbox settings under the "Survivor Quirks" page. Bleeder characters can optionally start with a few bandages, also configurable there.

3774789651.title: Long Term Preservation [42.20]
3774789651.description:
New ways to preserve and store food without a freezer. Salt cure meats, dry them, jar them, or make pemmican. Render lard from pork, mash berries into jam, and forage salt rocks to crush into salt. Beef, pork, venison and fish can be preserved.

This is an update of Skittles' Long Term Preservation for build 42.20. All credit for the mod goes to Skittles. The original is here: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3406392630]Long Term Preservation[/url]. Go rate it. If you are still on 42.13, use the original instead of this.

[b]To Skittles[/b]
If you want this taken down, message me and I will remove it right away. If you would rather update the original yourself, I will send you the full list of changes and the fixed files.

[b]Why it crashed on 42.19+[/b]
42.19 changed how recipe ingredient tags are looked up. One recipe asked for knives using the old style of tag name, which no longer exists in the new system. The game does not skip unknown tags anymore. It hits a null reference while building the world dictionary and the whole world load dies. That was the instant crash on loading a world.

[b]Changes in this update[/b]
- Fixed the world load crash by rewriting the knife tags to their registered names.
- Fixed jarring. The old canned food hooks were removed from the game, so sealing and opening jars now use the current built in handlers. Sealing stores your lid condition and opening gives the lid back, same as vanilla jarring.
- Fixed a script keyword typo that made the game skip part of the item file.
- Fixed translations not loading on Linux due to file name casing. Applies to all 12 languages.
- Updated the eating animation name to the current form.

[b]Notes[/b]
- Do not run this together with the original mod. The items would be defined twice.
- Preserved food from the original keeps working. Item ids are unchanged, so cured and jarred food in your save carries over. When you switch a save from the original to this version you get a one time missing mod warning. Accept and continue.
- Salt comes from foraged salt rocks. Crush them with a mortar and pestle.

3775310237.title: JB's Work Orders [B42] Task Automation
3775310237.description:
[h1]JB Work Orders[/h1]
[h3]Task Automation[/h3]
[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikej1977/jbWorkOrders/refs/heads/main/steam-images/anim-menu.gif[/img]

[hr][/hr]
Give your player some chores to complete while you run to the bathroom! Queue up automated gathering, clearing, processing and more. Now includes Auto-Resting!

This update for B42.20 has gotten rid of the right-click menu and radial menu and has been replaced with a resizable, movable window. The window can be opened from a right-click menu option, from a small button you can re-position or with an assignable hot-key. These options can be changed from the window itself(click on the gear icon) or from the mod options screen in the main menu.

Work Orders now includes "Bring Out Your Dead" to automatically move zombies to a selected area and a new "Farming" menu to automate repetitive farming tasks.

Added Endurance Reduction and Auto-Rest options. Reduce endurance used while performing work orders by 0 to 100%. Set your player to rest when your moodle level is between 1-4 (or keep at 0 to disable auto-rest). Endurance reduction is given as a "refund" to stamina, and is MP compatible. Be aware that syncing stamina between client and server may take a second or so.

[b]Your player cannot work in the dark. You can use a flashlight, car headlights, etc, to light the way and get your work done at night.[/b]

[hr][/hr]
[u][h2]Logging Menu[/h2][/u]
[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikej1977/jbWorkOrders/refs/heads/main/steam-images/logging-menu.jpg[/img]

[h3]Gathering - select a drop off location, then an area[/h3]
[list]
[*]Pickup all logs
[*]Gather all planks
[*]Collect all firewood
[*]Pickup all stones
[*]Gather all twigs and branches
[/list]
[h3]Clearing Options - select an area[/h3]
[list]
[*]Clear all trees in an area
[*]Dig all tree stumps in an area
[*]Cut down all bushes in an area
[*]Remove all grass and weeds from an area
[*]Break down and remove all boulders from an area
[/list]
[h3]Processing Options - select an area[/h3]
[list]
[*]Saw logs into planks
[*]Chop logs and large branches into firewood
[/list]
[h3]Includes new storage containers for your gathered items[/h3]
Each storage container can hold 100 lb/kg of the storage type, eg Logs, Planks, etc.

When gathering, you can select a container(including stacked crates), a trunk, truck bed or trailer, to drop your gathered items off. The containers will fill until they are full and then anything else will be dropped next to the full container. When selecting a vehicle trunk/truck bed, choose a tile that is directly underneath that area.

[hr][/hr]
[u][h2]Move Corpses Menu[/h2][/u]
[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikej1977/jbWorkOrders/refs/heads/main/steam-images/move-corpses-menu.jpg[/img]

[h3]Move corpses - select a drop-off location[/h3]
[list]
[*]Move outside corpses to the drop-off location
[*]Move all corpses inside to a drop-off location
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[u][h2]Farming Menu[/h2][/u]
[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikej1977/jbWorkOrders/refs/heads/main/steam-images/farming-menu.jpg[/img]

[h3]Prepare - select an area[/h3]
[list]
[*]Dig furrows with tool/hands in an area
[*]Remove plants from area
[/list]
[h3]Plant Seeds - select an area[/h3]
[*]Seeds packets need to be opened
[*]You will be given of list of seeds to plant
[/list]
[h3]Tend - select an area[/h3]
[list]
[*]Fertilize all crops in an area
[*]Water all plants in an area
[*]Water all plants in an area and auto refill container
[*]Treat Mildew (Not shown in image)
[*]Treat Flies (Not shown in image)
[*]Treat Slugs (Not shown in image)
[*]Treat Aphids (Not shown in image)
[/list]
[h3]Harvest - select an area[/h3]
[list]
[*]Harvest all ready crops in an area
[/list]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Mod Options[/h2]
[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikej1977/jbWorkOrders/refs/heads/main/steam-images/settings-menu.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*]Open Window From Right-Click Menu
[*]Keep Work Orders Right-Click Option At Top
[*]Show On-Screen Work Orders Button
[*]Stop Auto-Working When Zombies Are Near
[*]Repeat Area Selection Until Cancelled(Right-Click)
[*]Work Endurance Reduction Percent (0-100%)
[*]Rest at Endurance Moodle Level (0-4)
[*]Choose Color For Selection Outline
[*]Open Window Hotkey
[/list]
When using "Repeat Area Selection" you will need to right-click to cancel selected more area. This will drop you back to the menu where you left off.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Future Plans[/h2]
[list]
[*]Throwing corpses out the window (should be possible now)
[*]Clear trash from an area
[*]Demolish built structures in an area
[/list]

3775423228.title: Layered Placement [B42] - MP Compatible
3775423228.description:
Decorate with Pickup/Place Furniture without using Brush Tool but the way the admin brush allows.

Hang lights over tables and posters, and put lamps on railings and catwalks. Cabinets over fridges and much more. Put furniture under overhead strip lights, like the long fluorescent tubes the game normally will not let you build under. Outdoor and railing lights use battery when there is no building power, so they still turn on when placed.

Server owners choose allowed features in Sandbox Options. Players can turn allowed features off for themselves in Mod Options. Crates, tables and other floor furniture still stack by the normal rules, and skills and tools still matter.

B42.20+. Safe mid-save. Multiplayer supported, so enable it on the server and all clients. Hosting co-op counts as a server, so enable it in the co-op server's mod list too, or stacking on occupied tiles will do nothing.

COMPANION MOD (optional, not required)

Brush Tool Save Fix: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3775272983
A separate B42 multiplayer bug where admin Brush Tool tile edits are cosmetic only and revert once the chunk unloads. Layered Placement does not use the Brush Tool and works fine without it, but tiles vanishing looks the same from the outside and the two get confused. If you run a server, use the Brush Tool, and see edits reverting after a relog or restart, that is the one you want.

My mods are literally fueled by my caffeine addiction.
If I helped you, buying me a coffee would be AMAZING. Thanks guys. https://buymeacoffee.com/stormster10

Do not reupload. Subscribe on Workshop for updates.

3776182375.title: CH Status HUD
3776182375.description:
See how your survivor is doing at a glance, without opening any menu.

[b]Press ;[/b] (semicolon) to show or hide the panel - that's it, nothing else to set up. Enable the mod, load in, it's already there.

[b]Already had the mod installed?[/b] Yours is still on [b]U[/b]. The game keeps a key binding once it has one, so only new installs pick up the new default. Change either of them under Options - Key Bindings - "Toggle Status HUD".

[b]Quick start:[/b] [b];[/b] toggles the panel (or [b]U[/b] if you had the mod before) - [b]right-click it[/b] for Settings - [b]drag[/b] it anywhere and lock the position once you like where it sits.

[b]Seeing everything twice?[/b] Settings, Layout, "Hide vanilla moodles" switches the game's own icons off - this panel already covers them.

[b]Adding it to a save you already started?[/b] Build 42 gives every save its own mod list, so ticking the mod in the main menu does [b]not[/b] switch it on in an existing world - on the Load Game screen, pick your save and use [b]"Choose Mods..."[/b] to tick it there as well. Otherwise nothing appears and the key does nothing, which looks exactly like a broken mod. It is the most common reason it "doesn't work".

[h1]What it shows[/h1]
32 stats in 4 groups. Turn any of them on or off.
[list]
[*][b]Survival[/b] - Health, Food, Water, Rest, Endurance, Fitness
[*][b]Mental[/b] - Stress, Panic, Pain, Unhappy, Boredom, Anger, Morale, Nicotine Withdrawal, Idleness, Sanity
[*][b]Body[/b] - Body Temperature, Body Heat Generation, Wetness, Discomfort, Sickness, Infection, Fever, Drunk, Food Sickness, Poison
[*][b]Nutrition[/b] - Carry Weight, Body Weight, Calories, Proteins, Carbs, Fat
[/list]
Each row: icon, a bar that turns yellow then red as it gets worse, and the exact number. Hover a row for the full name.

[h1]Make it yours[/h1]
Right-click the panel - Settings, in four tabs. Everything updates live, so you see the change before you close the window.
[list]
[*][b]Hover anything in Settings[/b] for a one-line explanation of what it does - every stat and every option
[*]Vertical list, or a horizontal strip along the top/bottom edge
[*]Text sizes read from your machine's own fonts, marked [b]*[/b] where they are drawn perfectly sharp; 16 width steps; background down to fully invisible
[*]Choose where the stat name goes: off, auto (trimmed so the bar keeps a usable width), full, or drawn inside the bar
[*]Put the number beside the bar, or inside it so the bar runs the full row
[*]Group stats by category or order them freely; headings on or off, with a gap or a divider line between categories. Folding a category by clicking its heading can be switched off if you keep catching it while dragging.
[*]Turn bars and icons on or off, grayscale mode if you don't want colour
[*][b]Only show problems[/b] - hides every stat that's currently fine
[*]Hide the vanilla moodle icons too, since this panel already covers them
[*]Resize from any edge or corner, drag anywhere, lock the position once you're happy
[*]Optional second keybind to open Settings directly, no right-click needed (Options - Key Bindings - "Open Status HUD Settings")
[*]Reorder stats with the up/down arrows in the Stats tab. Grouped keeps a stat inside its own category; Free order lets it go anywhere. An "Order" button per group undoes just that group's reordering, and Reset to defaults restores your stat selection as well as the appearance.
[/list]

[h1]Extra[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Threshold ticks[/b] - marks on the bar showing exactly where the next moodle level kicks in
[*][b]Diagnose stats[/b] (right-click) - compares the game's raw value with what the HUD shows, for when a stat looks wrong. Off by default; a server can enable it.
[*]Knows what your server disabled - hides those stats instead of showing them stuck and broken
[/list]

[h1]Server admins[/h1]
A sandbox page under [b]CH Status HUD[/b] lets you lock which stats players can see, and switch off threshold ticks or the diagnose tool for everyone. Add the mod to the server's mod list too, not just your own subscription - the page only appears if the server itself loads it.

[h1]Installation[/h1]
Client-side only - no server-side Lua, no network traffic, nothing written into the save. That also means every player who wants to see the HUD needs it installed and enabled on their own machine - the host or a server doesn't hand it to anyone automatically.

[b]Singleplayer:[/b] enable it in the Mods menu, then load in - it appears on its own. On a save you already started you must also enable it inside that save's own mod list (see Quick start), since Build 42 keeps one per world. Otherwise it works fine on an existing save; you only need a fresh one for the server admin sandbox page (see above), which is fixed at world creation.

[b]Hosting (the in-game Host button):[/b] check both the regular mod list AND the separate Steam Workshop items list in the host setup screen. This mod has to be enabled in both, or it won't load at all - no panel, no keybind, nothing, and it can look like the mod is just broken.

[b]Dedicated server:[/b] add it to the server's own mod list, not just your own subscription - both [b]Mods=[/b] and [b]WorkshopItems=[/b] in the server's .ini need this mod (id [b]CHStatusHUD[/b], Workshop ID [b]3776182375[/b]). Every player connecting still needs it installed on their own end too, same as hosting.

[h1]Languages[/h1]
Fully translated into every language the game ships (28), including the new hover explanations. AI-assisted - if something reads wrong in your language, comment what it should say instead and I'll fix it.

[h1]Update - 23 August[/h1]
[b]If something goes wrong, the mod now says so itself.[/b] A window appears after the world loads, with a [b]Copy[/b] button - paste that in a comment and it tells me the game build, your screen, single or multiplayer, and what actually failed. Right-click the panel for [b]"Copy diagnostics"[/b] any time, even when nothing is broken.
[b]New:[/b] update rate is a setting now - Layout, Panel. Instant is still the default; 1s, 5s and 10s are there for anyone who would rather not re-read a hunger bar eight times a second.

[i]Also in this release, from the last few days: warning sliders show the real value instead of a percentage, so Proteins reads "below -300" rather than "below 13%", with - and + buttons either side to move one point at a time. The Settings window reopens where you left it. Nutrition warnings started working at all (Carbs and Fat could never count as a problem), the panel stopped moving after a relog, the toggle key gained a cycle mode, and the default key changed from U to ; because U is vanilla's Vehicle Info key. Existing players keep the key they have.[/i]

[h1]Not working?[/h1]
The mod writes one line to console.txt when it starts, beginning with [b][CH Status HUD] panel created[/b]. Paste that line in the comments and I can tell you exactly what happened. If instead you find [b]PANEL CREATION FAILED[/b], paste that one - it names the cause.
Also check console.txt for mods you thought you had disabled - a save keeps loading whatever it was created with, and one running unnoticed has been the answer before.
